## O75: what the act flag changes, counted with the output visible — 2026-09-14

O75 recorded that `vite.config.ts` loads `browser-setup.ts`, which sets
`IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT`, for the `browser` project alone, and quoted that
file's doc for the cost: without the flag "`act` does not actually flush
effects synchronously". It left open how many `jsdom` tests turning the flag on
would surface. Both were measured, and the quoted cost is not what the flag
does.

### What the flag does, on React 19.2.8

A throwaway `jsdom` test, deleted afterwards, mounted a component whose
`useEffect` sets state, through `createRoot` inside `act`, then made a second
update outside `act` — once with the flag deleted and once with it `true`,
recording `console.error` through a spy. The text is `effect:outside`.

| flag | text when `act` returned | errors inside `act` | text straight after the outside update | a macrotask later | messages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unset | `1:0` | 2 | `1:0` | `1:1` | "not configured to support act(...)" ×3, the third from the unmount |
| `true` | `1:0` | 0 | `1:0` | `1:1` | "An update to %s inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)" ×1 |

`1:0` is the effect's update committed: `act` flushed it either way. The source
agrees. In `react-dom-client.development.js` the flag is read in one function,
`isConcurrentActEnvironment`, which prints the "not configured" message itself
and whose two callers print "not wrapped in act" and "a suspended resource
finished loading … not wrapped in act"; `scheduleCallback$1` pushes work onto
the act queue whenever one exists, without reading the flag; and
`react.development.js`, where `act` lives, never names it. The profiling build
has the same function and the same two callers. The flag and the claim entered
together in `f81913d` (2026-08-09), with `react` already at `^19.2.8`, and this
file's record of that ("`act` was not flushing effects") was read off the
warning.

So what the `jsdom` project was missing was not the flush but the report: with
the flag unset, React says nothing about an update made outside `act`, which is
the case O75 was about.

### The first count could not see the output

Every run in this section passed every test; the question was only what React
printed. The first full `jsdom` run printed no `stderr |` block at all, though
every `mount()` renders inside `act` and the probe shows each such render
logging with the flag unset. A control test that calls
`console.error('O75-CONTROL-ERROR')` and passes printed nothing either, and a
full run with `--silent=false` printed none of the thousands of "not
configured" messages the `default` reporter showed for the same tests. Vitest 4.1 resolves its reporter as
`isAgent ? "agent" : "default"` when none is given (`coverage.DM_a_rWm.js`), and
the same control printed its line with `CLAUDECODE` and `AI_AGENT` unset and
printed nothing with them set. So a run under Claude Code shows no console
output from a passing test, whatever React logs. Every count below is from
`--reporter=default`, with the control in the run and its line checked present,
and the control deleted afterwards.

### Counted over the whole `jsdom` project

| state | passed | "not configured to support act" | "not wrapped in act(...)", control's excluded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main`: flag unset | 951 | 6,819, the control's own among them | 0 |
| flag set, tests unchanged | 951 | 0 | 20, in 7 tests |
| flag set, the 7 settled | 951 | 0 | 0 |

The twenty were 9 updates to `Library` and 6 to `Shell` in three
`Routes.test.tsx` tests — "does not mount the reader anywhere else", "answers
an unknown path with the library rather than the reader" and "sends a reader
route with no :work back to the library rather than crashing" — and 5 to
`PageView` in four `App.test.tsx` tests: "= and - and 0 move the drawn rect,
and 0 puts it back", "a shift-press pans, and a zero box moves nothing", "is
claimed and prevented while there is a page to zoom" and "waits for the
incoming page to decode, then applies the carried swap".

### None of the seven was passing on timing

In each, the update landed after the last assertion. The three route tests are
synchronous: they assert straight after `mount()` and return, and the mocked
fetches answer afterwards. The four reader tests change the zoom — with keys,
with a zoom key before a pan, with a wheel, and with a carried swap applied on
`load` — inside `act`, assert on `drawnRect`, which that dispatch committed,
and return without settling. `PageView`'s only state is `shown`, set when the
decode of a new `src` settles, so an update to it there is the page arriving at
a new `?w=`; logged either side of each trailing settle, the page's `src` went
from `?w=1024` to `?w=1536` in the first three and from `?w=1536` to `?w=1024`
in the carried swap. None of the seven awaits anything outside `act`, so no
un-acted update could have landed before one of its assertions.

"= and - and 0" ends back at fit-whole — `0` puts the rect back — and the page
it shows after the settle is the `?w=1536` one. Whether that is the width it
asks for there was not looked into. *(Looked into under O113, below: it is not.
Fit-whole asks for `?w=1024` there, and the `?w=1536` page was a superseded
decode drawn after `0`.)*

Each now ends in an `act`-scoped settle — `flush()` from
`tests/support/async.ts` in the route tests, the file's own `settle()` in the
reader tests — with nothing asserted after it, so no verdict can move; the
table's last row is its effect.
*(O113 has since given one of the seven, "= and - and 0", an assertion after
its settle: see below.)*

Each settle was then removed on its own, with the control in the run and the
file compared with its original after each. Its own test warned again — 5 in
each route test (3 `Library`, 2 `Shell`), 2 in "= and - and 0" and 1 in each
other reader test — and no other test did. With all seven in place, the two
files warned nothing but the control.

### Not done

- **Nothing fails on either warning.** Making React's act warnings fail the
  test was put to the user with this item and declined: the flag and the seven
  settles only. A new test that updates state outside `act` prints the warning
  under the `default` reporter and passes, and under the `agent` reporter it
  prints nothing.
- `browser-setup.ts` keeps its name, though the `jsdom` project loads it too.
- The `browser` project was not counted for warnings. `browser-setup.ts`
  changed there only in its doc, and its 28 tests passed in the gate.

## O47: `scan --add` takes the checked add — 2026-09-14

O47 recorded that `scan::add_root` accepts a root nested inside, or containing,
one already held, that the next scan admits the same directory twice as two
members of one work — measured on 2026-08-18 — and that nothing refuses it.
Since C4 PR 1 (#105, 2026-09-03) something has: `POST /api/library/roots` calls
`scan::add_root_checked`, which refuses an overlap in either direction. What
was left was `taiyaku library scan --add`, the one caller of `add_root` outside
a test; the rest are fixtures, and `taiyaku-library`'s `corpus.rs` and
`taiyaku-serve`'s `test_support.rs` are both `#[cfg(test)]`.

### Before and after, on a scratch tree

A tree `lib/Series/Series - v01/` holding three files, `000.jpg` to `002.jpg`,
and a fresh `--db` beside it, both under the session scratchpad, and a new tree
for every run. Two `taiyaku library scan --add` commands, in each order, run
with `target/release/taiyaku` built from `main` (no crate change on `main`
since that build) and with `target/debug/taiyaku` built from this branch; the
database was read back with Python's `sqlite3`.

| binary | order | second `--add` exits | it printed | roots | members of the one edition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | `lib`, then `lib/Series` | 0 | `1 rekeyed, 1 merged` | 2 | 2 — ordinals 0 and 1, one path, one `sha256`, 3 pages each, `root_id` 2 and 1 |
| `main` | `lib/Series`, then `lib` | 0 | `1 rekeyed, 1 merged` | 2 | 2 — the same, `root_id` 1 and 2 |
| branch | `lib`, then `lib/Series` | 1 | "`…/lib/Series` is inside existing root `…/lib` (id 1)" | 1 | 1 |
| branch | `lib/Series`, then `lib` | 1 | "`…/lib` contains existing root `…/lib/Series` (id 1)" | 1 | 1 |

The `main` rows are the shape the 2026-08-18 measurement recorded, in both
directions: the same directory twice, one member under each root. On the
branch the one root left carries `scan_interval_secs` 86400 in both orders; on
`main`, in the first order, both roots' were NULL. That is not O47: it is
`add_root_checked` recording the watch probe's interval when a root is added,
which `--add` now gets along with the refusal.

Re-adding a root already held exits 1 on both binaries and leaves one root; the
message changes. `main` says `UNIQUE constraint failed: root.path`; the branch
says "`…/lib` is inside existing root `…/lib` (id 1)", the exact-duplicate case
`add_root_checked`'s doc names.

**The first branch run of the second order was of the wrong binary.** It
printed the refusal and still left a second root, `lib`, with
`scan_interval_secs` and `last_scan_status` both NULL: an unchecked insert
followed by the refusal, which is exactly the last row of the table below.
`taiyaku-cli`'s `tests/cli.rs` runs `CARGO_BIN_EXE_taiyaku`, so a mutation's
`cargo nextest` run builds `target/debug/taiyaku` from the source as it
stands; the source was restored after that mutation and the binary was not.
The branch rows above are from a rebuild, `cargo build -p taiyaku-cli --bin
taiyaku`, made after checking that the source held the `add_root_checked` call
and no `add_root` call.

### The tests, watched

Two tests in `taiyaku-cli`'s `library/tests.rs` add a root through `scan
--add`, then a second root inside it or containing it, and assert the
refusal's message and that the library still holds one root and one member.
Each mutation was one substitution in `library.rs`'s `scan`; the file was
restored and compared with its original after each run.

| `--add` calls | inside | containing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_root_checked` (the fix) | passed | passed |
| `add_root` (the defect) | red: `a root inside a known root must be refused: ()` | red: `a root containing a known root must be refused: ()` |
| `add_root_checked`, its error replaced by `adding root {path} failed` | red at the message assertion | red at the message assertion |
| `add_root`, then `add_root_checked` | red at the *first* `--add` | red at the *first* `--add` |
| `add_root` only once a root exists, then `add_root_checked` | red: `left: (2, 1)`, `right: (1, 1)` | red: `left: (2, 1)`, `right: (1, 1)` |

The fourth row proves nothing and is kept for that reason. Inserting before the
check made the first `--add` refuse its own path, so both tests went red in
their setup and never reached the count the mutation was meant to exercise. The
fifth row reaches it.

All twenty `library::tests::scan*` tests pass on the branch.

### Not changed

- `add_root` still validates nothing, as its own doc and `add_root_checked`'s
  say it should not; fixtures are its callers now.
- **A refused `--add` still creates the database.** `scan` opens the library
  before it adds anything, so `--add` of a path that does not exist, with a
  `--db` that did not exist, exited 1 and left `new.db` behind. The refusal
  comes before a root is written, not before anything is.
- **A root added by `--add` is probed twice when the same run walks it**: once
  inside `add_root_checked`, and again by `scan`'s own loop, which probes every
  root it walks. It walks every root unless `--root` names a different one:
  `--add b --root a` walked only `a`, and left `b` with its interval recorded
  and no `last_scan_status`. On a filesystem that delivers no event the probe waits out its
  two-second timeout, so that is up to two more seconds, once per `--add`. Not
  measured.
- `add_root_checked`'s doc named `import` as a caller of `add_root`. It never
  was: `git log -S'add_root('` over the CLI's `library.rs` and `main.rs` finds
  one commit, `cec59e2`, which added `scan`'s call, and over
  `taiyaku-library`'s `import` module finds none. Corrected.

## O79: a progress document commits once — 2026-09-14

O79 recorded that `migrate::apply_progress` writes each position of a
`taiyaku.progress.json` with no transaction around the loop, so a failure
partway leaves the positions before it written; `migrate_progress` returns
`Malformed` and records no marker, and the next import's `holds_state` finds
the partial rows and answers `Kept`, so the rest of the document is never read
again. It named two failures that get there: "one malformed position later in
the document, or a database error".

### Half the premise was wrong

`progressdoc::from_json` deserialises the whole text — as a `ProgressDoc`, and
failing that as the bare legacy `Progress` — and returns before
`apply_progress`'s loop begins, so a malformed position anywhere in a document
fails with nothing written. The function is the same in `91b08d8`, the commit
that filed O79, as on `main`; in that commit the loop already called
`state::put_progress_at`, not the `state::put_progress` the row names.
`a_progress_json_that_does_not_parse_is_reported_and_skipped` already asserted
that an unreadable file writes nothing. What reaches the loop is a statement
SQLite refuses after an earlier position has been written.

### Nothing in the schema refuses a later position

`progress` was last created by `schema/009_progress_per_edition.sql`, and no
later migration names it. It has no `CHECK`. Every value `put_progress_at`
binds is non-null — two ids, a `String`, a `u32` and `coalesce(?5,
datetime('now'))`; both foreign keys name the one work and the one reader that
every position in a document shares; and the insert upserts on `(user_id,
work_id, edition)`, so a repeated edition updates its row rather than
conflicting. So the test creates a trigger — `BEFORE INSERT ON progress WHEN
NEW.edition = 'full-color'`, raising `ABORT` — over a versioned document
holding `raw-mono`, `full-color` and `en-fan`, in that order.

### Before and after

On `main`'s `migrate.rs`, with the test added, the first import returned
`Malformed` naming the refusal, and `state::progress` read back `[Position {
edition: "raw-mono", slot: 7, updated: "2026-08-27 09:00:00" }]` — the test
failed there. With that one assertion removed, the next one passed, finding no
`migrated_document` row, and the second import, trigger dropped, returned
`AlreadyPresent` where the test expects `Applied`. Each link of the chain O79
describes was observed.

With one `unchecked_transaction` around the loop, committed after it, all 19
`migrate::tests` pass: the first import returns `Malformed` naming the
refusal, no row and no marker remain, and the second returns `Applied` with
all three positions.

### The test, watched

Each change was applied by a script that checked its text replaced exactly one
occurrence, ran `migrate::tests`, restored the file and compared it with a
saved copy. The same script over the untouched fix passed all 19.

| change | the test fails at | with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no transaction — `main`'s loop | no rows | `left: [Position { edition: "raw-mono", slot: 7, … }]` |
| a transaction committed before the loop | no rows | the same |
| a transaction per position | no rows | the same |
| the transaction committed when a position fails, then the error returned | no rows | the same |
| no commit after the loop | every position, after the retry | `left: {}`; `a_progress_json_beside_the_sidecar_migrates_the_reading_position` and `a_versioned_progress_json_migrates_every_position` fail too |
| a failing position's error discarded, the rest committed | the first outcome | `expected Malformed, got Some(Applied)` |
| the fix, with `migrate_progress`'s `Err` arm recording the document settled | no marker | `left: Some(false)`, `right: None` |
| `main`'s loop, with the no-rows assertion removed | the retry's outcome | `left: Some(AlreadyPresent)`, `right: Some(Applied)` |
| the fix, with `updated` removed from the fixture's third position | the message | a parse error, not the trigger |

The first four stop at the same assertion, and each of the other five fails
at a different one, so every assertion in the test has been seen to fail.
The last is a change to the test rather than the code: a document that fails
to parse writes nothing either, and the message assertion is what says the
trigger was the failure.

### No caller holds a transaction open

A bare `BEGIN`, which `unchecked_transaction` sends, is refused while a
transaction is already open — `crate::Nested`'s doc in `lib.rs` records it.
`migrate::work` is called by `taiyaku-cli`'s `library::import_canonical`,
which `library import` and `serve`'s `serve_work` call, and by
`export/tests.rs`. `import_canonical` holds `library.conn()` and calls
`import::reimport` first; the `Nested` scope `import_with` opens is a local of
that function, so it has ended before `reimport` returns. `taiyaku-serve`
depends on `taiyaku-library` and not on `taiyaku-cli`, and nothing in it calls
into `migrate`. And the next thing `migrate::work` does is `migrate_notes`,
whose apply reaches `state::put_notes`, which opens `unchecked_transaction` on
the same connection.

Three `taiyaku-cli` tests import a `taiyaku.progress.json` through
`import_canonical` and assert `progress=migrated` —
`importing_a_work_with_all_four_siblings_present_migrates_every_one`,
`a_malformed_sibling_is_reported_and_skipped_and_the_sidecar_still_imports` and
`a_work_whose_siblings_all_read_cleanly_produces_no_warning_at_all` — and all
three passed with the fix, in the gate's run of 2129.

### `record_settled`, measured and left

`migrate_progress` writes the marker with `record_settled` once
`apply_progress` has returned, so outside its transaction. A throwaway test,
deleted afterwards, put a one-position document beside a work and a trigger
refusing an insert into `migrated_document` for `progress` with `absorbed = 1`;
a second, without the trigger, was the control.

| | first import | then | second import, trigger dropped | in-place `export::work` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | `Err`: "recording `progress` as migrated for work 1: refusing the progress marker" | the position written, no marker | `AlreadyPresent`, marker `absorbed` false | `taiyaku.progress.json` in `kept`, its bytes unchanged |
| control | `Applied` | marker `absorbed` true | — | `taiyaku.progress.json` written, its bytes changed |

The rows are whole, so no reading is lost, and it is not O79. What it costs is
the file: `absorbed` false is also what a sibling left unread because the rows
already held state carries, and an in-place export leaves such a file where it
is and reports it in `Exported::kept` until the reader moves it aside
(`export.rs`, "What an export will not touch"). The same order — apply, then
marker — is on all four documents' `Ok` arms, and each apply commits a
transaction of its own before the marker is written: `apply_progress` now,
`state::put_notes` and `state::put_truth` with `unchecked_transaction`,
`librarydoc::apply` with a `Nested` scope. A transaction opened around apply and
marker would be refused by each of the three that open theirs with
`unchecked_transaction`, so it would change `state::put_notes` and
`state::put_truth` as well as `apply_progress`; it is left as found.

### Not changed

- The order above, on all four documents.
- A versioned document with a position missing `updated` is reported with the
  legacy form's error: `from_json` falls back to reading a bare `Progress` and
  returns that message, so the last row of the table above read "missing field
  `edition` at line 4 column 44" for a document whose positions all carried an
  `edition`.

## O113: a return to the drawn page drops the decode it superseded — 2026-09-14

Opened and closed on one branch. O75's section above, under "None of the seven
was passing on timing", recorded that `App.test.tsx`'s "= and - and 0 move the
drawn rect, and 0 puts it back" ends showing the `?w=1536` page after its
trailing settle, and left open whether that is the width it asks for there. It
is not, and the same cause reaches a page turn.

### In jsdom, logged

Logging was added for one run and removed afterwards: in `App.tsx`,
`pageLongEdge`'s inputs and `borrowedLongEdge` at every render; in
`PageView.tsx`, each run of its effect and each present; in `decode.ts`, each
job's skip decision and each settled decode; and in the test, the drawn rect
and every page image's `src` after each key. It ran under `--reporter=default`
with a control `console.error` in the same test, whose line printed. jsdom's
window is 1024×768 at a `devicePixelRatio` of 1, and its `Image` has no
`decode` method, so `decodeTo` settles on the `TypeError` it swallows. The
reader opened in `single` mode, so the box's long edge was 1024 at every step.

| step | `view.w` | magnification | `pageLongEdge` | `PageView`'s effect | page `src` after the step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | 1 | 1 | 1024 | `src === shown`, returned | `?w=1024` |
| `=` | 0.8696 | 1.15 | 1536 | attempt 1, decode started | `?w=1024` |
| `-` | 1 | 1 | 1024 | `src === shown`, returned | `?w=1024` |
| `=` | 0.8696 | 1.15 | 1536 | attempt 2, decode started | `?w=1024` |
| `=` | 0.7561 | 1.3225 | 1536 | `src` unchanged, so the effect did not run | `?w=1024` |
| `0` | 1 | 1 | 1024 | `src === shown`, returned | `?w=1024` |
| settle | | | | attempts 1 and 2 presented, both drawn | `?w=1536` |
| a second settle | | | | | `?w=1536` |

`borrowedLongEdge` read 1024 at every render. A second logged test settled
between one `=` and `0`, and ended on `?w=1024`: `0` found `shown` at
`?w=1536`, took attempt 2 and decoded. So fit-whole asks for `?w=1024` in
jsdom, and the `?w=1536` page was a superseded request drawn after the reader
had gone back.

### The cause

`presentWhenDecoded` presents a decode whether or not it has been superseded.
Its doc makes ordering `present`'s job: `PageView` "hands in a callback that
ignores anything older than what it is already drawing, so a frame the reader
has moved past can be shown *on the way* and can never paint over a newer one."
That callback is `ordering.ts`'s `inOrder`, which drops an attempt only if it is
older than the one last drawn. `PageView`'s effect took an attempt number only
on the path that starts a decode. When `src` came back to `shown`, and on the
unbuffered path, it returned without one, so there was nothing newer to drop the
decode still in flight, and it was drawn when it settled.

The `src === shown` return is already in `PageView.tsx` at #10 (`5172922`).
There, and at `f81913d^`, `presentWhenDecoded` called `present` only
`if (!stale())`, and `stale` is true once `latestRef` has moved off the request,
so a return was safe. #35 (`f81913d`) removed that gate so a flick shows
intermediate pages, and added the ordering: `git log -S` on `main` finds "does
not gate this" in `decode.ts` and `inOrder` in `PageView.tsx` first in
`f81913d`.

### In a browser, before and after

**Substrate.** The development workstation, not the production host.
`taiyaku serve` ran from `target/release/taiyaku`, built 2026-09-14 at 00:24;
the only commit to touch `crates/` since is #136, `library scan --add`. It
served a scratch copy of `gotoubun-v01`'s sidecar with every member path made
absolute, a scratch database and a scratch `--cache`. A forwarding proxy
between vite's `/api` proxy and the server held any request whose URL matched a
pattern, for a set time, before forwarding it, and logged when it held, sent
and got each answer back. The browser, driven by Playwright, reported
`Chrome/153.0.0.0` on Linux. Before the fix the reader was `vite` in
development at `19a6988`. After it, the reader was two production bundles,
built with `vite build` from `19a6988` and from this branch and served by
`vite preview` through the same proxy, with the server restarted on a new
`--cache`.

Every drive set a new `en-mono` slot as the position, cleared the browser's
cache over CDP, and opened the reader in `single` mode at 1000×700 and a
`devicePixelRatio` of 1. It waited for the page to load and 1.5 s more,
dispatched keydowns on `window`, and read each page image's `src`,
`currentSrc`, `naturalWidth` and `naturalHeight` and the drawn rect from the
DOM, with a `MutationObserver` recording every change to a page image's `src`.
At that size fit-whole asks for `?w=1024`, from a long edge of 1000, and one
`=` asks for `?w=1536`, from 1150. At Playwright's default width of 1280,
fit-whole would ask for `?w=1536` already. In `pages/N`, `N` is the page's
zero-based index, and the image's `alt` counts from one.

The proxy's log shows a hold doing what it says. In the first held drive,
`pages/47?w=1536` was held at 02:46:32.285Z, sent at 02:46:35.285Z and answered
at 02:46:35.445Z.

| drive | before the fix, drawn at the end | after the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `=`, then `0` 2.5 s later; nothing held | `?w=1024`, 719×1024, at fit-whole | not rerun |
| `=`, then `0` 5 ms later; nothing held | `?w=1536`, 1079×1536, at fit-whole: drawn 163 ms after `=`, still there at 4.5 s | 3 ms apart: `?w=1024`, 719×1024, at 4.5 s; `?w=1536` fetched by 146 ms and never drawn |
| `=`, then `0` 57 ms later; nothing held | `?w=1536`, 1079×1536, at fit-whole, at 4.6 s | not rerun |
| `=`, then `0` 4.5 s later; `?w=1536` held 3 s | `?w=1536` drawn at 3,174 ms while zoomed, then `?w=1024` on `0` | not rerun |
| `=`, then `0` 307 ms later; `?w=1536` held 3 s | `?w=1536`, 1079×1536, at fit-whole, at 6.8 s | 304 ms apart: `?w=1024`, 719×1024, at 6.8 s |
| a turn, and a turn back 155 ms later; `pages/70` and `pages/72` held 4 s | `pages/72` drawn with `alt` "page 72", which is `pages/71`'s, at 7.2 s | 154 ms apart: `pages/71`, `alt` "page 72", at 7.2 s |
| `=` four times to 1.749×, then `-` and `=` 157 ms apart; `?w=1536` held 20 s | `?w=1536`, 1079×1536, at 1.749×, at 26.3 s | 155 ms apart: `?w=2048`, 1439×2048, at 26.3 s |

`gotoubun-v01` reads right to left, so the turn's `ArrowLeft` stepped forward,
to `pages/72`, and `ArrowRight` stepped back. The reader's saved position after
the turn was the slot it opened on, both times. At 1.749× the reader asks for
`?w=2048`, and before the fix the page drawn there was the 1536 one.

### A flick, before and after

Twelve `ArrowLeft` presses 25 ms apart at fit-whole with nothing held, once per
bundle, over pages the restarted server had not resized before that run. Before
the fix, from
`pages/95`, the image's `src` changed eight times, to `pages/96`, 97, 98, 99,
101, 102, 106 and 107, ending on `pages/107` at 533 ms with seven intermediate
pages drawn. After it, from `pages/124`, nine times, to 125, 126, 127, 128, 129,
131, 134, 135 and 136, ending on `pages/136` at 609 ms with eight. A flick in
one direction never returns to the drawn page, and after the fix it still draws
pages on the way. The two runs used different pages of the edition.

### The fix

`PageView`'s effect now takes an attempt number for every `src` before
anything else. In the two cases that start no decode, a return to `shown` and
the unbuffered path, it draws `src` through `inOrder` under that number at
once. A decode issued before the return has a lower number, so `inOrder` drops
it when it settles. The return still joins no cohort, and a number only orders
what one cell draws. The unbuffered path called `setShown(src)` directly; it
now calls it through `inOrder`, which is what drops a buffered decode that
settles while unbuffered.

`PageView`'s own doc comment said `presentWhenDecoded`'s `stale()` check
decides which attempt may touch the image, which has not been so since #35:
`f81913d^` presents only `if (!stale())`, and `f81913d` presents every decode
that settles. It now names `ordering.ts` and `inOrder` instead.

`PageView.tsx` stays at 100% on all four coverage measures. The web aggregate
reads 97.72% statements, 94.05% branches, 99.16% functions and 99.31% lines
with `main`'s three files and with this branch's, and `coverage-floor.mjs`
found every file above its floor both times.

### The tests, watched red

| | test | failing assertion, against the defect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | `PageView.test.tsx`, "drops a decode that settles after src came back to the page already drawn" | line 186: `b.png` where `a.png` was expected |
| T2 | `PageView.test.tsx`, "drops a decode that settles while unbuffered, so buffering again resumes from the current src" | line 209: `b.png` where `c.png` was expected |
| T3 | `App.test.tsx`, "= and - and 0 move the drawn rect, and 0 puts it back", given an assertion after its settle | line 796: `?w=1536` where `?w=1024` was expected |
| T4 | `App.test.tsx`, "a turn and a turn back before the page decodes leave the page the reader is on" | line 808: `pages/3` where `pages/2` was expected |
| T5 | `App.test.tsx`, "in two mode, a turn onto a solo page and back leaves both halves of the pair" | line 1171: `pages/4` in both cells where `pages/3` and `pages/2` were expected |

All five were written before the fix and failed. Each break below was then
applied by hand to the final code, the five run under `--reporter=default`,
and the file put back and compared byte for byte:

| applied to the final code | T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 | T5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main`'s `PageView.tsx` | red | red | red | red | red |
| the number taken but not drawn under: `setShown(src)` in place of `inOrder` | red | red | red | red | red |
| the unbuffered path alone put back | passes | red | passes | passes | passes |
| the return to `shown` alone put back | red | passes | red | red | red |

Each red test failed at the line and value in the first table. cargo-mutants
does not cover `web/`, so these are the mutation evidence. T3 now asserts after
its settle, which the O75 section above says none of its seven tests did.

### `two` mode, and the unbuffered path

Two throwaway tests, run once against the unfixed code and deleted:

- **`two` mode.** A break at slot 5 left slot 4 a group of its own. From the
  pair at slots 2 and 3, a turn and a turn back before settling left both cells
  drawing `pages/4`, and the second cell carried `aria-hidden="true"`.
  `GroupView` sets that when `secondCellAlone` answers true, and it compares
  what each cell last reported through `onShown`, so the defect reached
  `drawnSrcs` and hid the reader's second page. T5 pins this.
- **The unbuffered path.** `App.tsx` computes `buffered` as
  `mode !== 'scroll' && prefetchPrefs.enabled`, and scroll mode is a different
  arm of the page area's ternary, so switching the Prefetch module off is what
  makes a mounted cell unbuffered. A turn to slot 3 started a decode. Switched
  off through the settings panel, the cell drew `pages/3` unbuffered. A turn
  drew `pages/4`, and a settle let the slot-3 decode finish while the cell was
  unbuffered. Switched back on, the reader drew `pages/3` until a settle, and
  then `pages/4`. T2 pins the mechanism at the component, where the late decode
  is what `shown` holds when buffering resumes.

### Not checked

- The production host, a touch device, and the wheel or a pinch.
- `two` mode and the unbuffered path in a browser: both were seen in jsdom only.
- How often reading returns to the drawn page before its decode settles. The
  drives above chose the timing.

### Counts, and isolation

The web suite now counts 1,157 tests in `node`, unchanged, and 955 in `jsdom`,
four more: T1, T2, T4 and T5 are new and T3 is an existing test. The `browser`
project still counts 28. `check-all.sh` ended `all green, except NOT MEASURED:
standing corpus checks (TAIYAKU_CORPUS unset)`.

`date -Iseconds` was stamped at 2026-09-14T19:36:26-07:00, before the first
server started. After the last run, with every server stopped by PID,
`find corpus -newermt 2026-09-14T19:36:26-07:00` returned nothing.

## O71: the works handlers are tested directly, and the guard keeps its test — 2026-09-14

O71 recorded that `routes/tests.rs`'s `a_progress_read_does_not_stall_the_runtime`
passed with `get_progress` moved wholly onto the async worker. The request it
drives passes `auth::guard` first, and the guard's own `spawn_blocking` frees
the reactor before any handler touches SQLite. It named the ten `routes.rs`
handlers that do their work inside `spawn_blocking` as having nothing else
guarding that, and `curation/tests.rs`'s direct-call test as the shape of a fix.

### How a handler was moved

Each change replaced `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(` on one line with
`on_the_async_worker(`, and appended to the file

```rust
async fn on_the_async_worker<T>(f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, tokio::task::JoinError> {
    Ok(f())
}
```

so the closure runs where the handler is polled, and the `.await` and the
`JoinError` arm after it still compile. A script checked that the line held a
`spawn_blocking`, ran `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
--no-fail-fast`, copied the saved file back and compared it byte for byte.
Every run below restored cleanly, and `git diff -- crates/` hashed the same
before the ten handler runs and after the last run of this section.

### The premise, re-proved

On `6a2e72d`'s code, with `get_progress`'s closure moved (`routes.rs` line
1323): `2129 tests run: 2129 passed, 4 skipped`, and
`a_progress_read_does_not_stall_the_runtime` passed in 0.045 s. Nothing else in
the workspace saw it.

### The handlers, enumerated

`routes.rs` at `6a2e72d` holds ten `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(` calls, one in
each of `list_works` (line 410), `get_page` (793), `get_thumb` (864),
`get_notes` (995), `put_notes` (1066), `get_truth` (1177), `put_truth` (1246),
`get_progress` (1323), `put_progress` (1364) and `patch_alignments` (1647).
`routes/` holds only `tests.rs`. The row's list is complete and current. The
one other handler, `get_sidecar`, has no closure: it answers from the sidecar in
memory.

Two of the ten do no store work in theirs. `get_page`'s closure reads the page
through `ServeState::page`, which is the `PageSource`, and `get_thumb`'s reads
the tile cache and then the page. Neither calls `state.library.conn()`, and for

### What the old test does see

With `auth::guard`'s resolution moved instead (`auth.rs` line 432):
`2129 tests run: 2128 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped`. The one failure was
`routes::tests::a_progress_read_does_not_stall_the_runtime`, at
`routes/tests.rs:633`: "the runtime polled nothing else for half a second: the
progress read is running on the async worker rather than behind
spawn_blocking". No test outside `routes/tests.rs` and `curation/tests.rs` runs
a canary, and `auth.rs`'s doc on `guard` already said this test caught the

So the test was kept. It moved to `auth/tests.rs` as
`the_guard_does_not_stall_the_runtime`, its body unchanged but for the failure

`routes::tests::no_works_route_stalls_the_runtime` calls all ten handlers

down compare identical with `main`'s; `no_curation_route_stalls_the_runtime`
calls it from there. Each call asserts `!stalled` with a message naming the

The principal is the fixture account with an empty grant. The fixture,

With roots, `refuse_if_hidden` (in `get_page` and `get_thumb`, and twice in
`patch_alignments`) and `visible_editions_or_refuse` (in `get_sidecar`, and

`no_curation_route_stalls_the_runtime` says `routes.rs` uses `spawn_blocking`
"in every handler but `get_sidecar`" and names only `get_sidecar` for this. The
new test uses an empty grant so that this does not decide it.

## O94: the account screen has a URL of its own — 2026-09-14

O94 recorded that `Account.tsx`, the one screen where an account changes its
own password, was mounted only by `App.tsx`, which `Routes.tsx` mounts on
`/read/:work` alone, and that C4 PR C's `UserRow` sends an administrator there
when `users_api::patch_user` refuses a reset of their own password.

### The premise, on `main` (`6a2e72d`)

- `Routes.tsx` declared seven routes: `/`, `/series/:id`, `/search`,
  `/proposals`, `/config/*`, `/read/:work` and `*`. None was an account route.
- `git grep '<Account' 6a2e72d -- web/src` found it rendered in `App.tsx`
  alone outside the tests, which are `Account.test.tsx`'s mounts and a comment
  in `App.test.tsx`. `App.tsx` renders it unconditionally with `visible={accountOpen}`, and
  `accountOpen` is set by `keyPlan`'s `open-account`, which `keys.ts` binds to
  `A`.
- `UserRow.tsx`'s refusal read "That is the account panel — open any work and
  press A. It has no URL of its own yet (O94)."
- `users_api::patch_user` answers a password patch whose target is the caller
  with a refusal whose sentence names `/api/password`.
- What `Account` took from the reader was three props: `visible`, `onClose`,
  and `onSignedOut`, which `App` passes as `gate?.signOut()`. Its data come from
  `api.ts`'s `listKeys`, `listSessions`, `createKey`, `revokeKey`,
  `revokeSession`, `changePassword` and `logout`, none of which names a work.
  `Shell` provides the sidebar, `BrowseSettings`, `<main>`,
  `BrowsePrefsContext`, `InboxRefreshContext` and `StatusContext`, and hands
  `Sidebar` the gate's `admin` bit, which draws Proposals and Configuration only
  when it is true.

All of it held, and nothing in the row was found wrong.

### What the specs say

None names a URL or a placement. C4's screens design lists "a general account
screen outside the reader" as out of scope, and §6.1 says making the panel
reachable "is a change to the reader's chrome and is out of scope here. Worth
an open item on the way out." C1's browse design sketches the sidebar in §2
with no account entry. A2's auth design says in §9 that A2 ships "an account
screen", and names no route. C1's shell plan mentions the account only in
`keyplan`'s `accountOpen` guard and the key table's account row. So `/account`, linked beside `/config`, was
chosen, and the reader's panel was kept, since nothing asks for its removal.

### The fix

`/account` mounts `<Shell><AccountScreen /></Shell>`, and `AccountScreen`
hands `Account` the gate's `signOut`. The sidebar's Account link follows
Configuration and takes no guard. `Account` takes a `placement`. `'panel'`, the
default, is what `App` renders, and is unchanged. `'page'` renders a
`<section class="account" aria-label="Account">` holding a heading and the same
three sections, with no overlay and no Close. The panel's colours —
`sectionStyle`, `fieldStyle`, `secretStyle`, the alert's `#ffb4a8` and the
notice's `#a8ffb4` — moved into `LOOKS.panel`, and `LOOKS.page` is empty;
`index.css`'s `.account` block borders in `ButtonBorder` and inherits the
text colour. `UserRow`'s refusal now ends "Change your own on your account
screen", with the last three words a link to `/account`. `gate.ts`'s doc for
`signOut` named only the panel's Sign out button, and now names both.

A first `.account label` rule drew biome's `noDescendingSpecificity` warning
against `.root-row .fields label`. It was replaced by a margin on
`.account input`, after which `biome check` reported nothing.

Written before the fix and run against `main`'s components, all seven failed:

| `Sidebar.test.tsx`, "offers an admin the account screen too" | `expected undefined to be 'Account'` |

## O78: a fold drops a note copy the target already holds — 2026-09-14

O78 recorded that `fold::absorb` refuses the whole fold whenever one reader
holds one note id on both works, whatever the two rows hold, and that the
identical case — "same id, same body, and the same anchor once the mapped
edition's slot rewrite is accounted for" — loses nothing when the source's copy
is dropped, and nothing does it.

### The premise, checked

`fold::shared_note_ids` joined `note` to itself on `user_id` and `id` and
returned every id it found; `absorb` refused on a non-empty list. On `main`,
all 25 `fold::tests` passed, and one of them,
`the_shared_note_refusal_counts_the_ids_and_shows_a_few`, wrote five ids
identical in every column on both works and asserted a refusal. Migration 005's
rationale is as the row quotes it.

**There is no slot rewrite.** `move_notes` is `UPDATE note SET work_id = ?2,
edition = ?4 WHERE work_id = ?1 AND edition = ?3`. `edition_map` pairs editions
whose members carry the same digests in the same `ordinal` order, so slot and
region carry across unchanged and the edition key is the only part of an
anchor a fold rewrites. *Not true of every fold, marked here rather than
rewritten: a slot is an index into one edition's spread flags, and O121 found
the fold carrying it onto a twin that held none — see "O76 and O121".*

**The row's definition left three columns unsettled.** `PRAGMA
table_info(note)`, read in sqlite3 3.53.4 after replaying all thirteen
migrations, gives `user_id`, `id`, `work_id`, `edition`, `slot`, `rx`, `ry`,
`rw`, `rh`, `color`, `body`, `created` and `updated`, keyed
`(user_id, work_id, id)`; no migration after 005 names `note`. "Same body, same
anchor" says nothing about `color`, which the reader can change on an existing
note, or `created` and `updated`, which the client mints and
`state::merge_notes` reads to choose between two copies. Work stopped there and
the question went to the user, who answered: every column matches.

**"No ordinary path back out" is not supported.** `notes::validate` exempts an
anchor already stored and unchanged from the edition and slot checks, so a note
on a key a re-solve renamed survives later writes. But `absorb` runs `stranded`
before `shared_note_ids`, and `stranded` refuses any note on a key the edition
map does not hold, so a note the grandfathering keeps never reaches the shared-id
check. Deleting one copy through the app was not tried.

### The rule, and NULL

Two copies of one id, for one reader, are one note when `body`, `slot`, `rx`,
`ry`, `rw`, `rh`, `color`, `created` and `updated` are equal and the target's
`edition` is exactly the key `edition_map` sends the source's edition to. The
comparison is a derived `PartialEq` over a Rust struct of those nine columns,
beside `map.get(&from_key) == Some(&into_key)`.

It is in Rust rather than SQL because of NULL. The ordinary note — the whole
slot, the default colour — carries NULL in all five nullable columns. In the
same sqlite3:

| expression | result |
| --- | --- |
| `NULL = NULL` | NULL |
| `NULL IS NULL` | 1 |
| `CASE WHEN NULL = NULL THEN 'true' ELSE 'not true' END` | `not true` |
| `1 AND (NULL = NULL)` | NULL |

A comparison written with `=` calls two whole-slot copies different. Rust's
`None == None` is `true`.

### Order

The source's identical copies are deleted after the last of `absorb`'s five
refusal checks — the truth-provenance one — and before the move loop, whose
`UPDATE` would otherwise collide on those ids. Every refusal therefore stays a
`SELECT`. The transaction's rollback would also undo a delete made before a
refusal, so a test comparing the table before and after cannot see that
ordering; the refusal tests create triggers that raise on any insert, update or
delete of `note` before calling `absorb`, so such a write comes back as an
`Err`.

### What reports it

`Moved::dropped_notes` counts the deleted copies and `Moved::notes` still counts
only rows moved. `derive` sums the first into a new `DeriveReport::dropped_notes`;
the CLI's `derive_summary` prints it inside the fold's parenthesis as
"identical note(s) dropped"; `config_api::derive_report_json` sends
`dropped_notes`; and `ScanReport.tsx` draws it as "Identical notes dropped",
beside "Notes moved". The web `Derived` type and the four test fixtures that
build one needed the field as well, and the comments counting its fields moved
from twenty-nine to thirty. `preview::preview_with_rows` runs the real derive
in a transaction it rolls back and reads only `report.raised` from it, so a
rule preview carries no fold figure for a dropped copy to disagree with.

A refusal now names only the ids whose copies differ, and says so: "one reader
holds N note id(s) on both work A and work B whose two copies differ".

### The tests

`one_note_id_held_on_both_works_refuses_the_fold` became
`a_note_id_whose_two_copies_sit_on_different_slots_refuses_the_fold`, since its
two copies differ only in slot. `the_shared_note_refusal_counts_the_ids_and_shows_a_few`
wrote identical copies and asserted a refusal, which the rule now contradicts;
each work's copy now carries its own body, and the count and the three-ids
message are still asserted.

New in `fold::tests`: an identical whole-slot pair folding, with two other notes
moving beside it and the target's row read back by `rowid`; a pair with a sized
region and a colour on keys that map onto each other; one refusal each for body,
colour, `updated`, `created`, region and an edition key that does not map; one
identical id and one that differs, refused whole; and a second reader holding
the same id on the superseded work only. `derive`'s fan-out test gained an
eighth field, eight identical copies on both works, and
`derive_summary_says_what_a_fold_moved_and_what_its_delete_took` a fifty-five.
`ScanReport.test.tsx` counts forty-two fields and pairs "Identical notes
dropped" with its number per element.

With `dropped_notes` added and `absorb` unchanged, four of the new fold tests
failed. The three that expect a fold panicked with "the fold was refused: one
reader holds 1 note id(s) on both work 2 and work 1"; the mixed test's message
read "holds 2 note id(s)", naming the identical id beside the one that differs.

### The tests, watched against each defect

A script applied each change as a replacement that had to match exactly once,
ran `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` with `TAIYAKU_CORPUS` unset,
restored every file it had touched and compared it byte for byte. A control
with no change ran first and passed all 2139. Afterwards, `git diff` outside
`docs/` matched a snapshot taken before the run, apart from two edits made
after the snapshot: `fold.rs`'s `Moved` literal, which clippy asked for, and a
doc comment in `curation.ts`. Paths below are in `crates/taiyaku-library/src/`.

| defect | tests that failed | where, and with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compare `body` alone | the refusals over slot, region, colour, `updated`, `created` and an unmapped key | `fold/tests.rs:1703`: "dropping the identical copy of note `01JSHARED…` off work 2: a fold that should have refused wrote to note" |
| compare the raw edition keys | the two identical folds, the mixed fold, the second reader, the unmapped key, `derive`'s fan-out | `fold/tests.rs:112`: "the fold was refused … whose two copies differ"; `fold/tests.rs:1973`: "holds 2 note id(s)"; the unmapped key at `:1703` |
| ignore the edition | the unmapped key | `fold/tests.rs:1703` |
| drop copies that differ | all seven single-difference refusals, the mixed fold, the count test | `fold/tests.rs:1703`; `:1559`: "five note ids collided, yet it folded: Moved { … dropped_notes: 5 … }" |
| drop the target's copy | the two identical folds, the second reader, `derive`'s fan-out | `fold/tests.rs:1808` and `:1843`: the target's row under another rowid; `:2042`: `(2, 1)` against `(1, 1)` |
| drop before the last refusal | the mixed fold | `fold/tests.rs:1703` |
| the same, with the test's triggers removed | none | 2139 passed |
| ignore `color` | the colour refusal | `fold/tests.rs:1703` |
| ignore `updated` | the `updated` refusal | `fold/tests.rs:1703` |
| ignore `created` | the `created` refusal | `fold/tests.rs:1703` |
| NULL regions compare unequal | the whole-slot fold, the second reader, the mixed fold, `derive`'s fan-out | `fold/tests.rs:112`: "the fold was refused"; `:1973`: "holds 2 note id(s)" |
| count dropped copies as moved | the two identical folds, the second reader, `derive`'s fan-out | `fold/tests.rs:1814`: `(3, 1)` against `(2, 1)`; `:1848`: `(1, 1)` against `(0, 1)` |
| the delete without `user_id` | the second reader | `fold/tests.rs:2037`: reader 2's rows differ |
| the match without `user_id` | the second reader | `fold/tests.rs:2037` |
| `derive` never adds `dropped_notes` | the fan-out | `derive/tests.rs:3228` |

| `ScanReport.tsx`'s row reads `moved_notes` | "draws identical notes dropped apart from notes moved" | `expected '3' to be '7'` |

Under "NULL regions compare unequal" the mapped-key fold, whose copies carry a
sized region, stayed green; every fixture that failed holds whole-slot copies,
which is the case that defect breaks. The two
`ScanReport.tsx` changes ran `ScanReport.test.tsx` alone under

**One failure was not the defect.** The run that dropped the target's copy also

*Filed as O117 on 2026-09-14.*

## O70: a refusal is an offer, and a store fault is a 500 — 2026-09-14

O70 recorded that `proposals::{evidence, resolves, accept_with, unaccept,
dismiss}` report "no such row", "the library refuses this" and "the read
failed" as one `Err(String)`. After `lookup` and `evaluable`, what was left
was the write half: a store fault during an accept answered 409, because
`curation.rs` mapped the one type `accept_with` returned onto
`NoAnswer::Refused`.

### What each `Err` was, on `main`

Read from `proposals.rs` at `6a2e72d`, following each function's own `?` and
every helper it reaches. *Refusal* is a state the library declines, *missing*
is no such proposal, and *store* is an error SQLite returned.

| function | where | class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accept_with` | `acceptable_proposal`, through `one` and `lookup` | missing, or store |
| | `acceptable`: not `open`, `attach-chapters`, no `target_id` | refusal, three |
| | `resolves`' own `SELECT subject_id, target_id` | missing only if the row goes between `one` and it; otherwise store |
| | `resolves`, through `engine_parts`: an unknown `kind` or `match_on`, a `regex` that will not compile | refusal: the rule cannot be evaluated |
| | `resolves`, through `rules::read`, `scan::roots`, the `scan_entry` sweep, `series_id_by_sort_title`, `open`, `answers` and `works_moved` | store |
| | collateral, a target reached, nothing matched, the subject not reached, nothing moved | refusal, five |
| | `unchecked_transaction`, the ordinal query, `INSERT INTO rule`, both `UPDATE proposal` statements, `commit` | store, six |
| | this proposal, or another the rule answers, no longer `open` at its `UPDATE` | refusal, two |
| `unaccept` | `one` | missing, or store |
| | no `created_rule_id` | refusal |
| | `unchecked_transaction`, the reopening `UPDATE`, `DELETE FROM rule`, `commit` | store, four |
| `dismiss` | `one` | missing, or store |
| | `state = 'accepted'` | refusal |
| | `UPDATE proposal` | store |
| `evidence` | `one` | missing, or store |
| | `series_title`, `rel_paths_by_series`, `side`'s reads, `scored_reasons`, `offered_rule`'s reads | store |
| | every refusal `offered_rule` makes | not an `Err`: `rule: None` |
| `resolves` | its own `SELECT` | missing, or store |
| | `engine_parts` | the rule cannot be evaluated |
| | every read after it | store |
| | collateral and the other four | not an `Err`: fields of `Resolution` |

So `evidence` and `resolves` had nothing left to split: their `Err` is a
missing row or a failed read, plus, for `resolves`, a rule the caller wrote
that cannot be evaluated, which the dry-run route asks `evaluable` about
first. The three writes had all three classes in one type.

### The row, against the code

Two of its claims did not hold in `791df0a` (#88), the commit that filed the
row and added `Offer`, and do not hold on `main`:

- `evidence` did not report "the library refuses this" as an `Err`. It read
  `offered_rule` and answered `Offer::Refused(_) => None`, so its `Err`
  carried only a missing row or a failed read.
- "All three functions are public API with `taiyaku-cli` callers."
  `taiyaku-cli` calls `dismiss` and `unaccept`, and reaches `accept_with` only
  through `accept`. `rules::delete` also calls `unaccept`, and the row does not
  name it; `config_api::delete_rule` reaches it from the server.

### On `main`, driven

The tests were written first and run against `main`'s `proposals.rs` and
`curation.rs`. A trigger raises `ABORT` with the text `a simulated store
fault`.

| route | fault | status on `main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST …/{id}/accept` | trigger `BEFORE INSERT ON rule` | **409**: `writing the rule for proposal 1: a simulated store fault` |
| `POST …/{id}/accept` | `DROP TABLE scan_entry` | **409**: `reading scan entries for the dry run: no such table: scan_entry` |
| `DELETE …/{id}/accept`, after an accept | trigger `BEFORE DELETE ON rule` | **409**: `removing the rule proposal 1 wrote: a simulated store fault` |
| `POST …/{id}/dismiss` | trigger `BEFORE UPDATE OF state ON proposal WHEN NEW.state = 'dismissed'` | **409**: `dismissing proposal 1: a simulated store fault` |
| `GET …/{id}` and `POST …/{id}/resolution` | `DROP TABLE scan_entry` | 500 on both: `a_store_fault_under_a_real_id_is_a_500_on_both_routes_that_read_beneath_it` passed |
| all five id-addressed routes | id 9999 | 404: `an_unknown_id_is_a_404_on_every_route_that_takes_one` passed |

The un-accept fault sits on the `DELETE` that follows the reopening `UPDATE`
in one transaction, so a proposal still reading `accepted` afterwards also
shows the rollback. The two new CLI tests passed on `main`: a refused
`--unaccept` and a refused `--dismiss` each exit 1 with `taiyaku: ` and the
library's sentence on their own line, and print no success line. That is the
behaviour the change had to keep.

### The shape

`Offer<T>` was private, for `preview`. It is `pub` now, derives `PartialEq`
and carries `#[must_use]`, and the three writes return it inside their
`Result`:

- `accept_with(conn, id, rule) -> Result<Offer<i64>, String>`
- `unaccept(conn, id) -> Result<Offer<()>, String>`
- `dismiss(conn, id) -> Result<Offer<()>, String>`
- `evidence` and `resolves` are unchanged.

A missing row stays in the `Err`, worded by `one`. No third variant was added
for it: every write handler calls `present` first and answers 404 from
`lookup`, and the CLI prints either. `acceptable` reads nothing, so it returns
a bare `Offer`. `accept_with` calls `engine_parts` before `resolves`, because
`resolves`' `Err` folds a rule it cannot evaluate with a failed read. Without
that call, a mistyped pattern sent to the accept route would come back as a
failed store and a 500. `accept` keeps `Result<i64, String>` and folds a
refusal into its `Err` with `or_refusal`, as `preview` does. It is not one of
the five, and outside tests its only caller is the CLI's `--accept`.

In `curation.rs`, each write handler maps the `Err` to `NoAnswer::Failed` and
hands the `Offer` to `made`, which maps `Refused` to `NoAnswer::Refused`.
Nothing reads the sentence to decide which. The CLI's `--dismiss` and
`--unaccept` turn `Refused(why)` into `Err(why)`, which `main` prints as
`taiyaku: {why}` before exiting 1. `rules::delete` returns it as its own
error, as it did.

`proposals_dismiss_and_unaccept_reach_the_library_crate` passes M5c because it

M1a's first run also failed six `taiyaku-cli` `tests::serve_works_*` tests,
each with `opening the library: creating meta: disk I/O error`. They write
fixed names under `std::env::temp_dir()` with no process id in them, such as
`taiyaku-test-serve-works-single.db`, and four other worktrees on this machine
were running the same suite. `/tmp` had 25 GB free. Run again alone, M1a
failed only the two accept tests above, and both runs with no defect applied
passed all six.

*Filed as O117 on 2026-09-14, with no code change.*

### The survivor

M7 is a refusal a test cannot reach on one connection. `rules::delete` looks up
`SELECT id FROM proposal WHERE created_rule_id = ?1` and calls `unaccept` on
the first id, and `unaccept` refuses only when `one` reads no
`created_rule_id` for that row. With nothing between the two reads, the row
the lookup matched still carries it. Reaching the refusal takes a second
connection that un-accepts the proposal in that window. On `main` the same
line propagated the refusal with `?` and was no better covered. It is left
returning the refusal as `rules::delete`'s error, and
`config_api::delete_rule` answers that error 500, as it did.

### Not changed

- `evidence` and `resolves` keep their types, since neither returns a refusal
  as `Err`.
- `accept` keeps `Result<i64, String>`.
- `rules::delete` keeps `Result<Deleted, String>`.
- `web/`. `sendJson` throws `` `${path}: ${res.status} ${body}` `` for any
  status that is not ok, and `ProposalRow` and `AcceptForm` render
  `messageOf(err)`. So a store fault during a write now reads `500` where it
  read `409`, and nothing branches on either.
- The `serve_works_*` tests' fixed temporary names.

### Counts

Rust 2129 → 2140: five tests in `curation::tests`, four in
`proposals::tests`, one in `library::tests` and one in `tests/cli.rs`.
`unaccepting_a_never_accepted_proposal_is_an_error` is now
`unaccepting_a_never_accepted_proposal_is_refused`. `web/` is unchanged. No
server ran, and `corpus/` was not read.

## O83: a series answers its own titles — 2026-09-14

O83 recorded that `PATCH /api/library/series/{id}` replaces a series' whole
title set and that nothing a series GET answers carries that set back, so a
series page could only send the one display string it holds and would delete
every other title. It asked for a read path, not a screen.

### The premise, checked against the code

- `librarydoc::set_series_titles` updates `series.sort_title` to the primary
  title, runs `DELETE FROM series_title WHERE series_id = ?1`, and inserts each
  title it was given with `hand = 1`. It replaces; it does not merge.
- The routes that answer a series, from `routes.rs`'s route table: `GET
  /api/library/series` and `GET /api/library/search` answer `series_json` per
  tile, `GET /api/library/series/{id}` answers `series_json` beside the works,
  `/api/library/series/{id}/cover` is a 307, and `PATCH
  /api/library/series/{id}` answers the re-projected document. `GET
  /api/works` carries a series only as `series.sort_title`, a proposal side
  carries `series_id` and one `title`, and OPDS has no series. No GET carried
  the `{title, kind, primary}` entries.
- The PATCH answer does carry `series.titles`, as `librarydoc::of` projects
  them: `hand = 1` rows only, since O80, and `SeriesTitle` skips a `false`
  `primary`. The first PATCH in the drive below answered
  `{"kind":"native","title":"かぐや様は告らせたい"}`, with no `primary`.
- `SeriesCard.title` is `COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN st.is_primary = 1 THEN
  st.title END), s.sort_title)`: one string, the primary title or `sort_title`.
  The row calls it merged; it is chosen, and marked so in place.
- `MetadataEditor` is mounted once, in `Series.tsx`, inside a volume row's open
  panel, with `onPatch={patchWork}`.
- `PATCH /api/library/series/{id}` takes `SeriesEdit`: `titles`, `reading`,
  `tags` and `external`, each optional. `titles` is a list of `SeriesTitle`:
  `title`, `kind` from the closed set `romaji`, `native`, `english`, `alt`, and
  `primary`, defaulting to false.
- The row says a title edit means sending `LibraryDoc.series.titles` whole. The
  body's `titles` has that field's type but not its rows: the document holds
  only `hand = 1` titles, and `set_series_titles` deletes derivation's row as
  well, so sending the document's list whole would still drop one. That is why
  the read below answers every row rather than the document's, and it is
  marked in place.
- The row's "since C1's fix retired the old resolve-by-title path" matches what
  #91's commit body describes — the whole-branch review's finding and the delta
  review of its fixes — though the body does not use the label "C1".

### Red on `main`

The two tests below were written first, against `main`'s handler and
`librarydoc.rs`. Both failed in `titles_of`, after the fixture's titles were
planted and its id checks passed:

```
series 1 carries no `titles` array: {"series":{"added":1,"aligned":0,"cover":"/api/library/series/1/cover","editions":1,"id":1,"title":"五等分の花嫁","unread":1,"works":1},"works":[…]}
series 2 carries no `titles` array: {"series":{"added":2,"aligned":0,"cover":"/api/library/series/2/cover","editions":1,"id":2,"title":"Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai","unread":1,"works":1},"works":[…]}
```

That run's fixture still had one volume a series; the fixture is described as
it ended, under the tests.

### The fix

`librarydoc::series_titles` reads `SELECT title, kind, is_primary FROM
series_title WHERE series_id = ?1 ORDER BY rowid`, sharing its row parsing with
`series_info_of`, whose query differs only by `AND hand = 1`. `rowid` order is
the order `set_series_titles` inserted, so a list read, edited in place and
sent back reads back in that order.

`library_api::one_series` calls it only in the arm where `browse::one_series`
answered the series, so a series the grant hides stays a 404, and adds
`series.titles` with each entry built as `{title, kind, primary}`, a `false`
`primary` included. `series_title` has no per-root column, the same as the
`series.title` beside it. The grid and search are unchanged.

`library.ts` gains `SeriesDetail`, a `SeriesCard` with `titles:
Required<SeriesTitle>[]`, and `oneSeries` answers it. `Series.test.tsx`'s
fixture is typed to match. `MetadataEditor.tsx`'s module comment said no read
path existed, and now says one does and no screen uses it.

### The tests

`library_api::tests::one_series_carries_each_of_its_titles_in_the_shape_the_patch_route_takes`
reads all three series and checks each entry's `title`, `kind` and `primary`,
that the entry holds exactly those three keys, and the count.
`library_api::tests::a_series_titles_read_corrected_and_sent_back_whole_keep_every_other_title`
reads Kaguya's titles, corrects the romaji entry, sends the whole list as
`PATCH`, and reads all three series again.

`test_support::router_over_three_unrelated_series` scans `Go-Toubun no
Hanayome` v01 and v02, `Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai` v01 and `Oshi no Ko` v01.
`plant_titles` keeps derivation's row on each series — `hand = 0`, re-kinded
`romaji` on Go-Toubun and Kaguya, left `alt` on Oshi no Ko — and plants hand
rows beside it, so each series holds two or three titles and Go-Toubun's
primary is its native title. It then checks two things rather than assuming
them: no series' id equals its position in the grid, counted from nought or
one — Kaguya, id 2, lists first, Oshi no Ko, id 3, second, and Go-Toubun, id 1,
last, because a native title sorts after the romaji ones — and neither
Kaguya's nor Oshi no Ko's work carries its series' id.

### The tests, watched red

Each change was applied by a script that checked its text replaced exactly one
occurrence, ran `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, restored the file and
compared it byte for byte; after the last, `git diff -- crates` was
byte-identical to the one saved before the first. Every run compiled: each red
one counted 2129 passed and 2 failed, and the control 2131 passed.

`shape` is `one_series_carries_each_of_its_titles_in_the_shape_the_patch_route_takes`,
`round trip` is `a_series_titles_read_corrected_and_sent_back_whole_keep_every_other_title`,
and the lines are in `library_api/tests.rs`.

| `"kind"` left out of each entry | line 714, series 1 title 0's kind: `{"primary":false,"title":"Go-Toubun no Hanayome"}` | line 775, one romaji title: no entry has a `kind` |
| only the primary entry, `AND is_primary = 1` | line 710, series 1 title 0's text: `五等分の花嫁` | line 709, after the PATCH: "series 2 has no title 1, `かぐや様は告らせたい`" |
| another series' titles, `series_id != ?1` | line 710, series 1 title 0's text: `Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai` | line 787, the PATCH's status: 409, "series 2 would have more than one primary title" |
| the display string as the one entry, `kind` romaji, primary | line 710, series 1 title 0's text: `五等分の花嫁` | line 709, after the PATCH: "series 2 has no title 1" |

The first four rows are the defects the item's closing had to be seen to

titles it did not send, which is O83's own consequence observed.

**A first pass let one through.** The fixture then held one volume a series,
and derivation minted series and works in the same order, so work 2 sat under
series 2 and work 3 under series 3. With `works[0].id` in place of `card.id`
all 2131 tests passed. A second `Go-Toubun no Hanayome` volume moved Kaguya's
work to id 3 and Oshi no Ko's to 4, `plant_titles` now asserts that neither
shares its series' id. The other six mutants failed both tests in the first
pass as well.

The table above is the third pass. The second ran on the two-volume fixture,
and the third after the round trip's `titled` binding was renamed `ids`, which
`clippy::pedantic`'s advisory `similar_names` had flagged beside `titles`. Both
gave the lines in the table, for every row.

## O114: a title correction keeps the scan's key — 2026-09-15

O114 recorded that a rescan after `PATCH /api/library/series/{id}` minted a
second series under the scanned name and moved every volume onto it, because
`librarydoc::set_series_titles` moved `series.sort_title` and
`derive::reconcile_series` finds a series by it, and it left the fix as a
choice of key. The user chose on 2026-09-15: `sort_title` stays the scan's own
key, and a correction changes only `series_title`.

### Writers and readers of `series.sort_title`, read

Writers on `main`: `derive::reconcile_series` inserts the scanned name;
`librarydoc::apply_series` inserts a document's primary title for a series it
mints, and its matched branch, for a series it found by any shared title,
updated the column to that primary; `set_series_titles` updated it to the
primary title, or the first where none is primary.

Readers that find a series by it: `reconcile_series`;
`proposals::series_id_by_sort_title`, behind a candidate rule's reach and
`raise_attach_chapters`; `proposals::all_series`, behind `raise_edition_of`'s
` - ` prefix and `raise_same_series`'s match against another series' titles;
and `proposals::series_title`, behind `preview`, `offered_rule` (whose
`set_series` is that text), `answers`, `evidence`, `edition_of_signals` and `raise_same_series`'s reason.

Readers that show it, and what a person sees once a series' titles are
corrected:

| reader | shows | on `main` | on this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `browse::series`: the grid, a series page's heading, search's series | the primary title, else `sort_title` | the corrected primary | the corrected primary |
| the same, for a list sent with no primary | — | its first title, because `sort_title` held it | its first title, read in `rowid` order before `sort_title` |
| `download.rs`'s file name, `comicinfo::read`'s `Series` | a title ordered `is_primary DESC, title`, else `sort_title` | a title row: `set_series_titles` refuses an empty list, so `sort_title` is not reached | the same |
| `preview::grouping` | the primary title, else `series {id}` | not `sort_title` | not `sort_title` |
| `proposals::list`'s two titles (`ProposalRow.tsx`), `evidence`'s `Side.title` | `sort_title` | the corrected text, and the evidence sweep found no directory | the scanned name, and the sweep finds the directory |
| `works::summary`'s `series`, `GET /api/works` | `sort_title` | the corrected text | the scanned name; `label.tsx` maps the list to slugs, and no screen shows it |

**The list with no primary** keeps what the grid showed, without storing a
`primary` the caller did not send or refusing a list the route accepts today.

**The proposal readers stay on `sort_title`.** Each names a series the way the
rule an accept writes does — `offered_rule` puts `series_title`'s answer into
`set_series` — and a row naming one text while its rule names another is the
less honest of the two. Whether a row should also show a corrected title is not
decided here.

### A second defect behind the first

`reconcile_series` ran `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO series_title (series_id, title,
is_primary) VALUES (?1, ?2, 1)` on every pass. On `main` a correction that
replaced the scanned text sent the next pass to a new series, so that row landed
there. With the key frozen it lands on the corrected series: the text the
correction removed returns, marked primary, beside the corrected primary.
Found by reading while writing the fix, and M3 below is it put back. The row is now
written only onto a series holding no title, which a series minted in the same
call always is.

| --- | --- |

| `derive::tests::a_rescan_after_a_correction_making_another_title_primary_keeps_the_series` | failed: 3 series against 2 |
| `derive::tests::a_rescan_after_a_correction_keeping_the_scanned_primary_keeps_the_series` | passed |
| `derive::tests::a_rescan_after_a_document_names_another_primary_title_keeps_the_series` | failed: 3 series against 2 |

The kept-primary case answers what the row left unmeasured: a correction that
keeps the scanned text primary survived a rescan before the fix. The grid's

## O115: a grant is asked on the blocking pool — 2026-09-15

O115 recorded that for a reader whose grant names roots, `refuse_if_hidden`
and `visible_editions_or_refuse` call `state.library.conn()` in the handler,
on the async worker, before any `spawn_blocking`, in four `routes.rs`
handlers. "O71", "A reader with a grant", measured it with the handlers
unchanged.

### Eight handlers, not four

`refuse_if_hidden` is `pub(crate)`. A search for both names across `crates/`
on `aaacc2b` finds four callers besides the four the row named:
`opds::stream_page`, `opds::cover`, `download::edition` and
`download::member`, each asking `refuse_if_hidden` first in the handler,
before its own `spawn_blocking`. Nothing else calls either check.

The stall test below, run with only the tests, their fixture and `pub(crate)`
on the two OPDS handlers added to `aaacc2b`, failed with every one of the
eight stalled, and every call answered 200:

```
for a reader whose grant names roots, these asked it on the async worker: ["get_sidecar", "get_page", "get_thumb", "patch_alignments", "opds::stream_page", "opds::cover", "download::edition", "download::member"]
```

### Where the check went

Not into each handler's closure, as the row proposed. `get_page`,
`get_sidecar` and `opds::stream_page` each answer a matching `If-None-Match`
with 304 before their closures run, and a hidden work has to be refused before
that answer. In the closure, the check would have come after the 304.

Both checks now go through `routes::on_the_grant`. With no principal, or a
principal whose grant is empty, it returns the unrestricted answer on the
async worker without touching the library, as before. For a grant that names
roots it clones the principal and runs the check on the blocking pool. Each
handler awaits the check where it called it before.

`patch_alignments` asked three times: `visible_editions_or_refuse`, then, once
the body had parsed, `refuse_if_hidden` for `from` and for `to`. It now parses
the body first, keeping the `Result`, asks all three in one trip through
`visible_editions_for_a_correction` on one connection, and refuses a body that
did not parse only after the trip has answered. A hidden work is still refused
before a malformed body, and a hidden side before a malformed slot. One trip
rather than three also keeps all three inside what the stall test measures.

### The tests

- `routes::tests::no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` calls all eight handlers
  directly under `test_support::the_runtime_stalls_on`, as a reader granted
  root 1. Its fixture, `test_support::state_whose_grant_waits_on_the_library`,
  is O71's with two changes: every member moved under root 1, because an
  imported member's `root_id` is NULL and no grant admits one, and the work's
  four archives written, because the download routes read them. Every call is
  asserted to answer 200. The stalls are collected, so a failing run names
  every handler that stalled.
- `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_validator_is_answered` sends `get_page`,
  `get_sidecar` and `opds::stream_page` the tag each answers 304 to. Granted
  root 2, which holds nothing, each must answer 404; granted root 1, 304.
- `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_correction_is_read` sends
  `patch_alignments` the body `not a correction`: 404 for root 2, 400 for
  root 1.

The second and third also pass on `aaacc2b`'s handlers. They hold an order the
fix had to keep, not one it changed.

**What the stall test cannot see.** The watchdog holds the library's mutex
once and releases it when the canary runs, so it measures a call's first wait
on that mutex. For each handler here that wait is the grant check. A second
wait on the async worker after the check would pass.

### Watched red

Each change was applied to the final code by a script that checked it replaced
exactly one occurrence, or the named one of two. The script then ran
`cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`, restored the file and
compared its sha256. The eight "back on the async worker" changes call a
synchronous copy of the check as `aaacc2b` had it, appended to `routes.rs` for
that run only. Every run compiled. The control counted 2156 passed and 0
failed, and each red run 2156 less the failures listed.

| applied to the final code | failed | with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing, the control | nothing | 2156 passed |
| `get_sidecar`'s check back on the async worker | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["get_sidecar"]` |
| `get_page`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["get_page"]` |
| `get_thumb`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["get_thumb"]` |
| `patch_alignments`' three, on one connection | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["patch_alignments"]` |
| `opds::stream_page`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["opds::stream_page"]` |
| `opds::cover`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["opds::cover"]` |
| `download::edition`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["download::edition"]` |
| `download::member`'s | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | `["download::member"]` |
| `on_the_grant` calling the check without `spawn_blocking` | `no_grant_check_stalls_the_runtime` | all eight |
| `get_page` asking after its 304 | `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_validator_is_answered` | `get_page, granted root 2`: 304 for 404 |
| `get_sidecar` asking after its 304 | `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_validator_is_answered` | `get_sidecar, granted root 2`: 304 for 404 |
| `opds::stream_page` asking after its 304 | `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_validator_is_answered` | `opds::stream_page, granted root 2`: 304 for 404 |
| `patch_alignments` refusing the body before the trip | `a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_correction_is_read` | `patch_alignments, granted root 2`: 400 for 404 |
| neither side of a correction asked | `auth::tests`' `a_correction_naming_the_withheld_edition_on_the_from_side_is_still_refused`, `patch_alignments_refuses_a_correction_naming_a_withheld_edition` and `every_route_declares_its_grant_posture` | 200 for 404, each |
| only `from` asked | `patch_alignments_refuses_a_correction_naming_a_withheld_edition` and `every_route_declares_its_grant_posture` | 200 for 404, each |
| only `to` asked | `a_correction_naming_the_withheld_edition_on_the_from_side_is_still_refused` | 200 for 404 |
| the fixture's `UPDATE` removed, leaving every member under no root | all three new tests | 404 at each test's first call: `get_sidecar` for 200, `get_page` granted root 1 for 304, `patch_alignments` granted root 1 for 400 |

The three "side" rows are about the one-trip rewrite rather than the stall:
they show `auth::tests`' existing correction tests still reach each side's
check through `visible_editions_for_a_correction`.

### Flake runs

The stall test alone, 30 times through `cargo test -- --exact`: 30 passed,
each in 0.23–0.25 s, at one-minute load averages from 17.29 to 14.12 on 32
CPUs, read before the first run and after every tenth.

### Found beside it, not changed

A throwaway test in `opds/tests.rs`, removed afterwards and the file compared

- OPDS's `works` and `work_feed` ask a grant that names roots on the async

### Also changed

- `routes/tests.rs`'s `as_the_fixture_account` doc said a principal with roots
