## O117: every test's temp directory from one helper — 2026-09-15

O117 recorded that tests wrote fixed names under `std::env::temp_dir()`, and
that two suites running at once on one machine had failed twice for it
without anyone reproducing it on purpose. It is reproduced here first, then
closed with one helper that every crate's tests now take their directories
from, and a test that fails if a new one is written the old way.

### The collision, reproduced

Two copies of one test binary were started together, ten times, with one
`TMPDIR` shared between the two copies and a different one for each binary.
That is what two checkouts sharing `/tmp` look like, reduced to one checkout.
The binaries were built from `aaacc2b`. Each filter passed on its own first.

| binary, filter | attempts with a failure | copies that failed | what they said |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `taiyaku-cli` unit tests, `serve_works_` (6 tests) | 10 of 10 | 14 of 20 | `opening the library: setting WAL: disk I/O error`, and `…/taiyaku-test-serve-works-hub-grows/taiyaku.json: No such file or directory` |
| `taiyaku-serve`, `auth::tests::every_route_refuses_an_anonymous_request` | 6 of 10 | 6 of 20 | `NotFound` at `test_support.rs:23:82` five times, at `test_support.rs:45:33` once |
| `taiyaku-read`, every test (65) | 10 of 10 | 20 of 20 | between 3 and 16 failures a copy, 24 tests among them: `invalid Zip archive: Could not find EOCD`, `No such file or directory`, `File exists`, and `renaming the temporary into place: No such file or directory` |

The first two rows are the failures behind the row, `disk I/O error` for the
six `serve_works_*` tests and `NotFound` at `test_support.rs:23`, now seen on
demand rather than once each by accident.

### The helper

`taiyaku_read::test_support::TempDir`: `TempDir::new(label)` makes
`taiyaku-test-{label}-{pid}-{n}` under the temp dir, where `n` is a
process-wide counter, and its `Drop` removes it. It removes a directory
already at that name first, since only a run killed before its `Drop` leaves
one. It derefs to `Path`, so `&dir` goes where a `&Path` did and `dir.join(…)`
reads as it did when `dir` was a `PathBuf`, which is what let most sites move
without rewriting what they did with the path. A label holding `/` is refused.

It lives in `taiyaku-read`'s `test_support` because that is the one crate
every crate with tests depends on — `taiyaku-library`, `taiyaku-serve` and
`taiyaku-cli` all do, and `taiyaku-core` and `taiyaku-wasm` write no temp
files — and because that module was already shared through the
`test-support` feature, which only a `[dev-dependencies]` entry enables.
`taiyaku-library` already enabled it for O104; `taiyaku-serve` and
`taiyaku-cli` enable it now. The file name was already excluded by both the
coverage regex and `.cargo/mutants.toml`, so neither changed. `tempfile`
3.27.0 is in `Cargo.lock` as a dependency of `safetensors`; it was not
taken, for the reason the helpers this replaces gave: the workspace's
dependency list is short enough to quote in `docs/status.md`, and this is the
whole of what that crate would be used for.

There were four copies of the same shape on `aaacc2b` —
`taiyaku-read`'s `format/tests.rs`, `taiyaku-library`'s `tests.rs` and
`export/tests.rs`, and `taiyaku-serve`'s `test_support::Fixture` — and each is
now this type. `Fixture` stays in `taiyaku-serve` as a type alias for it.

### What moved

On `aaacc2b`, `git grep 'temp_dir()'` over `crates/` counts 138 lines in 32
files. On this branch, untracked files included, it counts five, all in the
helper's own two files: its one call, its test's assertion that a directory
is under the temp dir, and the standing check's name and two lines of its
doc. The rest, by shape:

- **A literal name**, removed and recreated or not: now a `TempDir`, with the
  file the test wanted inside it.
- **A name a helper was handed.** `taiyaku-serve`'s `test_support::work`,
  `state`, `state_with_two_editions`, `work_with_edition_key` and `log` take a
  directory rather than a name; `aaacc2b` held over 160 calls to them. So do
  seventeen local helpers in `taiyaku-serve`'s test modules and seven in
  `taiyaku-cli`'s. Each caller makes a guard just before the statement that
  needs it and passes `&tmp`. `test_support::cleanup` and its 156 calls are
  gone: the guard removes the directory, and does so when a test panics,
  which the call at the end of a test never reached.
- **A process id and no counter**, in `taiyaku-cli`'s `cache`, `library`,
  `score` and `user` tests, `tests/cli.rs`'s `db_path` and its two rule
  documents, `taiyaku-library`'s `backup` and `migrate` tests and
  `taiyaku-serve`'s `cache_root` tests, and three single tests that built one
  inline. These did not collide between runs. They left one directory per
  test per run behind, and now return a guard.
- **A name nothing greps for.** Five covers directories were placed beside a
  `Fixture` with `with_file_name` — four under fixed names such as
  `taiyaku-test-two-scanned-roots-covers`, one per prefix — so a covers cache
  was shared by every run and outlived all of them. Where the fixture's roots
  are subdirectories, covers go in `covers/` inside it. Where the fixture's
  own directory was the scan root — `router_over_a_scanned_tree`, and so
  every fixture built on it, and `router_over_two_scanned_volumes_of_one_series`
  — the tree moved to `tree/` and covers to `covers/`, the layout
  `router_over_a_scanned_cbz` already used. `router_over_a_library` returns
  its `Fixture` now, for its covers alone.

One helper depended on the old names. `duplicates::tests`' `synthetic_pages`
read a copy's role from the text after the last `-` in its whole path, which
is now the counter; the copy is named for its role inside its own directory,
and the role is read from the file name; three tests failed until it was.
And `tests/cli.rs`'s scan tests would have put their database inside the root
they scan, so the database has a directory of its own.

### The standing check

`test_support::tests::nothing_outside_this_helper_calls_temp_dir` walks every
`.rs` file under `crates/`, skips the helper and comment lines, and fails
naming each line that still calls `temp_dir()`. It also fails if the walk read
100 files or fewer, so a walk that reaches nothing cannot pass. **It sees the
call and nothing else**: a fixed name reached another way, as the five covers
directories were, passes it.

### The collision, again

The same three pairs, ten attempts each, on this branch's final code, with the
same shared `TMPDIR`s:

| binary, filter | attempts with a failure | copies that failed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `taiyaku-cli` unit tests, `serve_works_` | 0 of 10 | 0 of 20 |
| `taiyaku-serve`, `auth::tests::every_route_refuses_an_anonymous_request` | 0 of 10 | 0 of 20 |
| `taiyaku-read`, every test (70) | 0 of 10 | 0 of 20 |

No `taiyaku-test-*-{pid}-{n}` directory was left under any of the three
`TMPDIR`s afterwards. The seventeen entries still there were the fixed names
the first runs left.

### The tests, watched red

Each change was applied by a script that counted its substitution's matches,
one for each, ran `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
--no-fail-fast`, and put the file back byte for byte. After the last,
`git diff -- crates` hashed the same as before the first. The control passed
2158 of 2158.

| applied | tests failed | which |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing — the control | 0 | — |
| a fixed name, `taiyaku-test-{label}` | 284: 174 in `taiyaku-library`, 95 in `taiyaku-serve`, 10 in `taiyaku-cli`, 5 in `taiyaku-read` | `two_temp_dirs_under_one_label_are_distinct_and_both_exist` and `a_temp_dir_is_named_for_the_process_that_made_it` among them |
| no counter, `taiyaku-test-{label}-{pid}` | 16 | `two_temp_dirs_under_one_label_are_distinct_and_both_exist`, both paths `…/taiyaku-test-same-label-3662067`, among them |
| no process id, `taiyaku-test-{label}-{n}` | 253: 170 in `taiyaku-library`, 79 in `taiyaku-serve`, 4 in `taiyaku-read` | `a_temp_dir_is_named_for_the_process_that_made_it` among them |
| an empty `Drop` | 3 | `a_temp_dir_is_removed_with_its_contents_when_dropped`, and `taiyaku-serve`'s `tests::a_fixture_removes_its_directory_when_it_is_dropped` and `tests::a_fixture_removes_its_directory_when_the_scope_unwinds`, which test `Fixture` and so this type now |
| no removal before creating | 0 | — |
| the `/` assert deleted | 1 | `a_label_holding_a_slash_is_refused`: "test did not panic as expected" |
| a function returning `std::env::temp_dir().join("taiyaku-test-o117-mutant")` appended to `taiyaku-serve/src/routes/tests.rs` | 1 | `nothing_outside_this_helper_calls_temp_dir`, naming `taiyaku-serve/src/routes/tests.rs:3599` |
| the walk never descending, `pending.push(path)` as `drop(path)` | 1 | `nothing_outside_this_helper_calls_temp_dir`: "the walk read 0 files under …/crates" |

The fixed name and the missing process id fail far more than the helper's own
tests because `cargo nextest` runs every test in a process of its own, all at
once: with either part gone, tests that share a label collide inside one run,
which is O117 inside a single suite. The missing counter fails the tests that
make two directories under one label in one test — `tests/cli.rs`'s tree and
database, `routes::tests`' state and request log, and `duplicates::tests`'
copies of one tag among them.

**The removal before creating survived**, as expected. It matters only when a
process id is reused after a run was killed before its `Drop`, which no test
arranges, and a test cannot know the name the next `TempDir` will take: the
counter is shared by every test in its process. It is recorded rather than
pinned. `.cargo/mutants.toml` excludes `**/test_support.rs`, so cargo-mutants
never mutates this helper, and these hand mutations are all that has.

### What remains

- The removal of a stale directory before creating one is unpinned (above).
- The standing check sees the text `temp_dir()` and nothing else. A fixed name
  built another way — beside a guard with `with_file_name`, as the five covers
  directories were, or from `TMPDIR` read by hand — passes it.
- cargo-mutants excludes the helper's file.

## O119: the OPDS feeds ask a grant on the blocking pool — 2026-09-15

O115's branch measured, beside its own row, that OPDS's `works` and
`work_feed` stalled the runtime for a reader granted root 1 and not for an
empty grant ("O115", "Found beside it, not changed"), and did not file it. The
user chose on 2026-09-15 to file and fix it on one branch, so O119 opens and
closes here. The branch is based on O115's (`67f2f5b`), whose
`routes::on_the_grant` the fix reuses.

### What asks the library on the async worker, read

A script over `crates/taiyaku-serve/src/`, test files and `test_support.rs`
excluded, blanked comments and string literals, located the parentheses of
every `spawn_blocking(` call, and listed every `library.…()` call and `.roots`
read outside them. Each was read by hand, and so was each call site of the
synchronous functions among them.

| where | what it does | where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opds::works`, through `opds::visible_editions_by_work` | `state.library.conn()`, then `browse::visible_editions` | **the async worker**: this item |
| `opds::work_feed` | `state.library.conn()`, then `browse::work` | **the async worker**: this item |
| `library_api.rs`'s `home`, `series`, `one_series`, `work`, `search`, `cover` and `status` | `state.library.conn()` for every request | the async worker, whatever the grant: O116 |
| `routes::refuse_if_hidden`, `visible_editions_or_refuse` and `visible_editions_for_a_correction` | the grant, through `routes::on_the_grant` | the blocking pool, since O115 |
| `auth::resolve`, through `session::from_cookie` and `auth::from_basic` | the session or credential, and the account's roots | inside `auth::guard`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `download::prepare` | the edition's members | inside `download::edition`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `notes`, `truth` and `progress`: `load` and `store` | a reader's documents | inside the `routes.rs` handlers' `spawn_blocking`, all eight calls |
| the `config_api`, `curation`, `metadata`, `session`, `stamp` and `users_api` handlers | their store work | inside each handler's `spawn_blocking` |
| `routes::list_works` | copies `principal.roots` on the async worker and queries inside `spawn_blocking` | no library on the async worker |
| `serve`, in `lib.rs` | `is_claimed` twice, and the two sweeps | once, before the listener binds |
| `works::from_library` | projects the library's works | at startup, from `taiyaku-cli`'s `serve`, and in tests |
| `config_api::run_scan_inner` | `library.working()`, a second connection rather than the mutex | a background scan |
| `backup_api::directory` | `library.path()`, which takes no lock | — |
| `users_api::user_patch_from_json` | `patch.roots`, a field of the request body | no library |

Nothing but the two feeds and O116's handlers takes the library's mutex on the
async worker. *(O116 has since closed, on 2026-09-15 — see "O116".)*

### The fix

- `opds::visible_editions_by_work` is `async` and asks through
  `routes::on_the_grant`. No principal, or an empty grant, answers `None`
  without the library, as before; a grant that names roots runs
  `browse::visible_editions` on the blocking pool, and a failed query is the
  same 500.
- `opds::work_feed` asks `routes::visible_editions_or_refuse`, the question
  `get_sidecar` asks: `browse::work` on the blocking pool for a grant that
  names roots, `` no work `{id}` `` with 404 for a work outside it, as `missing`
  sent, and the same 500. It still asks after the unknown work's 404 and
  before the feed is built.
- `routes::on_the_grant` and `routes::visible_editions_or_refuse` are
  `pub(crate)`, and so are `opds::works` and `opds::work_feed`, for the test.

**After the check, neither feed takes the library.** `works` walks
`state.works` and reads each sidecar. `work_feed` reads its sidecar and,
through `download::advertised_type`, asks the filesystem whether a one-member
edition's file exists: a `stat` on the async worker, not the library's mutex,
and unchanged here.

Neither feed answers a conditional request, so there is no 304 for the check to
come before. The order that could change is the unknown work's 404 against the
grant's, and it is the same.

### The test, red on O115's branch

`routes::tests::neither_opds_feed_asks_a_grant_on_the_async_worker` calls
`opds::works` and `opds::work_feed` directly under
`test_support::the_runtime_stalls_on`, over
`test_support::state_whose_grant_waits_on_the_library`, as a reader granted
root 1 and then with an empty grant. It asserts every call answered 200 and
collects the calls that stalled.

With only the test and `pub(crate)` on the two feeds added to `67f2f5b`:

```
these asked the library on the async worker: ["opds::works, granted root 1", "opds::work_feed, granted root 1"]
```

It failed at its last assertion, so all four calls had answered 200, and
neither feed stalled with an empty grant.

### Watched red

A script applied each change to the final `opds.rs`, ran `cargo nextest run
--workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`, and wrote the file back from its
saved bytes, comparing sha256. The two "on the async worker" changes put back
the base's own code, whose guard is dropped before any `.await`, so both
compiled. The control passed 2157, with 4 skipped.

| applied to the final code | failed | at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing, the control | nothing | 2157 passed |
| `visible_editions_by_work` asking on the async worker | `routes::tests::neither_opds_feed_asks_a_grant_on_the_async_worker` | `routes/tests.rs:1023`: `["opds::works, granted root 1"]` |
| `work_feed` asking on the async worker | the same test | `routes/tests.rs:1023`: `["opds::work_feed, granted root 1"]` |
| `visible_editions_by_work` answering `None` for every caller | `auth::tests::every_route_declares_its_grant_posture`, `opds::tests::a_restricted_readers_works_list_counts_only_the_editions_they_may_see` and `opds::tests::the_works_feed_does_not_name_a_work_outside_the_grant` | `auth/tests.rs:1865`, `opds/tests.rs:1422` and `:1472` |
| `work_feed` asking no grant | `auth::tests::every_route_declares_its_grant_posture`, `opds::tests::a_restricted_readers_work_feed_lists_only_the_editions_they_may_see` and `opds::tests::a_restricted_readers_work_feed_404s_when_no_edition_is_visible` | `auth/tests.rs:2145`, `opds/tests.rs:1394`, and `:1447` with 200 for 404 |

The last two rows are about the rewrite rather than the stall: each feed's
filter is still held by tests that existed before it.

### Flake runs

The new test alone, 20 times through `cargo nextest run -p taiyaku-serve`: 20
passed, each in 0.054–0.058 s. The one-minute load average read 22.80 before
the first run, and 21.29 before the sixth, the eleventh and the sixteenth and
after the last.

### What remains

- The watchdog sees a call's first wait on the library's mutex, as O115
  recorded, so a second wait added on the async worker after either feed's
  check would pass.
- `library_api.rs`'s seven handlers take the library's mutex on the async
  worker for every request: O116, unchanged here. *(Closed 2026-09-15 — see
  "O116".)*
- `work_feed`'s `advertised_type` asks the filesystem about a one-member
  edition on the async worker. It is not the library's mutex, and it was not
  measured.

## O116: the browse handlers read the library on the blocking pool — 2026-09-15

O116 recorded that `library_api.rs`'s seven handlers take `state.library.conn()`
in their own bodies, on the async worker, read and not measured, and that it
waited on a measurement: O71's watchdog for whether each stalls, and O42's for
how long it matters. O115's branch had already measured one, `work`, stalling
for a reader granted root 1 and for an empty grant ("O115", "Found beside it,
not changed").

This branch takes the first measurement for all seven and not the second. A
handler that waits on the mutex on the async worker holds that thread for as
long as the wait lasts, however long that is, and O115 and O119 moved the same
wait off it in ten handlers without timing it either.

### What takes the library on the async worker, on `main`

O119's table ("O119") was read on O115's branch (`67f2f5b`), not on `main` as
it stands, so it was not reused. A script over `crates/taiyaku-serve/src/` at
`a57fde4`, read through `git show` with test files and `test_support.rs`
excluded, blanked comments and string literals, found the parentheses of every
`spawn_blocking(` call, and listed every `.conn()` and `.working()` on a
library outside them: 28 of 79. A second script placed every call of the
synchronous functions among them the same way. What neither script settled was
read by hand: `run_scan`'s call, inside the scan route's `spawn_blocking`;
`serve`'s four calls, before the listener binds; and `taiyaku-cli`'s
`serve_works`, which calls `works::from_library` before the server starts. A
grep for `.conn()` and `.working()` on a line without `library` found one more,
`backup_api::create_backup`'s `.working()` on a line of its own, inside a
`spawn_blocking` and among the 79.

| where | calls | where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `library_api.rs`'s `home`, `series`, `one_series`, `work`, `search`, `cover` and `status` | 7 | **the async worker, whatever the grant**: this item |
| `auth::from_basic` | 6 | `auth::resolve`, inside `auth::guard`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `session::from_cookie` | 1 | the same |
| `download::prepare` | 2 | inside `download::edition`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `notes`, `progress` and `truth`: `load` and `store` | 6 | inside the `routes.rs` handlers' `spawn_blocking`, all eight calls |
| `serve`, in `lib.rs` | 4 | once, before the listener binds |
| `config_api::run_scan_inner` | 1 | `library.working()`, a second connection rather than the mutex, reached through `run_scan` inside the scan route's `spawn_blocking` |
| `works::from_library` | 1 | at startup, from `taiyaku-cli`'s `serve_works` |

Nothing but the seven browse handlers takes the library's mutex on the async
worker.

### The fix

Each handler's body moves, unchanged apart from taking `conn` as an argument,
into a closure passed to `library_api::on_the_library`, which runs it on the
blocking pool over `state.library.conn()` and awaits the response it builds. A
panic in it is a 500 through the module's own `failed`, naming what was being
read.

`series` and `one_series` each ask two questions, and ask both in the one trip,
on one connection. `cover` built its redirect after `drop(conn)`; it now builds
it inside the trip, so the mutex is held for that `format!` as well. Every
other handler already built its response while it held the connection, and
still does.

### The test, red on `main`

`library_api::tests::no_browse_route_stalls_the_runtime` calls all seven
handlers directly under `test_support::the_runtime_stalls_on`, as a reader
granted root 1 and then with an empty grant. It asserts each call answers as it
does for a reader who can see the series, 307 from `cover` and 200 from the
rest, and collects the calls that stalled.

- **Both grants, because neither is spared.** `routes::on_the_grant` answers an
  empty grant without the library, but `browse` applies a grant in SQL, so
  these handlers read the library whatever the caller holds.
- **`test_support::router_over_a_scanned_work_in_a_series`, not O115's
  fixture.** `state_whose_grant_waits_on_the_library`'s work belongs to no
  series, so `one_series` and `cover` would answer 404 over it. The test
  inserts root 1 and moves every member under it, because a scanned member's
  `root_id` is NULL here too, and no grant admits one.

With only the test added to `a57fde4`, it failed at its last assertion, so all
fourteen calls had answered as asserted:

```
these took the library on the async worker: ["library_api::home, granted root 1", "library_api::series, granted root 1", "library_api::one_series, granted root 1", "library_api::work, granted root 1", "library_api::search, granted root 1", "library_api::cover, granted root 1", "library_api::status, granted root 1", "library_api::home, an empty grant", "library_api::series, an empty grant", "library_api::one_series, an empty grant", "library_api::work, an empty grant", "library_api::search, an empty grant", "library_api::cover, an empty grant", "library_api::status, an empty grant"]
```

### Watched red

A script applied each change to the final code, ran `cargo nextest run
--workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` with `TAIYAKU_CORPUS` unset, and
wrote the file back from a saved copy, comparing sha256; every copy matched.
Each "on the async worker" change pointed one handler's call at a copy of
`on_the_library` that calls `read` without `spawn_blocking`, appended to
`library_api.rs` for that run only. Every run compiled. The control passed
2170, with 4 skipped, and each red run 2169.

| applied to the final code | failed | naming |
| --- | --- | --- |
| nothing, the control | nothing | — |
| `home` on the async worker | `library_api::tests::no_browse_route_stalls_the_runtime` | `["library_api::home, granted root 1", "library_api::home, an empty grant"]` |
| `series` on the async worker | the same test | `series`, both grants |
| `one_series` on the async worker | the same test | `one_series`, both grants |
| `work` on the async worker | the same test | `work`, both grants |
| `search` on the async worker | the same test | `search`, both grants |
| `cover` on the async worker | the same test | `cover`, both grants |
| `status` on the async worker | the same test | `status`, both grants |
| `on_the_library` calling `read` without `spawn_blocking` | the same test | all fourteen calls |
| the test's `UPDATE member SET root_id = 1` removed | the same test | `library_api::one_series, granted root 1: no series 1`, 404 for 200 |

### Flake runs

The new test alone, 20 times through `cargo nextest run -p taiyaku-serve`: 20
passed, each in 0.161–0.164 s. The one-minute load average read 9.81 before
the first and the sixth run, and 9.27 before the eleventh and the sixteenth and
after the last.

### The mutation sweep

`scripts/mutants.sh --since main` on `081cd83`: 8 mutants, 8 caught, none
unviable or timed out. Each replaced one handler or `on_the_library` with
`Default::default()`. It generates no mutant that moves a read back onto the
async worker, which is what the changes applied by hand above are for.

### What remains

- The watchdog holds the library's mutex once and lets it go when the canary
  runs, so it measures a call's first wait on that mutex, as O115 recorded. A
  handler that went back to the library on the async worker after its trip
  would pass. None of the seven does: each returns what its trip built.
- No test reaches `on_the_library`'s panic arm.
- O42's one connection behind one mutex is unchanged. A browse request still
  waits for it, on a blocking thread rather than on the async worker.
- `opds::work_feed`'s `download::advertised_type` asks the filesystem on the
  async worker ("O119", "What remains"). It is not the library's mutex, and it
  is not changed here.

### Counts

Rust 2169 → 2170: one new test, in `library_api/tests.rs`, counted by the
control run above. `web/` was not changed.

## O77: a test that names the guard — 2026-09-15

O77 recorded that `&&` → `||` in `derive::unattached_chapter_dirs`'s guard
passed the `taiyaku-library` suite. "O77 and O51" above found it caught on
2026-09-14, by `preview::tests::a_preview_and_a_real_save_produce_the_same_structure`
alone, a test that pins a preview against a real save and does not name the
guard.

### Before the test, on `eeff032`

The substitution was applied by hand in place (one match), then
`cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`, then `git
checkout` of the file and an empty `git diff`:

- 2170 tests ran: 2169 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped.
- The one failure is the preview test, at its literal `Impact`:
  `proposals_raised: 1` against `0`.

The incidental catch holds across the whole workspace, not only the crate, and
nothing else sees the guard.

### The test

`derive::tests::only_a_directory_resolving_a_chapter_and_no_volume_is_asked_about`
calls `unattached_chapter_dirs` itself. `report.unattached_chapter_dirs` cannot
stand in for it: that count is `classify`'s `chapter_dirs`, collected under the
same condition written a second time. The fixture is five directories under one
root, one per side of each half of `volume.is_none() && chapter.is_some()`, with

## O33: two fixtures that reach the two block constants — 2026-09-15

O33 recorded that `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` and `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` reject nothing
in any test: every page `detect/tests.rs` refused was refused before either
filter, and every block it kept sat far inside both. The corpus half was
answered before ("`MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` fires twice in 90 pages.
`MAX_BLOCK_AREA` fires on 89 of 90"); this branch closes the test half. No
production code changes.

### The two fixtures

`a_block_shorter_than_two_stroke_scales_is_not_a_region` draws six bars 40px
long and 4 or 5px thick on a 15px pitch, on a 400×600 page. Every bar's longer
side is 40, so `stroke_scale` is 40 and the filter asks for 80; the block is 79
or 80 long and 40 across. It draws the pair stacked and turned, so a filter
reading `width()` or `height()` in place of `longer()` fails one orientation
each.

`a_block_over_the_area_ceiling_is_not_a_region` draws five bars 100×39 on a
pitch of 141 or 140, on a 400×1000 page: one vertical block, 100×603 (0.15075
of the page) or 100×599 (0.14975).

Each test first asserts that the band keeps every bar and the scale is the one
above ("fixture must bite"), then that the refused page is empty and the kept
page is one region at the bars' own size. Every other filter has room on both
pages, computed from the fixtures:

| filter | span pair, 79 / 80 | area pair, 603 / 599 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BAND` (`lo` 64, `hi` 2000), a bar in ‱ of page height | 666 | 1,000 |
| `MIN_STROKES` (4) | 6 | 5 |
| `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` (2 × scale) | 79 / 80 against 80 | 603 / 599 against 200 |
| `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` (0.15) | 0.0132 / 0.0133 | 0.15075 / 0.14975 |
| `MIN_INK` (0.05) | 0.304 / 0.375 | 0.323 / 0.326 |

### Hand mutations

A script applied each change to `detect.rs` in place, ran
`cargo nextest run -p taiyaku-cli --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/detect::tests::/)'`,
and restored the file; a control ran first in each of the two batches (39
passed, both times), and `detect.rs` matched `main` after each batch. "Span"
is the new span test, "area" the new area test; messages as printed.

| mutation | fails | message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` 2 → 8 (×4) | span, area, and 2 others | `80px against a span of 80, turned=false: got []`; area: `100x599 is 0.14975 of the page, against 0.15: got []` |
| `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` 2 → 4 (×2) | span | `80px against a span of 80, turned=false: got []` |
| `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` 2 → 1 (÷2) | span | `79px against a span of 80, turned=false: got [Region { x: 0.25, y: 0.3333333333333333, w: 0.1, h: 0.13166666666666665, axis: Vertical }]` |
| `MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` 2 → 0 (÷4) | span | the same 79px message |
| span `>=` → `>` | span | `80px against a span of 80, turned=false: got []` |
| span `>=` → `<` | span, area, and 9 others | the 79px message; area: the 599 message |
| span `longer()` → `width()` | span, area, and 8 others | `80px against a span of 80, turned=false: got []` |
| span `longer()` → `height()` | span, `a_column_beside_a_row_keeps_both_axes` | `80px against a span of 80, turned=true: got []` |
| span filter removed | span only | the 79px message |
| span `scale * MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` → `gap` | **SURVIVED** | equivalent; see below |
| `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` 0.15 → 0.6 (×4) | area | `100x603 is 0.15075 of the page, against 0.15: got [Region { x: 0.375, y: 0.2, w: 0.25, h: 0.603, axis: Vertical }]` |
| `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` 0.15 → 0.3 (×2) | area | the same 603 message |
| `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` 0.15 → 0.075 (÷2) | area | `100x599 is 0.14975 of the page, against 0.15: got []` |
| `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` 0.15 → 0.0375 (÷4) | area, `a_block_of_hollow_strokes_is_mostly_paper` | the 599 message |
| area `<=` → `<` | **SURVIVED** | unreachable; see below |
| area `<=` → `>=` | area, span, and 9 others | the 603 message |
| area `w × h` → `w × w` | area | the 603 message |
| area `w × h` → `h × h` | area, `a_block_of_hollow_strokes_is_mostly_paper` | the 599 message |
| area in pixels, not a fraction of the page | area, span, and 9 others | the 599 message |
| page area as `width × width` | area | the 599 message |
| area filter removed | area only | the 603 message |

The rows below tighten an *earlier* filter past each fixture's margin, to show
the fixtures depend on passing it rather than on it being loose:

| mutation | fails | message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BAND.lo` 64 → 700 | span, and 8 others | `fixture must bite: all six bars must pass the band and set the scale, turned=false` — the area test passes, its bars being 1,000‱ |
| `BAND.lo` 64 → 1100 | span, area, and 9 others | area: `fixture must bite: all five bars must pass the band and set the scale` |
| `MIN_STROKES` 4 → 7 | span, area, and 7 others | the kept pages come back empty: `80px … got []`, `100x599 … got []` |
| `MIN_INK` 0.05 → 0.35 | area only | `100x599 is 0.14975 of the page, against 0.15: got []` — the span pair's kept page scores 0.375 |
| `MIN_INK` 0.05 → 0.38 | span, area | `80px against a span of 80, turned=false: got []` |
| `SMEAR_K` 2 → 1 | area; `a_field_of_screentone_is_not_a_region` and `glyphs_survive_a_screentone_background` timed out at 60 s | `100x599 is 0.14975 of the page, against 0.15: got []` — at a gap of 100 the area pair's 101px spaces no longer merge, so each bar is a block of one stroke and `MIN_STROKES` empties both pages; the kept page is what fails. The span test passes: its 11px spaces still merge at a gap of 40 |

### The two that survive

**The area filter's `<=` as `<`.** The filter compares
`area / page_area <= f64::from(MAX_BLOCK_AREA)`, and `f64::from(0.15f32)` is
0.15000000596046448, which is exactly 5,033,165 / 2²⁵. A block sitting on the
limit needs `area / page_area` to equal that, and 5,033,165 is odd, so the page
must be a multiple of 2²⁵ pixels — 33.5 million — before any block can land on
it. A page of that size is not a unit test, and on every page smaller the two
comparisons agree.

**The span filter's `scale * MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN` as the smear `gap`.**
`gap` is `(scale * SMEAR_K).max(1)`, `SMEAR_K` is 2 like
`MIN_BLOCK_STROKE_SPAN`, and `scale` is at least 1, so the two expressions are
the same number on every page. No test can tell them apart while both
constants are 2.

### Counts

Rust 2170 → 2172: two new tests in `detect/tests.rs`, counted by the gate's
`status-test-count` check. `web/` was not changed.

### What remains

- O32 is untouched. `MAX_BLOCK_AREA` still clamps every surviving region under
  0.15 before `median_area` is taken, and the fix its entry names is unwritten.
- `region_experiment.rs`'s comment above its filter tally still says O32 and
  O33 record two constants rejecting nothing in any test. It is test-gated code
  outside `detect/tests.rs`, and this branch changes nothing else, so it is
  left as written.

## O120: the work feed types its editions on the blocking pool — 2026-09-15

O119 ("What remains") recorded that `opds::work_feed`'s
`download::advertised_type` asks the filesystem on the async worker, that it is
not the library's mutex, and that it was not measured. O116 ("What remains")
recorded it again, and neither changed it. The user chose on 2026-09-15 to file
and fix it on one branch, so O120 opens and closes here, on `main` at `eeff032`.

### What the handler does on the async worker, read

Every step of `work_feed`'s body on `eeff032`, in order:

| step | what it does | on the async worker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state.work_or_missing` | searches `state.works`, in memory | nothing waits |
| `extensions.get::<Principal>()` | reads a request extension | nothing waits |
| `routes::visible_editions_or_refuse` | the grant, through `routes::on_the_grant` | nothing since O119: a grant that names roots is asked on the blocking pool, an empty or absent one without the library |
| `work.sidecar()` | clones an `Arc` under `Work`'s `std::sync::RwLock`, for reading | **waits while a writer holds that lock**: not changed here, see below |
| `download::advertised_type`, for each edition the feed names, for a reader who may download | `download::passthrough_extension`: `is_file()` on the member of an edition of one member, and nothing for an edition of several, which stops at the count | **a `stat`**: this item |
| escaping, `writeln!`, the response | memory | nothing waits |

**The sidecar lock is not the same defect, and it is not this handler's
alone.** `Work::update` holds the lock for writing across its closure, and its
one caller outside tests, `patch_alignments`, writes the sidecar inside that
closure with `taiyaku_read::atomic::write`, synced since O104, when the work has
one, and then its rows through `alignments::store`. A `work.sidecar()` on the
async worker waits that long, and only while a correction to the same work is
being written. The same read is on the async worker in `opds::works`,
`routes::get_sidecar`, and `routes::locate_member`, which `routes::get_page` and
`opds::stream_page` call in the handler: five handlers with this one. Moving
this handler's read would leave four, and none of the five is a `stat`, so all
five are left and recorded here. *(Counted again from the code on 2026-09-15,
while filing O122, and the count here is wrong rather than stale:
`routes::get_page` calls `locate_member` **inside** its own `spawn_blocking`
(opened at `routes.rs:878`, the call at `:886`), so it never took this read on
the async worker. The set is four — `opds::works`, `opds::work_feed`,
`routes::get_sidecar` and `opds::stream_page`. Marked here rather than
rewritten.)*

### Every filesystem call in `taiyaku-serve`, placed

A script over `crates/taiyaku-serve/src/`, with `tests.rs`, `tests/` and
`test_support.rs` left out, blanked comments, string and character literals,
then listed every `is_file`, `is_dir`, `exists`, `metadata`, `read_dir`,
`File::open`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions`, `std::fs::`, `canonicalize`,
`write_all`, `flush`, `sync_all` and `atomic::write`, with the function around
each and whether it sat inside a `spawn_blocking(` call's parentheses. The
callers of each synchronous function among them were listed the same way and
read by hand. `corpus.rs` is `#[cfg(test)]` and is left out.

| where | call | where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download::passthrough_extension` | `is_file()` | from `advertised_type`: **the async worker** on `eeff032`, which is this item, and the blocking pool since; and from `download::prepare`, inside `download::edition`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `download::prepare` | `metadata` | inside `download::edition`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `download::prepare_member` | `is_dir()`, `metadata` | inside `download::member`'s `spawn_blocking` |
| `download::passthrough` | `File::open` | on the thread each download route starts for its body: `produce`'s in `edition`, and `member`'s own |
| `cover::cached_or_generated_page`, `cover::cached`, `cover::at_path` | `create_dir_all`, `read`, `atomic::write` | inside the `spawn_blocking` of `routes::get_page`, `routes::get_thumb` and `opds::cover` |
| `backup_api::download_backup` | `read` | inside its `spawn_blocking` |
| `routes::patch_alignments` | `atomic::write` | inside its `spawn_blocking` |
| `stump::cache::load`, `stump::cache::store`, `stump::resolve::resolve_member` | `read_to_string`, `write`, `rename`, `metadata` | from `stump::resolve::resolve_work`, inside `serve`'s `spawn_blocking`, after the listener binds |
| `stump::cache::forget` | `remove_file` | from `forget_all_works`, in `serve` before the listener binds, only for `--refresh-stump` |
| `cache_root::create` | `create_dir_all` | in `serve`, before the listener binds |
| `reqlog::Log::new` | `OpenOptions::open` | in `serve`, before the listener binds |
| `reqlog::Log::finish` | `write_all`, to a `File` held in a `std::sync::Mutex` | **the async worker**: `build_router`'s request-log middleware calls it after `next.run(request).await`, once per request while `--log-requests` is on |
| `works::load_works` | `read_to_string` | only from tests |

So one call besides this item runs on the async worker, for every request:
`reqlog::Log::finish`'s write, to an unbuffered file, while the request log is
on. It is not changed or filed here. **What this cannot see**: a call into
another crate that reaches the disk — `taiyaku_read` opening an archive,
`taiyaku_library` reading the library — is none of the tokens above. Those
reads are what O12, O71, O115, O116 and O119 placed.

### The fix

- `opds::advertised_types` answers, for each edition the grant admits, what
  `download::advertised_type` answers, in one `spawn_blocking` over the sidecar
  snapshot `work_feed` builds its entries from. It answers a panic with a 500,
  `typing the editions panicked: …`, and a work `id` does not name with the 404
  `missing` sends, which the handler has already sent before asking.
- `work_feed` asks it only for a reader who may download, and its loop reads
  the answer for each edition. A key with no answer would be declared
  `CBZ_TYPE`, `advertised_type`'s own answer for a file it cannot find; the loop
  names no edition that was not asked about.
- `download::advertised_type`'s doc now says it blocks and who asks it, and
  that its `metadata` call is for an edition of one member.

### The test

`test_support::the_runtime_stalls_on` sees a handler that waits on the
library's mutex. A `stat` does not, and one of a file on a local disk answers
before a watchdog could notice, so no test in the crate could tell where it ran:
the feed is the same XML either way. A `stat` could be made to wait with a
filesystem that stalls under the fixture, or with a seam in
`passthrough_extension` for a test to hold, and neither was needed: the kernel
records which thread made each call.

`opds::tests::the_work_feed_stats_its_members_on_the_blocking_pool` runs itself
again as a child under `strace -f -qq -y -e trace=%%stat`, as O104's tests run
under `strace` for their syncs. The runner is
`taiyaku_read::test_support::strace`, split out of `traced`, which now calls it.
The child builds a current-thread runtime whose `on_thread_start` writes down
the id of every thread it starts, which in a current-thread runtime is its
blocking pool, and calls `work_feed` through `block_on` from a thread whose id
it also writes down: the runtime's async worker. Each id is the kernel's thread
id, read from `/proc/thread-self`, which is the number `strace -f` prints at the
head of each line. The work has two editions of one member each,
`raw` a `.pdf` and `en` an `.epub`, and the child requires each entry's
acquisition link to declare its own edition's type. The parent requires each
member's path in at least one `stat`-family call, so a log that matches nothing
fails, and every such call made by a thread the runtime started.

### Red

Each change was applied to the final code by a script that checked the change
was in the file, ran `taiyaku-serve`'s tests, restored the file and compared it
with a copy taken before the first. The control, run through the same script
with nothing applied, passed 586 of 586.

| change | failed | message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `work_feed` as on `eeff032`: no trip, `advertised_type` called in the loop | the new test alone, 585 passing | `…/work/volume.pdf was statted by thread(s) ["2301903"], which the runtime did not start: the async worker is 2301903 and the blocking pool is []` |
| `advertised_types` calling its closure in place of `spawn_blocking` | the new test alone, 585 passing | the same, with thread `2311209` both the one that statted and the async worker, and an empty blocking pool |
| the loop declaring `CBZ_TYPE` for every edition, its answers unread | the new test alone, 585 passing | the child's `` `raw`'s acquisition link must declare application/pdf `` |
| `advertised_types` typing every edition as the sidecar's first, `en` | the new test alone, 585 passing | the child's `` `raw`'s acquisition link must declare application/pdf `` |

No other test in the crate saw any of the four. The feed's acquisition-type
test uses an edition of two members, which is never statted, and
`download::tests` call `advertised_type` itself rather than the feed.

Run alone 20 times at a one-minute load average of 15.37–15.58, the new test
passed 20 times.

### What remains

- `work.sidecar()` waits on `Work`'s lock on the async worker in five handlers,
  while a correction to that work is written. *(Four, not five — see O122 and the
  marker above.)*
- `reqlog::Log::finish` writes each request's line on the async worker while the
  request log is on.
- No test reaches `advertised_types`' panic arm or its 404, sees that an edition
  outside the grant is not statted, or sees that a reader who may not download
  makes no trip.
- Nothing here was timed, on this workstation or on the NAS.

### Counts

Rust 2170 → 2171: one new test, in `opds/tests.rs`. `web/` was not changed.

## O72 fix round — 2026-09-15

An independent review of `4404d2d` found no blocking defect and seven things
to address. They land as a second commit on the same branch.

### 1. A decided row's controls were pinned on the line's direct children only

The per-state test read `.row > button`. The reviewer's W5, an Undo calling
`unacceptProposal` inside an accepted row's opened panel, and W5b, the same
Undo on the line inside a `<span>`, both passed all 59 `ProposalRow` and
`Proposals` tests. The new `ProposalRow` test mounts an accepted and a
dismissed row, each collapsed and then opened with the panel loaded (`rule:
null`, as the server sends for any proposal not open). It asserts every
`button` and `[role="button"]` in the row as one list, then presses every
enabled one and asserts `unacceptProposal`, `acceptProposal` and
`dismissProposal` were never called.

### 2. Releasing the write guard after a success was unpinned

The reviewer's W2 deleted `inFlight.current = false` from the success path and
passed: the success tests read `disabled`, which comes from `writing`, and
never pressed again. The new test keeps both rows mounted, as a failed reload
would, and presses Dismiss twice and Reopen twice, asserting two requests
each.

### 3. The header paired one state's count with another state's name

`Proposals.tsx` drew `{total} {state}` from the pressed control while `total`
still came from the previous answer: "37 open", press Dismissed, and "37
dismissed" over the open rows until the dismissed list landed. The empty state
chose its words the same way. The inbox, its counts and the state they were
fetched for are now one piece of state, and the header and the empty state
read that state. Emptying the list on every switch was not chosen: it blanks
the screen each time, and its header would still need a word for "nothing
loaded". The new test holds the second and third responses open and asserts
the header and the empty state inside each window, in both directions.

### 4. A refusal could describe a row another process had changed

`reopen` ran its conditional `UPDATE` and then read the row to word the
refusal, as two statements. A row dismissed by another process between them
read "is `dismissed`, not dismissed", and a row deleted between them made
`one`'s `Err` a 500.

Both writes now run in one transaction. `rusqlite` 0.38's
`unchecked_transaction` is `Transaction::new_unchecked(self,
self.transaction_behavior)` (read in the crate source), and
`Library::configure`, which `open_in_memory` also calls, sets `Immediate`. So
the write lock is taken at `BEGIN` and held to the commit, and the read sees the
row the `UPDATE` missed. The `(dismissed, no rule)` arm of `reopen`'s refusal
and the `(not accepted, no rule)` arm of `dismiss`'s cannot be reached while
that lock is held. Both are worded anyway, and neither is tested.

A missing row is a 404 through `curation::failed_unless_gone`: after a write's
store `Err`, it asks `proposals::lookup` again, and only a row that is gone
turns the 500 into a 404. `dismiss` and `reopen` use it; `accept` and
`unaccept` have the same gap behind `present` and do not.

**No test reaches the race itself.** SQLite has no hook between `present`'s
`SELECT` and the store's `BEGIN`, and a trigger that deleted the row during the
store's own `UPDATE` is rolled back with the transaction the `Err` abandons.
The mapping is tested directly, with a row that is gone and one that is not.
Pointing both handlers back at `NoAnswer::Failed` survived.

### 5. `dismiss` read, then wrote unconditionally — this predates O72

`dismiss` read the state, refused `accepted`, and then ran `UPDATE proposal SET
state = ?1 WHERE id = ?2` with no condition. That shape is on `main` at
`eeff032` and came in with `cec59e2`, the library scanner (#77, 2026-08-18),
per `git log -S` on the statement. An accept committing between the read and
the write left a `dismissed` row holding a live `created_rule_id`. Reopening
made that worse: `reopen`'s `WHERE state = 'dismissed'` would make the row
`open` with its rule in force, and `acceptable`, which checks the state alone,
lets it be accepted again beside that rule.

- `reopen`'s `UPDATE` adds `AND created_rule_id IS NULL`, and its refusal for
  a dismissed row holding a rule names `unaccept`, which removes the rule and
  reopens the proposal. The test takes that advice and checks the row is
  `open` with no rule anywhere.
- `dismiss` is `UPDATE … WHERE id = ?2 AND state <> 'accepted' AND
  created_rule_id IS NULL` in the same transaction shape, with its refusal
  worded from the read after it.
- **One refusal was false and is reworded.** An accepted proposal whose rule
  has gone was told "un-accept it first", and `unaccept` refuses a proposal
  with no rule. Both writes now say the next scan reopens it, and the test
  runs `raise` to show it does.
- `dismiss_refuses_an_accepted_proposal_rather_than_orphaning_its_rule`
  checked the refusal and that the rule survived. `dismiss` never deletes a
  rule, so a version that wrote `dismissed` over the accepted row and refused
  anyway passed it. It now also asserts the state and `created_rule_id`.

The rows the race leaves are built by hand in the tests. The race itself is
not staged, for the reason in 4.

### 6. The decided filters keep the score threshold — recorded, not changed

The Accepted and Dismissed filters keep the inbox's default threshold. A weak
decided proposal is therefore absent whenever a strong one is listed, and the
hint that Show weak proposals reveals more is drawn only over an empty list.
Added to the row's What remains.

### 7. Wording

`curation::reopen`'s doc sentence comparing the two `DELETE`s did not parse;
it now says the route is to `POST …/dismiss` what `DELETE …/accept` is to
`POST …/accept`. `status.md`'s `taiyaku-serve` paragraph said "those five"
handlers resolve the row through `proposals::lookup` and "all six" run on the
blocking pool. `rg 'present\(&conn'` finds six calls in `curation.rs` and
`rg spawn_blocking` seven handlers, and both sentences are marked in place.

### Watched red

Scripts as before. Each mutation was applied to the final code, run, and
written back from a saved copy, with sha256 matching every time. Rust ran with
`TAIYAKU_CORPUS` unset, filtered to one package's module: controls passed 98

--project jsdom --reporter=default` over `ProposalRow.test.tsx` and
`Proposals.test.tsx`: the control passed 62. W5, W5b and W2 are the reviewer's
own edits, read out of their `webmut.py`.

| applied | failed |
| --- | --- |
| W5: Undo calling `unacceptProposal` in an accepted row's opened panel | the decided-row test: `['disclosure', 'undo:Undo', …]` |
| W5b: Undo on an accepted row's line, inside a `<span>` | the decided-row test: `['disclosure', 'undo:Undo']` for `['disclosure']` |
| W2: `inFlight.current = false` removed from the success path | the second-press test: `[[5]]` for `[[5], [5]]` |
| the header reads the pressed state | the held-response test: `'2 dismissed'` for `'2 open'` |
| the empty state reads the pressed state | the held-response test: "Nothing to answer…" where "Nothing dismissed" was expected |
| `failed_unless_gone` answers a gone row with `Failed` | `a_write_error_for_a_proposal_that_has_gone_is_a_404_and_any_other_a_500` |

| `dismiss`'s `UPDATE` unconditional (`AND ?3 IS NOT NULL`) | four, `dismiss_refuses_an_accepted_proposal_rather_than_orphaning_its_rule` among them: `expected a refusal, got Ok(Made(()))` |
| `dismiss`'s state clause removed | `an_accepted_proposal_whose_rule_has_gone_is_refused_by_dismiss_and_reopen` |

### What remains

- `accept_with`'s own comment says `unchecked_transaction` "opens a *deferred*

## O76 and O121: a fold carries alignments, and places every slot by page — 2026-09-15

O76 recorded that `fold::DISCARDED` took an emptied work's `alignment` rows
whoever wrote them, so a person's correction went with a folded work, counted
as one more row beside a scanlation credit. The user chose to carry alignments
rather than refuse the fold: nothing undoes a correction short of making
another (`web/src/correction.ts`), so a refusal would leave a duplicate work
standing for good.

### The brief, and the premise that was false

The brief carried every alignment of the folded work onto the target,
rewriting `work_id`, `from_key` and `to_key` through `edition_map`, with the
runs following by `alignment_id`. It rested on one premise: a fold only goes
ahead between editions holding the same archives in the same order (absorb's
second refusal), so an alignment's slots mean the same pages on either side.

That is false, and the code says why in three places. `Edition::slots` builds
an edition's slots from its page count, its spread flags and its work's
reading direction. `derive` builds every edition with `spreads: Vec::new()`,
so a scan writes no spread flag; `taiyaku align` measures them from the images
(`spread_flags`) and a `taiyaku.json` import writes them. And a fold's twin is,
in the ordinary case, the edition the same scan has just built. So a slot past
a spread on the folded edition is a different page on the twin.

**The probe**, a scratch test appended to `fold/tests.rs`, run once and
reverted (`git diff --stat` empty afterwards): a folded edition holding a
spread at page 2, a twin holding none, one alignment whose first span is
`0-2R`. Read through `project::sidecar` and `route`:

| state | `runs_of` | `route` pages 0–5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| folded work, before the move | `Ok`, three runs | all six resolve |
| target, rows moved and keys rewritten | Err("the source edition has no slot `2R` in span `0-2R`") | `None` |
| target, the spread flag carried as well | `Ok`, the same three runs | all six resolve, the same |

**Across the corpus**, by `scratchpad/o76/corpus-emulation.py` — a
re-implementation of `runs_of`, not the Rust code, kept with its log and
re-run on 2026-09-15: all 22 alignments in the 12 `corpus/*/taiyaku.json` read as stored, 16
touch an edition holding a spread flag, and with both editions of each read as
holding none, 14 are unreadable — seven name a half, and seven straddle a
spread and pair unequal counts (`gotoubun-v03`: `2-20` is 19 slots against
`1-18`'s 18).

The branch stopped there and reported it. The user's decision: carry the spread
flags. And a suspected defect on `main` was to be measured first, because the
fold already carried `progress.slot` and `note.slot` as numbers.

### O121, on `main`

`fold::tests::a_carried_position_and_note_name_the_page_they_named_before_the_fold`
was written against unchanged `fold.rs`: a folded edition `colour` spreading
page 2 (slots `0, 1, 2R, 2L, 3, 4, 5`), a place on slot 5 (page 4) and a note on
slot 3 (the left half of page 2), folded onto a twin holding no flags.

```
assertion `left == right` failed: position slot 5 and note slot 3 on the target must name what they named on the folded work
  left: (Some(Slot { page: 5, half: None }), Some(Slot { page: 3, half: None }))
 right: (Some(Slot { page: 4, half: None }), Some(Slot { page: 2, half: Some(Left) }))
```

It reproduced over real archives too — the drive below, run with a release
binary built from `eeff032`.

### What the fold does now

`fold::plan_slots` decides everything addressed by slot before anything is
written, so every refusal is still a `SELECT`:

- **Spread flags.** A twin holding none takes the folded edition's. A twin
  holding a set keeps it. Two folded editions meeting on one twin that both
  hold flags, in different sets, give it neither. One holding none is
  unmeasured — a scan never writes a flag — and does not stop the other's
  being taken. *This bullet said "with different sets give it neither" until
  the review of the first commit, which found the code did not treat an
  edition holding none as a set; the code's rule was kept, and the words now
  say it.*
- **Places and notes, on both works.** Every slot moves as the page and half it
  named. A half is a side of the scan, so this holds across reading directions:
  a left half stays a left half and takes the slot number that sits there. The
  twin's own rows were written under the slots it had before the flags, and are
  placed too, before any carried row lands beside them.
- **Refused rather than counted**, where a place or note named a page and has no
  slot naming the same page and half on the surviving edition, or where the new
  flags would lengthen a span of an alignment the target already holds. A slot
  past the end of its edition names no page and moves as it is. A place on another
  page with a number beside it cannot be undone; a standing duplicate can.
- **Alignments** (`fold::plan_alignments`) are carried where every span covers
  the same pages and halves before and after. Where both works align one pair,
  in either stored direction, a hand-corrected alignment (any run with
  `by: "hand"`, `merge_spoke`'s own test) replaces one that is not, and
  otherwise the target keeps its own. `uncarried_alignments` counts an
  alignment naming an edition the folded work does not hold, one whose spans
  would move, a hand-corrected one the target's own hand-corrected alignment
  outranks, and a hand-corrected one between two editions the fold makes one.
  A solver's alignment whose pair the target already answers is not counted,
  and neither is a solver's edge between two editions the fold makes one.
- `alignment` and `run` left `fold::DISCARDED`; its `page_flag` entry counts
  credit flags only.

O76's row said `alignment.by` records whether an alignment was corrected. It
does not: `run.by` does, and `alignment.by` reads `hand` only on an edge
`Sidecar::correct` created. The row is marked in place.

M11 is caught by a false refusal, not by a refused fold leaving writes behind:
a refusal returns with the transaction dropped, which rolls every write back,
so no ordering of the writes against the refusals can leave one standing.

The brief's "move progress and notes before the flags are in place" has no
literal form here: a slot's new place is computed from the planned flags, not
read back from the table, so the order of the flag write against the moves
changes no value. What order does matter for is the twin's own rows against
the moves, and that is M04.

### What remains

- The fold writes rows and no file. A surviving work with a `sidecar_path`
  holds a carried alignment in rows until `library export --in-place`, and the
  folded work's own `taiyaku.json` still names it — as has always been true of
  the notes and truth a fold moves.
- A fold is refused, not carried, where a twin's own place, note or alignment
  sits on a page the new flags split, and where two measurements of one
  archive's spreads disagree under a place or note that depends on them. An
  alignment in that second case is left and counted instead.
- An alignment the target already held, on an edition that takes new flags, keeps
  its stored `quality` block, whose `slots` counted the sequence without them.
  `Sidecar::quality_of` recomputes from the runs and nothing reads the stored
  count, so it is stale rather than wrong in use.
- `scripts/mutants.sh` was not run on this branch; the table above is by hand.
- **Unmeasured, read and not driven.** `library import` of a document over a
  surviving work (`import::reimport`, `Scope::Document`) replaces that work's
  page flags from the document. A document holding no spreads would drop the
  flags a fold wrote, and every place and note the fold had placed under them
  would then name another page.

### The review's fix round

An independent review of the first commit, `db2fe30`, drove its own probes and
twenty-six mutations (`scratchpad/o76-review/`). It found no reader row placed
on a wrong page in anything it drove, and eight things to address, which the
branch's second commit does. One line each: what changed, and what was watched
failing.

1. **Two statements over reader data were unpinned.** `resequence_rows`'
   `UPDATE progress` passed every fold and derive test with its `user_id`
   dropped (the review's M14) or its `work_id` dropped (M15); its probes moved
   one reader's place onto another's page, and a place on an unrelated work.
   **Fixed by** `every_statement_that_places_a_slot_touches_only_its_own_row`:
   two readers on one twin at different pages, the first reader on the
   target's other edition too, and the same reader, key and note id on an
   unrelated work, every slot different. **Watched**: the review's M14 and M15,
   and F01–F09 below, each fail it. Its first draft put the unrelated work's
   rows before the spread, where placing them changes nothing; since this round
   `resequence_rows` skips a slot already where it stands, so a read that had
   lost its work wrote nothing there and F03 and F08 survived. The rows moved
   past page 3 and both fail.
2. **A row naming no page refused a fold `main` makes.** `Resequenced::place`
   returned `None` for a slot past the end, which `notes::validate` keeps on
   purpose, and the refusal said the row would name another page. **Fixed**:
   a slot that named no page before the fold is carried as it was, and only a
   row that named a page and has no slot naming it refuses.
   `a_row_naming_no_page_is_carried_as_it_was_and_only_a_row_naming_one_refuses`
   covers a note past the end on the twin, a place past the end on the folded
   edition, and a refusal counting only the row that named a page. **Watched**:
   F10, the first commit's `place`, fails it (`the fold was refused … (1
   note)`); F11, carrying an unplaceable row too, fails four refusal tests.
3. **The flag rule and its docs disagreed.** The code treats a folded edition
   holding no flags as unmeasured and lets the twin take the measured set; the
   docs said two different sets give neither. **Kept the code** (the
   coordinator's decision) and fixed `plan_slots`' doc, the bullet above and
   the O76 row. `a_folded_edition_holding_no_flags_does_not_disagree_with_one_that_holds_them`
   pins it, with a note on the unmeasured copy placed under the taken flag and
   one the flag would split refusing. **Watched**: the review's M26 fails it,
   `left: ([], 4, …)`.
4. **The scan JSON's counter was unasserted.** The review rendered it as
   `discarded_rows + 0 * uncarried_alignments` and all 585 `taiyaku-serve`
   tests passed. **Fixed by** `a_scan_report_counts_the_alignments_a_fold_left_behind`,
   through the scan route: three alignments on the folded work naming editions
   it does not hold, `uncarried_alignments` 3, and `discarded_rows` checked not
   to be 3 (it is 0). **Watched**: the review's M12 fails it, 585 passed and 1
   failed.
5. **The slot refusal's message had three runs of fourteen spaces**, its line
   continuations lost, and it reaches `DeriveReport::unfoldable`. **Fixed**, and
   `a_note_on_a_half_the_twin_does_not_have_refuses_the_fold` asserts the whole
   sentence. **Watched**: F12, the gapped message, fails it.
6. **A write moved above a refusal was hidden by the rollback** (the review's
   M09, the flag write above the slot refusal, and M09c, all four writes above
   the truth refusal). **Fixed**: the fold tests' `refusal` helper makes every
   insert, update and delete on `page_flag`, `progress`, `note`, `alignment` and
   `run` raise first, O78's `refused_leaving_every_note` widened, and
   `a_fold_refused_after_its_slot_plan_has_writes_makes_none_of_them` refuses at
   the last arm with a flag, a place and an alignment all planned. **Watched**:
   M09 fails four tests (`writing spread flag 3 onto full-color: a fold that
   should have refused wrote to page_flag`), M09c fails that one.
7. **Three claims overstated.** The O76 row said "the rest are counted"; two
   kinds are not, and the row now names them as `DeriveReport`'s doc does.
   `THE_FOLD` said the fold refuses when it would leave "anything it carries"
   on another page; the refusal covers rows already on the surviving edition
   too, and the sentence now says "a place or note on either side, or an
   alignment already on this edition". `shared_note_ids`' doc still said
   "there is no slot rewrite to account for" above its own correction; that
   sentence is rewritten, and so is `fold.rs`' module doc, which said an
   alignment not carried is always counted. Grepping for the shape afterwards
   found the same "no slot rewrite" claim twice more: an O78 test's doc in
   `fold/tests.rs`, corrected, and O78's own section of these notes, marked in
   place. **Watched**: F13, the first
   commit's `THE_FOLD` sentence, fails `curation.test.ts`.
8. **Recorded, not fixed**: `library import` over a surviving work could drop
   the flags a fold wrote — What remains above, and the O76 row.

## O89: a directory that qualifies a captured series — 2026-09-16

### The gap, and what the row got wrong

O89's row said two releases of one volume merge "when only the directory, or a
suffix after the volume marker, tells them apart", and offered three fixes: a rule
that reads the directory, an edition key derived from it, or attribution so the
inbox could offer the split. **Rule 1 already reads the directory.** For
`[Oshi no Ko] - Fan Translated/[Oshi no Ko] - v01.cbz` seeded rule 1 captures
`[Oshi no Ko] - Fan Translated`. Seeded rule 4 then captures `[Oshi no Ko]` from the
filename, and `Resolved::set` overwrites. The qualifier is discarded by the next rule
to set a series, after it was read correctly, and `classify` merges what is left, as it should for two
entries that really resolve to one `(series, volume)`. The defect was upstream of
`classify`, in which of two correct captures wins.

Re-measured against the database before any code: 25 editions held more than one
member, and **all 25 drew those members from two different parent directories.**
None drew from one. Three series: `[Oshi no Ko]` 12, `Death Note` 9,
`Yu Yu Hakusho` 4.

### The pre-flight, before any code

The first plan predicted that three directories would move. Simulating seeded rules 1
and 4 over every member's path found eight. The simulation was checked first: its
"before" series agreed with the database for all 1,895 members. One of the eight was
a regression. `Hunter × Hunter (Official Colored) ` carries a trailing space, and the
draft's "extends" would have moved 37 members to a series name ending in whitespace.
So a qualifier must now contain a letter or a digit.

The spec promised that a user's `name` rule would still win, and it could not be
built. Seeded rule 4 is itself a `name` rule, and the draft's guard never changed an
outcome. It was replaced, by decision, with **literals win, captures reconcile**. A
`captured_series` helper is shared with `apply_captures`, so the two cannot disagree
about an empty group. The renames of three series that were not colliding were
accepted rather than narrowed away. Narrowing would need cross-entry state that
`resolve` does not have.

### Executing it: this reverses O95, by decision

The pre-flight simulated the real library and never the test fixtures, and the
conflict was in the fixtures. Task 1's first run broke three `preview::tests`. Two of
them pinned **O95**, which had recorded rule 4 folding `Death Note (Colored Council)`
into `Death Note` as intended. It called the editor remedy that split them "the one
thing that broke it", and this reconciliation *is* that split. The two findings never
met: O95 was decided without the measurement that the fold concatenates two releases
whenever their volumes collide.

**Decided 2026-09-16 that O89 governs.** A qualifying directory is its own series.
The `edition-of` proposal folds it back with an edition key, and since accepting
writes a literal `set_series`, it is never reconciled. O95's two tests moved to the
GTO directories. Those are real shapes whose filename capture is not a prefix of the
directory, so the override stands. The colour-edition fixture now pins that it is no
longer an override. The third broken test's fixture directory `Series 1` qualified
`Series` (remainder `" 1"`) and became `Omnibus 1`.

### Over the real library, before and after

`/home/davey/temp/manga-test`, after the Vagabond repack, binary at `2ee01ac`. The
database was verified byte-identical to its backup before the scan.

Two things the spec did not predict. **`25 rekeyed`** is the 25 formerly merged works

## O111: a page that fits skips the permit — 2026-09-17

### The gap, and why the row's decision was narrowed

`cover::cached_or_generated_page` served a cache hit, then took
`GENERATION_LIMIT`, then fetched the page, then parsed its header in `fit_at`
to learn whether a resize was needed. A page that already fit decoded nothing
and still queued for one of two permits to find that out. O107's timing
measured the wait at a median of 163.8–166.5 ms behind a cold filmstrip, and
170.1 and 169.7 ms after O107's own fix ("O107", "The permit wait", above).

O111's row filed it as a decision with two shapes. The build design
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-o111-permit-scope-design.md`) narrowed it.
The permit's own doc comment justifies it by decode memory and by nothing else,
and a full-size request already fetches with no permit. So taking the fetch and
the header parse out of the permit makes the `?w=` path agree with the permit's
stated purpose and with the full-size path. Its memory cost is the one the row
already named: a page that needs a resize holds its fetched bytes while it
queues, one per queued request, and that cost is not measured. A budget for reading pages alone lost, because two budgets bound two
things and their sum bounds nothing.

### What the design had not seen

Three found by the pre-flight before any code, and two while building:

- **A test pinned the ordering this changes.**
  `a_cold_reading_page_waits_for_a_generation_permit` asserted that a cold page
  does not *fetch* while every permit is held. After the change a page that
  needs a resize does fetch then, by design. The test was rewritten to watch
  the resize finish. This reverses no closed decision: O105's row pins that
  deleting the permit at either site is caught, and so is a semaphore built
  with one permit more than `MAX_CONCURRENT_GENERATIONS`. The rewritten test
  catches both: the first is in the table below, and the second, applied by
  hand on 2026-09-17, turned it and `a_cold_cover_waits_for_a_generation_permit`
  red, 25 of 27 `cover::` tests passing. `cached_or_generated_page`'s doc already said "Moving the fetch
  out of the permit is a separate change".
- **Doc comments defined a generation as "fetching a page and decoding it"**:
  `Semaphore`'s and `MAX_CONCURRENT_GENERATIONS`'. Still true of covers and
  tiles, no longer of reading pages, and both now say which.
- **O107's timing kept no script.** It is rebuilt from the description above
  and kept in the repository this time: `scripts/permit-wait.py` makes the
  requests, and `scripts/permit-wait.sh` serves one build with its own
  database and cache and runs it. One check in the kept script is not the one
  that ran: the runs checked each resize's content type, which cannot fail on
  `raw-mono`'s JPEG pages, and the kept script counts the resized pages in the
  cache instead. The cache each build's last run left held a `-r768` file
  for every resize that run asked for, 7, 13 and 7, beside the warmed hit. The three builds below were run in order,
  each started only after 30 s with no `cargo`, `rustc`, `nextest` or
  `vitest` process running.
- **`fit_at` could not stay `pub`**, as the design said it would. With
  `cached_or_generated_page` calling the halves, it had no production caller,
  and `-D warnings` refuses dead code. It is gone. Its halves are
  `fits_within` (the header) and `resize_to_long_edge` (the decode), and its
  doc comment's arguments moved onto them. The comments in `routes.rs` and
  `routes/tests.rs` that name `fit_at` historically now say where the decision
  lives.
- **`App.tsx` said a full-size page is a generation behind the permit.** Its
  comment on a borrowed page's long edge called the original bytes "a
  full-resolution generation behind `cover.rs`'s two-permit
  `GENERATION_LIMIT`". A full-size request has never taken a permit or
  resized anything, before O111 or since. It now says the whole page at full
  resolution, which is the cost the comment was arguing about.

### The change

```rust
let fetched = page()?;
if fits_within(fetched.as_ref(), long_edge)? {
    return Ok(Fitted::Original(fetched));
}
let bytes = {
    let _permit = GENERATION_LIMIT.acquire();
    resize_to_long_edge(fetched.as_ref(), long_edge)?
};
```

`at_path`, which covers and tiles share, still fetches inside the permit. Each
always decodes, so fetching first would not spare it the wait, and would hold
its page in memory through it.

### Timed before and after

**Substrate.** This workstation, not the NAS: 32 cores, the corpus on local
NVMe with a warm page cache. Release builds of `main` (`c2e3e72`, built in a
detached worktree) and of this branch. Each build served a scratch copy of
`gotoubun-v01`'s sidecar with every member path made absolute, with a fresh
copy of a scratch database holding one admin account and its API key, and a
fresh `--cache`. The machine was not idle: another project's browser tests, a
desktop file indexer and a game were running at points, which is why load is
given beside every run and `main` was run again after the fix.

**Method**, O107's as described, with three differences. A page that **needs a
resize** was added to each round: `raw-mono` at `?w=768`, a different page each
round, so none was a cache hit. The design expected it not to improve. Times
are whole responses, request sent to body read, where O107 did not record which
it took. p90 is nearest-rank. The added request makes a round longer, so n per
filmstrip run is 7 or 8 on `main`, against 14 in O107.

Everything else as before: the tile cache wiped (the one cached reading page
kept), all 187 `en-mono` tiles requested cold over six keep-alive connections,
and 300 ms in, one connection requesting in turn `raw-mono` page 10 at
`?w=1024` (685×1024, so it fits), the same page at full size, the same page at
`?w=768` (a cache hit, warmed first), and the resize, then 50 ms, for three
seconds. Three runs without the filmstrip interleaved with three with it. Checked
once per build before the runs: the page at `?w=1024` and at full size came
back with the same type and size, `image/jpeg`, 197077 B, and the hit 83482 B,

on `main` (n 43), about 16 ms lower; the mean of the run medians was 14 ms
lower. It still queues for the permit behind the tiles, which is the bound this
change keeps. The difference is not explained.

round's fitting page waits for a permit before the resize is asked for, so
fewer rounds fit in the window (7 or 8 against 12 or 13) and each resize lands
at a different point in the filmstrip. That is a guess, not a measurement. A filmstrip took 6.9–7.6 s and a tile a median of 220–240 ms on
every build, so the page that stopped queueing did not slow the tiles.
