## O90: the scan says why a file was skipped — 2026-09-17

O90 closed without a RAR decoder. taiyaku is `GPL-3.0-or-later`, and RARLAB's
UnRAR source carries a restriction the GPL forbids a distributor to add. `unrar`
builds that source, and `unrar-rs` declares GPL-3.0 while incorporating it. The
clean-room `rar` crate was too young for the crate every page read passes
through. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-o90-unreadable-attribution-design.md`
§1 is the record, and `Format::is_readable`'s doc now points at it. What closed
the row is the other half: the twelve files were repacked, and one number that
stood for four causes is now split into those four.

### The repack, 2026-09-15

The twelve Vagabond volumes stored as RAR archives named `.cbz` were converted
in place with `bsdtar -c --format zip --options zip:compression=store
@<archive>`. Each was written to a temporary beside the original and verified
entry by entry before it was renamed over the original. The RAR payloads were
stored rather than compressed, so 4.52 GiB converted in seconds. A rescan then
reported:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unreadable` | 13 | **1** |
| works | 1858 | 1870 |
| members | 1883 | 1895 |
| `merged` | 25 | 25 |

Vagabond went from 25 works to 37, and volumes 3–12, 19 and 20 are the twelve.
`merged` did not move, which is the control: repacking must not touch O89's
case.

**Two of the twelve failed their first verification, and the check was what was
wrong.** It compared sorted entry names and the concatenation of every entry's
bytes. `Vagabond - v19.cbz` and `- v20.cbz` hold their pages under a directory
entry, which RAR records without a trailing slash and zip writes with one. So
the name lists differed by a character on an entry that is not a page. Checked
per entry with directories excluded by type, 178 and 198 files were
byte-identical. Neither original was replaced while its check failed.

Repacking changes every member's `sha256`, and so its work's `content_key`,
which is O81's condition. It cost nothing here: the library held 0 `progress`
rows and 0 `note` rows on 2026-09-15.

### The thirteenth entry was not a vanished member

O90's row, this file under "Twelve volumes that cannot be opened", and this
file's account of the first scan report a serving process sent all called the
thirteenth `unreadable` a member whose bytes could not be hashed. Each passage is now marked in place. Measured read-only on
2026-09-16 against `/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db`:

```
Bisque Doll de Chu ♡/Bisque Doll de Chu ♡.cbz | format zip | pages NULL | sha256 NULL
```

`classify` tests `pages` before it hashes anything, so this entry never reached
`digest`. The archive itself is sound. It is 168 MB; `bsdtar -tf` lists it with
exit 0, `python3 -m zipfile -l` lists it, and `zipfile.testzip()` finds no bad
entry. All 185 entries end `.jxl`. `taiyaku-read`'s `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` has no
JPEG XL, so `member_page_names` found nothing. `member_pages` then took
`read_member`'s "no page images" refusal, and `scan::pages_of` swallowed it
into a NULL.

**A NULL page count is therefore two facts.** Either the archive would not
open, or it opened and held nothing taiyaku reads as a page. The walk keeps no
record of which. An archive with no page images never gets `Some(0)`, because
`member_pages` refuses it. Only a directory reaches `Some(0)`. That is why the
field is `uncounted` and not the spec's first `unlistable`: the one real
instance lists perfectly well.

### What changed

`DeriveReport::unreadable` is a `derive::Unreadable`:

| field | cause | shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `by_format` | a format `Format::is_readable` refuses, by token; `unknown` for NULL | count per token |
| `uncounted` | a container whose pages the walk could not count | full paths |
| `vanished` | a member gone before it could be hashed | full paths |
| `no_pages` | a container holding no page images of its own | count |

`refused_format()` and `total()` are methods, so neither sum can disagree with
the breakdown. Paths are `root.path.join(rel_path)`, since two roots can hold
the same `rel_path`. **Counts for two causes and paths for two was the
person's decision on 2026-09-16.** A file someone has to find is named. A whole
format is fixed by one loop, and a volume directory of archives is a layout
rather than a fault, so those two are counted.

The CLI's scan line prints the total and then each cause that happened.
`config_api::derive_report_json` renders `"unreadable"` as an object through
`unreadable_json`, which destructures with no `..` and adds `total` and
`refused_format`. That renderer serves a scan, a rule apply and a root removal
alike. The Settings scan report draws the total, then each cause as its own
`data-field` row, at zero too.

### The real library, through the branch

Development workstation, debug build of the branch, scanning a copy of
`library.db` in the session scratchpad:

```
  0 added, 1 updated, 0 gone
derived 134 series, 1895 works, 1895 editions, 1895 members, 1 unattached chapter directories, 1 unreadable (1 whose pages could not be counted: /home/davey/temp/manga-test/Volumes/Bisque Doll de Chu ♡/Bisque Doll de Chu ♡.cbz), 4 series holding no work; 0 proposal(s) raised
```

Then `taiyaku serve` over the same copy, vite over the branch's `web/`, and a
Playwright-driven "Scan now" on Configuration → Roots. The report's
`unreadable` row read, element by element: total `1`; "In a format taiyaku does
not read" `0` with no list; "Pages could not be counted" `1`, listing the
Bisque Doll path; "Gone before they could be hashed" `0`; "Holding no page
images" `0`. The report drew 47 `data-field` elements, the number
`ScanReport.test.tsx` asserts. The long path wraps inside its cell, which works
and is left to the style pass.

### Isolation

`date -Iseconds` was stamped at 2026-09-17T00:14:16-07:00, before the scan.
After the CLI scan and again after the browser scan, the original
`library.db` had the same size, mtime and SHA-256 (`9250c8b5…`), and its WAL was
still 0 bytes. `find /home/davey/temp/manga-test -newermt` the stamp returned
one path, the `Volumes` directory itself, with mtime 00:14:22.29, the second
of the CLI scan. That is `watch::probe`, which creates
`.taiyaku-watch-probe-<pid>` in the root and removes it, and no such file
remained. The root's `keeps_documents` is 0, so no document was written. A
read-only `sqlite3 -readonly` query does move `library.db-shm`'s mtime, which is
a reader's side effect and not content.

### The JPEG XL volume, converted — 2026-09-17

The person decided to convert that one file and to leave reading JPEG XL for a
future item (O130). **This wrote into the library tree**, so the original was
kept first: copied to
`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/backups/2026-09-17-bisque-doll-jxl/`, outside the
scan root `Volumes/`, and checked byte-identical by SHA-256 (`55effde9…`).

`jxlinfo` called every sampled page `lossy`, with no JPEG reconstruction data,
so the original JPEGs cannot be recovered and a JPEG target would lose a
second generation. **PNG instead**, which holds exactly what the JPEG XL
decodes to. Each of the 185 pages was read from the backup, decoded by `djxl`
0.12.0 once to PNG and once to PNM, and the two required to hold identical
pixels: 185 of 185 did, 173 greyscale and 12 RGB. The pages were written in
their original order to a stored zip, each `.jxl` name ending `.png`, and every
entry read back and checked against its PNG's SHA-256. 167.8 MB of JPEG XL
became 433.4 MB of PNG. The new archive was copied beside the original under a
dotted temporary name, checked by SHA-256 (`d01a4445…`), and renamed over it.

**A rescan of a copy of `library.db`** with this branch's debug build, the
original's hash, size and mtime checked unchanged afterwards:

```
  0 added, 3 updated, 0 gone
derived 135 series, 1896 works, 1896 editions, 1896 members, 1 unattached chapter directories, 4 series holding no work; 0 proposal(s) raised
```

Nothing is unreadable, works went from 1895 to 1896, and the archive's
`scan_entry` reads 185 pages. The library held no `progress` or `note` rows,
and the archive had never been a member, so no content key named it.

### What remains

- **The walk records no reason for a NULL page count**, so `uncounted` cannot
  say whether an archive would not open or held nothing taiyaku reads. Telling
  them apart needs the refusal kept at scan time, which is a schema change.
  *Filed as O131 on 2026-09-17.*
- **taiyaku reads no JPEG XL page**, which is why the Bisque Doll archive was
  unreadable until it was converted, above. `image` 0.25.9, which the server decodes pages with, has
  no JPEG XL decoder of its own; its `hooks` module only lets one be
  registered. Not looked into beyond that and this one archive. *Filed as O130
  on 2026-09-17, and the archive converted — see above.* *(O130 has since
  closed, on 2026-11-17 — see "JPEG XL pages: the decoder, the clients and a
  real archive (2026-11-17)".)*

## Style pass ①: the foundation — 2026-09-17

PR ①'s tokens, fonts, base rules and theme switch — per
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-style-pass-design.md` — were driven in a
real browser against a scratch copy of the NAS library before the gate ran.
What follows is what that pass measured; nothing here is assumed.

### The split, and the bundle it ships

Task 1's split, which moves `index.css`'s rules into six `@import`ed partials,
changes nothing that ships: `diff -r target/style-pass/dist-before
target/style-pass/dist-split` printed no differences — `dist identical`, same
bytes and the same content-hashed file names.

The fonts are the growth this PR adds. Sizes here are apparent bytes, every
file's `find -printf '%s'` summed; this section first gave the two totals as
612 KB and 36 MB, which were `du -sh`'s disk usage. Before the fonts, at
`948efbc`, `target/style-pass/dist-before` held 604,783 bytes, with one CSS
asset of 16,306 bytes. After them and before the strip below, at `b42c095`,
`target/style-pass/dist-after` held 34,294,658 bytes, with a 713.98 kB CSS
asset (312.31 kB gzip); the JS is close to untouched — `main` 191.45 kB (58.04
kB gzip), `label` 10.87 kB (4.29 kB gzip), the shared chunk 215.92 kB (68.92 kB
gzip) — and the wasm binary's 170.46 kB is unchanged. The difference is fonts:
570 `.woff2` files, 14,841,516 bytes total, and 574 `.woff` fallbacks,
18,148,448 bytes, plus 693,791 bytes of `@font-face` CSS in that build (608
rules; the CSS asset grew 697,682 bytes, the rest this PR's own rules), since
`@fontsource` splits each weight into about 121 `unicode-range` subsets. Before
the user chose to keep every subset (option A, decided 2026-09-17), the
alternatives were measured too: Latin subsets alone would cost about 18 kB of
CSS total (`latin-400.css` is 310 bytes, one `@font-face`) with Japanese falling
back to the device font, against 966,336 bytes (Zen Kaku Gothic New 400) to
1,992,116 bytes (Shippori Mincho B1 700) per weight for a whole Japanese-subset
file.

**The `.woff` fallbacks are stripped from the build**, a user decision of
2026-09-18. Each `@font-face` from `@fontsource` lists `url(….woff2)
format('woff2'), url(….woff) format('woff')`, and every browser that
understands `light-dark()` supports woff2, so the second source is never
fetched. `web/src/stripWoff.ts`, a PostCSS plugin wired through
`vite.config.ts`'s `css.postcss`, removes it before Vite emits anything. Built
at `b09ac9a` into `target/style-pass/dist-stripped`, these are the current
figures: 0 `.woff` files and 570 `.woff2` (14,841,516 bytes, unchanged), a
573.60 kB CSS asset (243.22 kB gzip), 16,005,973 bytes in all, and the JS
chunks at the same sizes as `dist-after`. Summed rule by rule, the 608
`@font-face` rules in each built CSS asset come to 693,791 bytes in
`dist-after` and 553,346 in `dist-stripped`. The CSS shrank by more than the
URLs' text because Vite inlines a small asset as a `data:` URI: 33 *more*
`.woff` sources, beyond the 574 files, were inlined that way — 607 `.woff`
sources in all — and went with the rest. The 37 inlined `.woff2` stay, and
every other font URL in the stripped CSS names a file that exists in `dist`.

### The figures face, and what a page downloads

Zen Kaku Gothic New has no tabular figures, read from the font file with
fontTools before any of the above ran: its Latin subset
(`@fontsource/zen-kaku-gothic-new@5.3.0`, `latin-400`) carries only the `ccmp`,
`frac`, `vert` and `vrt2` GSUB features, no `tnum`, and its digit advances are
0: 504, 1: 383, 2: 445, 3: 484, 4: 493, 5: 468, 6: 493, 7: 412, 8: 509, 9: 475
units. That is why tables use `--font-figures`, a `taiyaku figures` face that
maps U+0030–0039 to a local tabular sans and falls back to `--font-ui` for
everything else. Measured in a `<table>` inside `.library`, after
`document.fonts.ready`: `1111111111` and `8888888888` both come to 101.8 px.
Outside a table the same two strings come to 61.28 px and 81.45 px — the
control that shows Zen Kaku Gothic New's own digits are proportional, so the
fallback face is doing the work and the first pair is not vacuous.

On `/`, signed in, in ink, the library page downloaded five font files
totalling 84,196 bytes: the two Latin subsets,
`zen-kaku-gothic-new-latin-400-normal.woff2` (9,752 bytes) and
`shippori-mincho-b1-latin-600-normal.woff2` (32,452), and three Japanese
subsets fetched because the library holds Japanese titles —
`shippori-mincho-b1-115-600-normal.woff2` (15,416),
`shippori-mincho-b1-104-600-normal.woff2` (17,772) and
`zen-kaku-gothic-new-97-400-normal.woff2` (8,804) — the lazy per-subset
behaviour working as designed.

### Tokens resolve, and the choice persists

On `/` at 1440×900, with Ink chosen, `getComputedStyle('.library')` answers
`data-theme="ink"`, `color-scheme: dark`, background `rgb(21, 19, 15)` and
colour `rgb(236, 228, 212)`, and `localStorage['taiyaku.prefs.theme']` holds
`{"choice":"ink"}`. After a full reload, `data-theme` is still `ink` before any
React code runs — the pre-paint script — the background is still the ink value,
and the Ink radio is checked. The body font family resolves to `"Zen Kaku
Gothic New", system-ui, sans-serif`; `.sidebar-heading`'s to `"Shippori Mincho
B1", serif`.

The other three cases, measured afterwards on the same page through
Playwright's `emulateMedia`. With Paper chosen, the ground is `rgb(243, 238,
227)` and the text `rgb(35, 30, 23)`, `color-scheme: light` — and they stay
exactly that with the OS emulated as dark, which is what pinning a theme is
for. With System chosen, `data-theme` is absent and `color-scheme` reads
`light dark`; under an emulated dark OS the ground is the ink value, `rgb(21,
19, 15)` with text `rgb(236, 228, 212)`, and under an emulated light OS the
paper value. So all three choices do what spec §3 says, in both directions.

### The reader, and the browser project

With the chrome shown at 1440×900 in ink, the reader's layout button `single` —
a bare `<button>` — computes `border-radius: 0px`, `border-width: 2px` and
background `rgb(107, 107, 107)`, so `base.css`'s scoped control rules do not
reach it; and `font-family: Arial`, which is the evidence that `:root`'s font
does not reach it either: the UA stylesheet sets a font on `button`, so a bare
button does not inherit one. What it keeps is the platform's UA default —
Arial is what Chromium on Linux gave — not a promise of Arial; another browser
or OS may draw another face. Task 4's review had predicted these buttons would
change font; measured, they do not. What does change is anything that opts in
with `font: inherit`: `Chrome.tsx`'s Library button computes `"Zen Kaku Gothic
New", system-ui, sans-serif` in a 70.67 × 32.39 box, and
`document.elementFromPoint` at its centre still answers `Library` — O65's
property holds. The readout row computes the same family. `body`'s background
is now `rgb(21, 19, 15)` in ink, the surround the reader draws over until PR ③
makes it `#000`.

The browser test project — 5 files, 28 tests, covering O65's docked button
among others — passed in full at `b42c095`; its baseline before any task was

## O133: covers sized per screen — 2026-09-18

Found on the user's iPhone during style pass ②'s device pass: covers were
visibly blurry. Every cover in the library was the reader's filmstrip tile —
`/api/library/series/{id}/cover` answered 307 to `/pages/0/thumb`, and the web
drew the same route for volume tiles and continue cards — 160 px on its long
edge (`cover.rs`'s `THUMB_LONG_EDGE`), drawn at about 256 CSS px on a phone's
grid, 768 device pixels at 3×. **The user chose one size per screen density**
over 768 px everywhere or 512 px everywhere.

**The fix sizes page 0 on the tile route.** `GET /api/works/{work}/{edition}/pages/0/thumb?w=N`,
for N one of `cover::COVER_LONG_EDGES` (256, 512, 768), is page 0 fitted inside
a long edge of N, served by `routes.rs::serve_page` — the page route's own
body, moved out of `get_page` so that both call it — so it is resized with
`CatmullRom` rather than `thumbnail`'s fast sampler, cached per size by content
in the same file the page route would use, and carries the page route's `ETag`
and `Cache-Control` (`private, no-cache`). Any other page, any other size, and a
`w` that is not a number get the 160 px tile (`cover_edge`). The web draws the
tile URL with `srcSet` `?w=256 1x, ?w=512 2x, ?w=768 3x` (`library.ts`'s
`coverSources`, drawn by `Cover.tsx`), and the series cover route passes a
cover size through: `?w=512` answers 307 to `/pages/0/thumb?w=512`, and `?w=1`,
`?w=1000`, `?w=abc` or no `w` to the plain tile.

**The first version sent covers through the page route** — `workCover` named
`/pages/0` and the series cover route redirected to `/pages/0?w=N` — and the
review of that version found what it cost: the page route refuses an account
without `can_stream` (`refuse_if_cannot_stream`, whose own doc says covers must
stay outside it so that a download-only account still sees its shelf), so
every cover on such an account's shelf would have been a placeholder. The
reviewer measured it on a copy of the scratch library with such an account
added: the unsized series cover 200, every sized one 403. The gate had been
green, because the one test of that policy,
`download/tests.rs::without_can_stream_the_pages_are_403_and_the_download_still_works`,
asks only for the unsized tile, and asks `!= 403` of a fixture whose tile
answers 404. Sizing the page route for such an account instead was not an
option: it would let it read every page at up to 4096 px. So the tile route
takes the size, for page 0 and three sizes only. The first version's bytes and
this one's are the same — the same function makes them, into the same cache
file — so the measurements below, taken on the first, stand for both where
they say so.

Measured on the scratch copy over HTTP, on the first version's debug binary:
Berserk v01's page 0 (1810×2560) comes back 181×256 (17,623 bytes), 362×512
(55,191) and 543×768 (106,981), each with an `ETag` ending `-r256v2`,
`-r512v2`, `-r768v2`. The fix, on a release build, answers the same three
sizes through the tile route (below).

In Chromium at three device pixels per CSS pixel and 390×844, the first version
fetched `w=768` for each of the first six covers on the home screen, continue
cards and grid tiles alike; the fix, emulated the same way with the cache
disabled, fetched `…/pages/0/thumb?w=768` for the four continue cards and
`…/cover?w=768` for the two series tiles, all six loaded, and at 1× and
1440×900 it fetched `?w=256` for the same six. **`naturalWidth` reads 170–181 there, not 543**:
with density descriptors a browser reports the image's size divided by the
density it was chosen for (543 / 3 = 181), so it is not the evidence it looks
like — the `w=768` in `currentSrc` and the 543×768 the route returns are. At
1× and 1440×900, in the first version's debug run, the two covers loaded within
six seconds fetched `w=256`; the rest had not loaded, because each size of each
cover is generated on its first request and a debug resize takes seconds.

**On the user's iPhone**, through `tailscale serve` to the first version, the user
looked at the library home and reported the covers sharp.
The request log holds 62 requests from it, all with the user-agent
`Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) … Version/26.6.1
Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1`, and every one of its 42 cover requests — 20
series-cover redirects and 22 page 0s — asked for `w=768`; none asked for the
tile. The fix draws the same bytes from the same cache file, so the phone was
not asked again.

**What a cold cover costs, timed on a release build** of the first version, on this
workstation (not the NAS the deployment runs on), against the scratch copy with
an empty cache directory, one request at a time through the series cover route
with redirects followed, for the first twelve series: a cold tile took a median
of 31 ms (max 181), and then cold covers at `w=256`, 512 and 768 took 34, 39 and
49 ms (max 310, 284, 295); a second request for `w=768` took 1 ms (max 6). The
comparison flatters the resize a little: each series' tile was asked for first,
so its archive was already in the operating system's file cache when the three
sizes were made. In the debug binary a cold resize took about 2.4 s. The fix,
timed the same way on its own release build with an empty cache, for eleven
series — 1–5, 7–10, 137 and 138, as the review read them back from that run's
cache files, the script having kept no list: cold covers at 256, 512 and 768 px took a median
of 35, 38 and 48 ms (max 302, 287, 292), and a second 768 px request 1 ms (max
3). A cold tile took a median of 52 ms (max 210) in that run; the review's
repeat of the same eleven on its own server gave 31 ms for the tile and 38, 39
and 46 ms for the covers, so the covers' figures held and the tile's did not.

The first version's five hand mutations, each against its own test and
restored after: `Cover.tsx` without `srcSet` failed "leaves a cover that loads

failed its own test and "leaves a cover that loads alone"; `workCover` back to

continue-card case and the `workCover` test; and the series cover handler
ignoring `w`, and without its `> 1` filter, each failed its redirect test.

The fix's five, the same way, after a control run of the five tests they
touch: the stream check put back on the sized branch failed
`a_download_only_account_sees_covers_at_every_size_and_still_no_pages` at
`?w=256` (403); `cover_edge` without `index == 0` failed
`the_tile_route_sizes_page_zero_only_and_only_to_a_cover_size` at page 1;
`cover_edge` taking any size failed it at `?w=1000`; the sized branch serving
the whole page failed the download-only test at the image's long edge; and the

`a_series_cover_asked_for_a_cover_size_redirects_to_the_tile_at_that_size` at
`?w=1`. The page-1-and-other-sizes test passed before the fix as well as
after, which is what it is for: it holds the line the fix must not cross.

**A download-only account, measured on the fix.** A copy of the scratch
library, served by the fix's release build, with an account `dlonly` added and
its `can_stream` set to 0: sign-in 204 and the series list 200; the series

181×256, 362×512 and 543×768; a `workCover` URL at `?w=256` 200; page 0
through the page route at `?w=256` still 403; and page 1's tile at `?w=768`
the 160 px tile. The first version answered every sized cover 403 for such an
account.

**The review of the fix** found its behaviour right and the move into
`serve_page` faithful, and one gap: nothing tested the grant check on the sized
branch. `serve_page` asks no grant, so `get_thumb`'s `refuse_if_hidden` is all

O122's row undercounted the handlers that take a work's lock on the async

still asks only `!= 403` of an unsized tile its fixture answers 404, which the

## The cover version: covers the browser keeps (2026-10-29)

The loading work's second PR (spec `2026-10-28-loading-library-design.md`,
§4) gives each library cover an address that names its bytes, so the
browser keeps it and a return to the grid asks for no cover. It closes
O224.

**What the version is made of.** `cover::cover_version(sha256, offset)` is
`{sha256}-{offset}-{PAGE_FORMAT_VERSION}`: what a cover's `ETag` is made of
(`cover::page_key`, through `routes::page_etag`) but its long edge, so it
changes exactly when the `ETag` of any cover size would. One address per
edition carries it, and the client adds the size per screen density.

**The answers that carry it.** A series row's `cover`, in the grid, search
and a series page's own row, and each edition card's `cover`, are
`/api/works/{work}/{edition}/pages/0/thumb?v=…`, built by
`library_api.rs`'s `cover_address` with each segment and the version
encoded as `encodeURIComponent` would (`uri_component`). `coverSources`
adds `w`. The series cover `307` is unchanged, and the web client no
longer asks for it.

**The route's three answers to `?v=`**, read on a cover alone (page 0 at
one of `cover::COVER_LONG_EDGES`) and decided in `routes.rs::serve_page`
against the page it locates:
- a version equal to that page's: the `200` and the `304` both carry
  `COVER_CACHE_CONTROL`, `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`;
- any other version, such as one from a list read before the member
  changed: the current image with `PAGE_CACHE_CONTROL`,
  `private, no-cache`, so no address is kept for good over bytes it does
  not name;
- no version: `PAGE_CACHE_CONTROL`, as before. A tile with a `v` is the
  tile.

**Why this answers O1's reason for declining `immutable`.** O1 declined it
because a page's URL names a work, an edition and an index, none of which
move when an archive is replaced, so an entry the browser never
revalidates would keep the old bytes ("`immutable` is not shipped either",
above). A versioned cover address names the bytes: a replaced member or a
new `PAGE_FORMAT_VERSION` gives the cover a new address, the next list read
carries it, and the old one is not asked for again. Pages, tiles and an
unversioned cover keep `private, no-cache`.

**O224's evidence, on the user's iPhone** over the tailnet, 2026-10-29
00:18:46–00:20:04, against a release build of the branch over a scratch
copy of the test library. The user agent read `Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU
iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko)
Version/27.0.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1`, Safari 27.0.1. The user went
Back from a series page to the grid, Back from the reader to One Piece's
series page, and used the reader's Library button, and said "yes these all
go back to where I was". The phone's 269 requests held no `307`, no `304`
and no `/cover` path, and no cover or thumbnail address was asked for
twice. Its lines for those returns, from the server's request log, as the
check recorded them with its notes beside them:

```
00:19:02.045 GET 200 /api/library/series            (Back from series/23 to the grid; next image 8.6 s later, a first-time cover from scrolling on)
00:19:02.045 GET 200 /api/library/home
00:19:24.291 PUT 204 /api/works/one-piece---v007--2005--cbz/progress   started 1793258364291277, 497 µs
00:19:24.298 GET 200 /api/library/series/91          started 1793258364298300 (after the PUT's end 1793258364291774); Back from the reader
00:19:28.902 GET 200 /api/library/series            (Back from series/91 to the grid; no image request follows)
00:19:28.902 GET 200 /api/library/home
00:19:35.519 GET 200 /api/library/series            (to the grid from series/79; no image request follows)
00:19:49.393 GET 200 /api/library/series?library=1  (to the grid from series/13; no image request follows)
00:19:57.825 PUT 204 /api/works/oshi-no-ko----v01-cbz/progress  (last save, ends 1793258397825397)
00:19:59.339 GET 200 /api/library/series?library=1  (the reader's Library button; no image request follows)
00:20:04.190 GET 200 /api/library/series?library=1  (the Library button again, from Goblin Slayer Gaiden 2 v01; no image request follows)
```
