**In Chromium**, on the same build, Back from Jigokuraku to the grid at
1280 px kept a scroll of 2000 with 18 of 18 covers complete at the first
frame, and the server's log held `series?library=1`, `home?library=1` and
the favicon's `304`, with no thumbnail, `/cover` or `307`. **The exception
is O230's.** After One Piece's 111 thumbnails and three visits to the
reader, Back from Nana to the grid showing Unread, sorted by Added, kept
its scroll of 2500 at React's commit with 1 of 18 visible covers complete,
and 18 of 18 at +590 ms. About 70 thumbnails were read again from the
browser's HTTP cache (`transferSize` 0, `private, max-age=31536000,
immutable`), and the server's log has none of them, only
`series?library=1` and `home?library=1`: the browser's in-memory image
cache had dropped them. The reader's Library button returned to a scroll
of 4762 with 1 of 18 covers complete at its commit, the same effect. In
that browser, animation frames ran at about one a second from the first
reader visit on, so the readings were taken at React's commit.

## Style pass ③: the reader — 2026-09-19

What §8 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-style-pass-design.md` promised,
measured. The app is this branch (`style-pass-3-reader`, `e67f667`) served by
vite against `taiyaku serve` on the scratch copy of the NAS library
(`target/style-pass/lib/library.db`, 1,896 works), driven in Chromium through
Playwright at 1440×900 and 390×844, and opened on the user's iPhone over the
tailnet. Every figure below was read off the running app unless it says
otherwise.

**The planning probes.** `light-dark()` in an unregistered custom property
resolves where a property *uses* the token, against that element's
`color-scheme`: a page holding the token rules, one paragraph outside a
`color-scheme: dark` box and one inside, computed Ink's text
`rgb(236, 228, 212)` for the inside paragraph in all four combinations of
{Paper pinned, System} × {OS light, OS dark}, in Chromium 151 and Firefox 153,
while the outside paragraph followed the theme. jsdom keeps `var()` verbatim in
an inline style — `border-color`, `bottom: calc(var(…) + 8px)`, `background`,
and a four-value `padding` shorthand all read back exactly as written, with the
shorthand's longhands empty — which is why the reader's viewport-dependent
geometry stays inline and reads custom properties. Biome 2.5.7 accepts
`env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)`, `html:has(.reader)`, `rgb(21 19 15 / 0.92)`,
a custom property redefined inside `@media (width < 900px)`, and
`clip-path: inset(50%)`. Today's layout row, before it was removed, measured
37 px tall with the page area at 863 px at 1440×900 (987 at 768×1024).

**The bars, in the app.** At 1440×900 with the chrome shown: the top bar is
0–52 across the full width; the bottom bar 689–900, 211 px tall — its 1 px
rule, the 176 px strip, the 2 px progress line and the 32 px readout row; the
page area is 0–900, the reader's whole height, and the same figure with the
chrome hidden, which is the 37 px the layout row used to take. At 390×844: the
top bar 0–52, the bottom bar 697–844 at 147 px, the strip 112. No sideways
scroll at either size. The top bar's text computes to `rgb(236, 228, 212)` and
the body's background to `rgb(0, 0, 0)`.

**The panel docking rule (§8.1), in the app.** At 390×844 the keyboard help
sits at top 68 — the top bar's 52 plus 16 — and bottom 681, which is exactly
16 px above the bottom bar's 697; left 16, right 374. At 1440×900 the same
rule holds against the 689 px bar.

**Paper and Ink are the same reader, to the pixel.** Captured back to back in
one state (single, slot 5, chrome shown, notes off), flipping only
`data-theme`: **0 differing pixels** over the whole 1440×900 viewport
(ImageMagick `compare -metric AE`). At 390×844 the same comparison gives 88
differing pixels, confined by `compare`'s own trim to a 366×12 box at (12,
824) — the readout row, where the reading clock ticked between the two shots.
*(An earlier comparison of 177,960 pixels was two different pages and two
different note states, not a theme difference; the pair has to be captured
back to back.)*

**The bar's ink over each ground, sampled from the screenshot.** At the top
bar's own row: `srgb(19, 17, 14)` where it lies over the black letterbox and
`srgb(39, 37, 34)` where it lies over the white page — within a unit per
channel of the "panel over white artwork" the spec's §8.2 contrast model
computes (`rgb(40, 38, 34)`). The difference is *consistent with* the browser
quantising the panel's own layer before compositing it, which was not
measured: round(0.92 × 21, 19, 15) is (19, 17, 14), and + 0.08 × 255 lands on
(39, 37, 34) — both channels the sample reads. The layout
icons' stroke reads `srgb(236, 228, 212)`, Ink's `--text`.

**O112's answer, in the app.** With two notes on the slot on screen and the
list under the page: chrome hidden, the list is visible and the page area is
835 px at 1440×900 (779 at 390×844); chrome shown, the list's computed
visibility is `hidden` and the page area is **the same figure**, so the page
does not resize on `Tab`; the readout still says "2 notes here of 2".

**The strip's tiles are shorter than the slot they sit in, by the scrollbar.**
The rail is `overflow-x: auto`, and a real volume's 207 tiles always overflow
it, so a classic scrollbar takes 15 px off the rail's client height: at
1440×900 a tile button measures 149 px and its image 145 inside the 176 px
strip; at 390×844, 85 and 81 inside 112. The spec's "shown at exactly 1:1"
therefore holds only where scrollbars overlay rather than take space — iOS
does overlay them. This is not new: the rail's `overflow-x: auto` predates
this branch, and so does the subtraction. Filed as O138. The browser
project's own tile-height case passes because its six-page fixture never
overflows the rail.

**Scroll mode does not follow a tile taken from the strip.** In scroll mode
with the chrome shown, clicking the tile for slot 10 moves the reader's
position — the readout reads `slot 10 / 207 · p. 10` — while the view stays
where it was: pages 4 and 5 at the top, `scrollTop` unchanged at 9,803.
**Measured on `main` the same way**, in a worktree served beside this branch
against the same server: the readout reads slot 10 and `scrollTop` stays 0,
pages 0 and 1 at the top. So this predates the branch; filed as O136. What
this branch did add, `scroll-padding-top` on the page area, is in place and
computes to 52 px, so the *next* scroll target clears the top bar.

**Correcting, a gap and a borrowed page could not be reached in this
library.** Every one of its 1,896 works is single-edition and unaligned
(`editions.length === 1` for all of them, `aligned` false for all of them), so
`c` has nothing to correct and neither arm of the gap/borrowed code can be
entered. Adding the repository's `corpus/` as a second root and scanning it
(808 s, `last_scan_status: ok`; its report counted 1,955 editions and
2,006 members, against the 1,947 and 1,998 rows the database then held —
the report's counters are the derive's, not row counts) produced 38
proposals — `edition-of` and `attach-chapters`, including
"Go-Toubun no Hanayome - Full Color Edition may be the Full Color Edition
edition of Go-Toubun no Hanayome" — rather than multi-edition works, and
accepting one goes through the proposals screen, which is ⑤'s. The three
states' geometry is pinned in jsdom instead (`Chrome.test.tsx` draws no top
bar while correcting; `CorrectionBanner.test.tsx` pins the banner in the top
bar's place; `Borrowed.test.tsx` pins the mark below the bar's line), and
④'s device pass is where they are first seen on a screen.

**The iPhone**, over the tailnet, user-agent read from
`target/style-pass/three/requests.log` before any answer was believed: 188
requests from `Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_7 like Mac OS X)
AppleWebKit/605.1.15 … Version/26.6.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1`. The user
reports: the library upright sits clear of the status bar and its last row of
covers clear of the home indicator; held sideways everything stays clear of
the notch and the rounded corners, the drawer included; opening a work is
**black from the first moment**, with no flash of paper — which is what the
`.reader-route` wrapper is for; in the reader the ground is black edge to edge
and the status bar draws as transparent black over it; and nothing sits under
the notch or the home indicator that should not. The bars themselves, their
44 px targets and Safari's own resolution of the tokens inside `.reader` are
④'s device pass, since a phone cannot open the chrome until touch input
exists.

**One thing the phone found that the desktop could not.** With the note
editor open, a tap on the page draws a region rather than closing the editor,
so on a touch screen the only way out of the panel is Delete: `Escape` and a
click on the background are what `NotePanel`'s own doc offers, and neither is
available to a finger. Filed as O137.

## Style pass ④: touch — 2026-09-20

What §9 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-style-pass-design.md` promised,
measured. The app is this branch served by vite against `taiyaku serve` on the
scratch copy of the NAS library (`target/style-pass/lib/library.db`), driven in
Chromium through Playwright at 1440×900 and 390×844, and opened on the user's
iPhone over the tailnet. Every figure below was read off the running app unless
it says otherwise.

**The planning probes.** `setChromeVisible` had exactly two call sites on
`main` at `333b3ab` — `keyPlan`'s `Tab` and the correction path — so a finger
could not reach the chrome at all, which is why ③'s device pass saw the
reader's ground and nothing the reader draws on it. `readerIntent` is declared
inside the keydown effect, so the pointer reaches it through a ref, as
`closeEditorRef` already does. `clampRect` allocates a fresh rect on every
call and `readerIntent` runs `setView(clampRect)` on every step, so
`view === WHOLE` is dead after the reader's first page turn: the swipe is
gated on `isWhole`, by value. `@vitest/browser-playwright` does expose
`contextOptions`, so `hasTouch` was reachable — and declining it was the
choice, because the project has one instance and enabling it would put all
fifty-eight existing browser cases into a touch context to reach two things
the device pass owns anyway.

**The gestures, in the app.** The page area is the whole viewport at both
sizes — `[0, 0, 1440, 900]` and `[0, 0, 390, 844]` — and computes
`touch-action: manipulation`. Its thirds fall at 480 and 960 on the desktop,
130 and 260 on the phone. A tap in the right third of a right-to-left work
steps the slot **down** and the left third steps it up, which is `stepFor`
applied to a physical `by` and is the mirroring working rather than failing.
The middle third brought the bars up and took them down again at both sizes.
**The swipe, measured in isolation** because a first pass through a whole
battery read 40 px as no turn and 39 px as a turn — an artefact of the slot
sitting at the start of the volume, not of the rule: at both sizes a drag of
39 px turns nothing, 40 px turns, 41 px turns, and 60 px the other way turns
back. Zoomed in, a 120 px drag turns nothing and pans.

**The letterbox, and why O137's second exit had to be built.** The page
`<img>`'s box **equals** the page area at both sizes, and `object-fit:
contain` letterboxes the picture inside that element. At 1440×900 a 900×1350
page paints at `[420, 0, 600, 900]`, leaving 420 px of margin either side; at
390×844 a 683×1024 page paints at `[0, 130, 390, 585]`, leaving 130 px above
and below. So every press in the reader was "on an image", `gestureFor`'s rule
1 could never fire, and the exit `NotePanel`'s doc had promised since the
editor shipped did not exist. Measured before the fix, three points at each
size — and the pair differs, because the margin does: at 1440×900 the page
paints full height, so the points were left of it, right of it and on it; at
390×844 it paints full width, so they were above, below and on. All six left
the editor open. Measured after: the margin closes it, the painted page still
draws, all six correct. The editor's Close button measures **44 px tall by
61 wide** under `(pointer: coarse)` and 31 px on a fine pointer; the five colour
swatches, in the row above the editor's Delete and Close buttons, are 22 px
on both.

**The panels.** The three `docked-panel` panels sit in a corner — the keyboard
help `[1040, 68, 384, 605]` at 1440 and `[16, 68, 358, 613]` at 390, credits
and the note list 88 and 107 px tall — and a tap beside one closes it and
turns nothing, measured at both sizes (the slot read 4 before and after). At
390 the help panel is 358 px of a 390 px screen, so the right-third point
lands inside it and the tap is the panel's, not the page's. **Settings is a
`reader-dialog` whose scrim is the whole viewport**, measured `[0, 0, 1440,
900]` and `[0, 0, 390, 844]`, so before ④'s fix no tap could reach the page
area while the one panel O135 records as closing on neither `Escape` nor `s`
was open. Its Close button, which style pass ③ gave it, was already a pointer
exit — what it lacked was the tap-outside ④ gives every other panel. It now dismisses from its own scrim: measured at
1440×900, 768×1024 and 390×844, each time closing and turning nothing. The
bare scrim either side of the panel is 480 px at 1440 and 144 at 768, but only
**20 px at 390** — where the band to aim at is the 84 px above or below it.

**What it costs to open the chrome.** With the bars hidden the reader is
**30 elements and 1 image**; with them shown, **774 elements, 238 images and
246 buttons** — the filmstrip builds one tile per page, unwindowed, every
time, because `Chrome` returns `null` when hidden. From the tap to the bars
fully on screen at 390×844 on a 237-page volume: **44–76 ms to appear and
157–177 ms to settle** unthrottled, **182–387 ms and 290–500 ms** at 4× CPU
throttling. About 115 ms of that is the opacity fade, whose default is 120 ms
(`modules/motion.ts`). The user reported it as slow on the phone; it is its
own PR after ④, by their decision.

**O138, both ways.** In headless Chromium at 1440×900 the strip's rail reads
`clientHeight` 176 against `offsetHeight` 176 — the scrollbar takes **0 px** —
and a tile button is 164 px with its image at 160, which is what spec §8.4
claims. The user then looked on their own desktop: a scrollbar track is
visible and the thumbnails are the height the strip is. Both readings are the
overlay case; the 15 px O138 recorded belongs to a classic scrollbar, which is
a platform setting rather than anything this code chooses.

**The iPhone**, iOS 18.7 Safari over the tailnet. The user reports: the thirds
and the middle tap and the swipe all work; nothing turns by accident,
including a finger that lands, drifts and lifts; pinch still zooms the
document and a double tap turns two pages without zooming it. Three things
they found that no test could:

1. **Signing in left the whole document zoomed**, and a pinch was the only way
   back. The login fields compute to **14px** — they inherit `--text-ui`
   (0.875rem) from their label through `base.css`'s `font: inherit` — and iOS
   Safari zooms the document whenever a text field under 16px takes focus, a
   zoom that outlives the field. Floored to 16px under `(pointer: coarse)`;
   measured after, a touch context reads 16px and the desk still reads 14px.
   The user confirms it is fixed. *The login screen is ①'s, not ④'s.*
2. **The reader rubber-banded** under a swipe that drifted vertically.
   Measured first, to be sure there was nothing real to scroll: the document's
   scroll height equals its client height, the page area is `overflow: hidden`
   and carries `touch-action: manipulation`. `overscroll-behavior: none` on
   the reader's own root; measured after, the library's root reads `auto` and
   the reader's `none`. The user confirms it is fixed.
3. **A new note can only be started by `n`**, and on a phone held upright an
   existing one cannot be opened by pointer either: the painted page fills
   the width at 390×844, so `Annotations.tsx`'s margin tab is laid out at
   **x = 394 in a 390 px viewport** — just off screen. Held sideways the tab
   is on screen and a click on it does open the editor (measured at
   1440×900 and at 844×390). `NoteList`'s rows open one by pointer too, and
   the list needs `annotations.reveal` — which `r` toggles, and which the
   Settings panel writes by the other door, `reveal` being a key of
   `annotationsModule.defaults` that `Settings.tsx` generates a checkbox
   for. So a portrait route does exist, through ⚙, and it was driven end to
   end at 390×844: middle tap, ⚙, scroll the panel to Annotations —
   *reveal* is the sixth section's third row, laid out at y ≈ 1134 in an
   844 px viewport — tap it, dismiss the panel, drop the bars, tap a row.
   The bars must come down first: with them up the list is
   `visibility: hidden`, and a tap where a row sits hits a filmstrip tile
   and turns the page instead. The user: *"I'm not sure how to make a
   note on mobile, but it's ok. this is a small feature and we can worry
   about it later"*. Filed as O139.

**What the user answered, the same day.** The rows ④ put to them, and the
things they raised unprompted, quoted rather than paraphrased so the rows that
cite them have a source:

- **O134**, the strip's softness on a 3× screen — asked with the strip in
  front of them. They chose **a sharper tile from the server**, the way O133's
  covers were fixed, over leaving it or leaving it open. So the row stays
  open as server work.
- **O138**, the rail's scrollbar — they looked on their own desktop and
  reported: *"there is a scrollbark track and the thumbnails are
  appropriately sized for the strip"*. A visible track that costs no tile
  height is the overlay case.
- **The chrome's key**, unprompted, reading on a desktop: *"one thing about
  pressing tab to open the menu, I can't keep pressing tab. I can press it to
  close the menu, but then after that tab highlights stuff in my browser and
  starts moving around there outside of the in-page content"*. Offered a
  dedicated key now or the accessibility pass, they chose **the accessibility
  pass**, which is where O135 already sits.
- **The chrome's cost**, unprompted: *"is it possible to speed up the menu
  opening at all?"*, after *"the middle tap seems a bit slow to actually pull
  up the menu"*. Shown the measurements, they chose **its own PR straight
  after ④** over widening this one or only cutting the fade.
- **The zoom after signing in**, unprompted: *"the page seems to start zoomed
  in on my phone a bit after login which is annoying. I have to pinch to zoom
  out"* — and afterwards, *"the sign in thing seems to work"*.
- **The rubber band**, unprompted: *"is it possible when fully zoomed out to
  prevent scrolling so that if someone is swiping they don't accidentally
  scroll up and down? … it may just be safari's refresh animation - is it
  possible to remove that in the reader part?"* — and afterwards, *"ok that
  pull down is fixed"*.

**The scrim, on the phone.** The one thing ④ shipped that no test here could
reach: `Settings.tsx`'s dismissal depends on `pointerup` carrying the lift's
coordinates while implicit pointer capture holds the event's target, and that
was measured in Chromium only — no WebKit is installed on this machine. Put to
the user on their iPhone on 2026-09-20, after the PR was opened: press the
bare scrim beside or above the panel and lift. They report it closes and turns
no page — *"the ios test seems good"*. So the fix works on the device it was
written for. **What that does not cover**: the failing direction I4 was filed
for, a press that goes down on the scrim and is released over the *panel*,
which is the case the hit test exists to refuse. It was not asked for, and
iOS's own touch-scroll slop is still its own figure.

**Correcting, a gap and a borrowed page.** ③ left all three pinned in jsdom
because the scratch library held no multi-edition work and the screen that
accepts a proposal is ⑤'s. The **CLI accepts one**, which ③'s note did not
consider: `library proposals --accept` run three times, for 25, 3 and 15 — it takes
one id — wrote rules 5, 6 and 7, and a rescan derived 149 series, 1,927 works and **1,955 editions**.
`chainsaw-man---v06--2021--cbz` now holds `raw` and `digital-colored-comics`,
and pressing `2` on it draws **the gap screen, at both sizes** — "No
digital-colored-comics page for raw page 1", in ink on black with the display
face on the headline. The chrome was hidden for that run, so neither bar was
drawn; when they are, they are `zIndex: 3` and draw **over** the gap, which
fills the page area's full height beneath them. A borrowed page and a correction still
could not be reached: both need *aligned* editions, and these are unaligned,
so they stay jsdom-only and pass to a later pass.

**One thing that work found.** With the second edition viewed, the readout
carries the edition's name and a verdict, and at 390×844 the row overflows:
`scrollWidth` **402** against `clientWidth` **390**, with the text flush to
both edges instead of inside its 12 px padding. There is no overflow at 1440.
The bar is ③'s; ④ found it only because a two-edition work now exists.
*(This is O141, closed on 2026-11-13 by the phone fixes: its row in
`docs/status.md` says how the line now ends in "…" inside its padding.)*

## O140: the chrome's build cost — 2026-09-21

What §6 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-o140-chrome-build-cost-design.md`
asked for, measured. The app is this branch served by vite against
`taiyaku serve` on the scratch copy of the NAS library
(`target/style-pass/lib/library.db`), driven in Chromium at 390×844 with 4× CPU
throttling — the design's §0 conditions — and opened on the user's iPhone over
the tailnet, where the production build was served by `vite preview` behind
`tailscale serve`. The volume is `akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz`, 237 pages,
`rtl`, in `single` mode, under **desktop emulation at `devicePixelRatio` 1**.
Thumbnails warm for every timing below. The emulation mode is stated because
this same work found the rail drawing a tile 58.16 px wide under desktop
emulation and 68.19 under mobile — "390×844 at 4×" alone does not reproduce
these figures.

**The five numbers, before and after.**

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| first open of the chrome | 274 ms | **87 ms** |
| a later open | 274 ms | **62 ms** (61–70) |
| a page turn, chrome open | 178 ms | **78 ms**, 10 of 10 turns moved |
| a page turn, chrome closed | 37 ms | **33 ms** |
| thumbnail requests on a first open | 101 | **26** |

And what the chrome is made of, shown: **774 elements, 238 images, 237 tiles**
became **155, 34 and 33**.

**The two that are not numbers.** A reader who never shows the chrome — by
`Tab`, by ④'s middle tap, or by starting a correction — still requests **zero**
thumbnails: six page turns with the chrome never mounted, no `/thumb` request.
That is the protection the unmount existed for and the only reason `Chrome`
still renders nothing before its first show. And the fade still plays: opacity
sampled per frame runs 0, 0.163, 0.467, 0.65, 0.836, 0.929, 0.985, 1, against
`modules/motion.ts`'s `transition: opacity ${ms}ms ease` at its default 120.

**The open-chrome page turn is a defect nobody had filed.** At 178 ms against
37 ms closed, a reader who keeps the strip up paid nearly five times the cost
on every turn, on `main`, with no row recording it. Windowing more than halved
it. It was found by profiling rather than by reading, and only because the
profile asked what the chrome costs when it is *not* being opened.

**Two things in the record the profile contradicted**, both now corrected
where they were written: `loading="lazy"` does defer here (101 of 237
thumbnails requested at 390×844 on a 237-tile rail, not all 237), and the
DevTools forced-reflow insight blaming `recenter` is not additive — replacing
`scrollIntoView` with a no-op prevented 103 calls and moved the open cost from
225 ms to 225 ms.

**What the device pass found, and what the gate was not doing.** Seven reviews
across four tasks had passed, and every agent report said "all green" — but
**the gate was not green and had never been run whole**. `reader.css.test.ts`
broke at `ba160157`, the first commit to touch `reader.css` (it added
`--strip-unit` beside `--strip-tile` in a media block whose test required that
block to hold one declaration), and was not fixed until `3b784e93`: 1 failed /
1274 passed in the node project for most of this branch's life, the whole
device pass included. Every dispatch named specific test files rather than a
whole project, so the reports were true of what they had been asked to run;
and when an agent did notice the failure, it checked whether it pre-existed
against another commit *on this branch* — a comparison that cannot tell
"already broken on `main`" from "broken earlier by us" — and concluded,
reasonably and wrongly, that it did. Against that, the user reported on their
own phone that the strip could not be flicked: it scrolled and slid back. Three separate causes came out of that, in order, each
found by measurement and none by reading:

1. **The rail's `load` listener.** `recenter()` on every thumbnail `load`
   pulled the rail back to the current tile. Windowing turned that from a
   settle-once behaviour into a continuous one: before, every tile mounted at
   open so every load happened then; after, scrolling *renders* new tiles whose
   loads fire it mid-flick. Removed — and the reason it existed had already
   gone, because a tile now has a `minWidth` floor and no longer lays out at
   near-zero width until its image decodes. Reproducing it needed a *small*
   scroll (so the current tile stays in the window) on a volume with *cold*
   thumbnails (so loads fire); neither synthetic `TouchEvent`s nor setting
   `scrollLeft` directly could do it, and both reported the code healthy.
2. **The window re-anchoring per frame.** 65 window changes across 181 frames
   in one 1.2 s flick, each rebuilding the tiles. Fixed by re-anchoring only
   when a **spacer** comes within a quarter of the rail's width of the visible
   strip, with that distance floored at 200 px. Two earlier rules failed and
   are recorded because each failed instructively: a drift rule counted in
   tiles and opened a **321 px** blank gap at 1440, because the viewport
   extends forward from the focus tile rather than straddling it; and a rule
   testing the first and last *rendered tiles* fired on nearly every frame,
   because the rail is `row-reverse` for a right-to-left work and the last tile
   in the DOM is the leftmost on screen. Checking both ends does not make a
   test direction-agnostic — it makes one half of it always true.
3. **`--strip-unit` was a constant that cannot be right everywhere.** It said
   54 px. Measured at 390×844 on this machine in this browser: under desktop
   emulation the rail subtracts 15 px of its own height (`offsetHeight` 112,
   `clientHeight` 97), the image draws 81 tall and a loaded tile 58.16 wide;
   under mobile emulation it subtracts nothing, the image draws 96 tall and
   the tile **68.19** — 10.19 px over the nominal the spacers use.
   **What subtracts those 15 px is still not established.** *(O145 has
   since established it, on 2026-10-04: a classic scrollbar on the rail. See
   "O145: what takes 15 px of the rail".)* A classic
   scrollbar is the obvious candidate, but O138 measured this same rail at
   1440×900 at **0 px** — in headless Chromium, where this branch measured in a
   driven, emulated one — recorded that neither this
   machine's Chromium nor the user's desktop shows a classic scrollbar, and
   left an explicit hook: *"If the 15 px returns, that unexplained difference
   is where to start."* It returned during this work and nobody went there —
   a story was written around it instead, in every place the code was
   explained — one of them citing O138 as its authority for the claim O138
   disproves — and it took four passes to clear. The whole-branch review
   caught the contradiction; the first correction missed some places *and*
   invented a new claim (that O138's 1440×900 reading implies a width, when
   it measured only heights); a grep for the phrase missed a site where it
   wrapped across a line break; and two pre-merge claim checks found the
   rest. **The lesson is not the count**, which moved on every pass: a claim
   that nothing tests can be wrong in as many places as it is written, and
   the only thing that found them was reading each one against the file it
   described. The fix never depended on
   the cause: whatever takes the height, a constant cannot be right in both
   conditions, so `Filmstrip` measures the tiles that have drawn and writes
   **their median** into the property, and the floor, the spacers and the
   tiles then agree by construction. The median rather than the first tile
   because an unmarked double-page scan is a one-unit tile drawing at two and
   would otherwise double the value for the session; every tile contributes,
   normalised to one unit, because a one-unit-only sample is **empty** in
   `two` mode — measured in the running app, 0 of 13 loaded tiles there are
   one-unit. Content drift over a flick fell from **31 frames, worst 217 px**
   to **4 frames, worst 64 px**.

**The worst thing this branch produced, and what caught it.** A whole-branch
review found that turning a page with the chrome open, *after* the reader had
flicked the strip, left the strip **blank**. The centring effect did
`setScrolledTo(undefined)` and then called `recenter()` synchronously in the
same body, reading refs that point into the window rendered from the *old*
`scrolledTo`; flick far enough and the new current tile is not in that window,
so all three refs are null and `scrollIntoView` is a silent no-op — and the
effect's dependencies have not changed, so it never runs again. Driven at
390×844: after a flick the window held **pages 115–147 at `scrollLeft`
−8165**; after the turn it rebuilt correctly to **62–94** while `scrollLeft`
stayed **−8165**, with **0 tiles visible**. Fixed with a `pendingRecentre` ref
and a retry effect that runs until it succeeds — deliberately *not* by adding
`scrolledTo` or the window bounds to the centring effect's dependencies, which
would re-centre the rail mid-flick and restore the defect the `load` listener
had just been removed for. Re-verified in the browser: after the turn
`scrollLeft` moves to −4890, seven tiles are visible and the current tile is
on screen.

**No per-task review caught it, and no single commit introduced it.** Before
windowing, a tile that existed was always rendered, so the centring chain was
null only in states with no tile to centre on — never because the tile lay
outside a window. The test that *names* this behaviour
(`Filmstrip.test.tsx`'s "recentres when the same instance's `currentIndex`
changes") uses the file's four-group fixture, which sits wholly inside the
window and cannot reach the case.

**The residual is data, not layout.** Those four remaining jumps are six pages
on this volume whose thumbnails are 160×120 — genuine double-page scans the
sidecar never marked `spread: true`, so `tileUnits` correctly calls them one
unit while they draw at two. Filed as O144.

**Three times on this branch the measurement was the thing that was wrong.**
A settled sweep reported the 321 px gap as "1 px, only at the clamped ends",
because it sampled after the motion rather than during it. A probe reported a
full-width blank that did not exist, because it set its stop flag and then
teleported `scrollLeft` in the next statement, and a frame scheduled earlier
fired in between. And a probe reported every tile as double-width, because it
detected the unit count with `minWidth.includes('* 2')`, which matches the
*border* term `--strip-tile-border) * 2` on every tile — caught only because
it produced an impossible aggregate.

## O134: what a sharper tile costs, measured — 2026-09-22

Steps 1, 2 and 6 of Task 8's brief. Machine: this workstation (AMD Ryzen 9
9950X3D, 16 cores/32 threads, 60 GiB RAM), not the NAS the product deploys to.
Steps 3–5 — the phone pass and `docs/status.md`'s five-part edit, which
cannot be written until that pass has happened — are a separate pass. The
measurements below were taken without touching `docs/status.md`; the test
counts in it were corrected afterwards, on their own, for the reason the gate
gives below.

**The gate.**

```
env -u TAIYAKU_CORPUS NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS=8 RUST_TEST_THREADS=8 scripts/check-all.sh
```

Red, but only at its last step. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, the rustdoc build,
the advisory pedantic clippy pass, and `cargo llvm-cov nextest` all passed —
2236 tests run, 2236 passed, 4 skipped, 93.46% aggregate line coverage, every
file at or above its per-file floor. `scripts/status-test-count.mjs` then
refused: `docs/status.md` states 2231 tests at both of the lines it checks,
against the 2236 this run just recorded. The five are this branch's own
Task 1–7 commits, each of which added tests without the count being updated.
Nothing else in the gate found anything.

**Corrected separately, and the gate re-run green.** The count is not the row's
prose and does not wait on the phone, so it was fixed on its own rather than
held for the five-part edit: 2231 → 2236 at both checked sites. Fixing it
surfaced a staleness **nothing gates** — `status-test-count.mjs` checks the
Rust figure alone, and the web clause beside it was already wrong before this
branch began, claiming 1,245 `node` / 1,070 `jsdom` / "seventy" `browser`
against a true 1,282 / 1,096 / 75 at `main`. Re-measured rather than
incremented, per that clause's own history of drifting:

```
npx vitest run --project node --reporter=default     →  66 files, 1,291 tests
npx vitest run --project jsdom --reporter=default     →  49 files, 1,096 tests
npx vitest run --project browser --reporter=default   →   7 files,    77 tests
```

A later commit on this branch added one more Rust test, and both Rust sites
moved again, to **2237**, which is what `docs/status.md` reads now. The web
figures did not move with it: that commit changed an assertion inside an
existing `it()` rather than adding one.

1,291 + 1,096 = 2,387 is the figure the clause states, with the browser
project's 77 counted separately as it always has been. The re-run of the whole
gate after that edit ends `all green, except NOT MEASURED: standing corpus
checks (TAIYAKU_CORPUS unset)`, exit 0; the corpus job run on its own
afterwards is 24 passed, 0 failed.

**The cache measurement.** `akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz`, 237 pages, the
same edition O140 profiled, served by this branch's own release build:

```
cargo build --release
./target/release/taiyaku serve --db target/style-pass/lib/library.db \
  --cache <a directory created empty for this measurement, outside the repo> \
  --addr 127.0.0.1:8489
```

`cache_root.rs`'s `--cache` flag pins the root (`Resolution::Flag`), so the
figures below are this run's and nothing else's: the directory held nothing
before the first request (`find <dir> -mindepth 1` printed nothing), and
nothing outside it moved during the run — neither the repository's own
`.taiyaku-cache/` nor `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/taiyaku` gained a file dated today,
checked afterward with `find <dir> -newermt '2026-09-22 00:00:00'` against
both. The scratch library ships one account (`local`, `admin`), and every
route — including the plain 160 px tile — answers `401` without a session, so
a password was set (`taiyaku library user password local --db
target/style-pass/lib/library.db`) and a cookie taken from `POST
/api/session` (with a matching `Origin` header, which the session route
requires) before driving any request.

For each of `cover.rs`'s `TILE_LONG_EDGES` — 160, 320, 480 — every one of the
edition's 237 pages was fetched once, cold, one request at a time, in page
order:

```
GET /api/works/akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz/raw/pages/{0..236}/thumb?w={edge}
```

| rung | files | total bytes | total | mean/tile | cold pass | ratio to 160 px |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 160 px | 237 | 1,647,213 | 1.57 MiB | 6,950 B | 4.26 s | 1.00× |
| 320 px | 237 | 5,426,877 | 5.18 MiB | 22,898 B | 5.14 s | **3.29×** |
| 480 px | 237 | 11,025,981 | 10.52 MiB | 46,523 B | 6.50 s | **6.69×** |

All three rungs held at once — every size a dense screen might ask for,
cached together for this one edition: 711 files, 18,100,071 bytes, 17.26 MiB.

**This replaces §8's extrapolation; it does not confirm it.** The design doc
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-o134-sharper-strip-tile-design.md`, §8 item 1)
guessed 320 px near 3.6 MiB and 480 near 7.2 MiB per 195-page edition against
O11's 1.12 MiB at 160 — ratios of 3.21× and 6.43×, extrapolated from two of
O133's points on a different edition's cover. The ratios measured here, on
this edition's own 237 tiles at all three rungs, are higher at both: 3.29×
and 6.69×, about 2% and 4% over the guess. The guess's assumed shape — bytes
growing as area to the 0.85 — holds up: solved from these measured ratios,
bytes here grow as edge^1.72–1.74, i.e. area^0.86–0.87, close to what was
assumed. It is the absolute prediction that undershot, not the shape of the
curve. **O11's row needs the ratios measured above, not §8's guess.**
*O11's row stopped carrying this edition's sizes when it narrowed to its Stump
half on 2026-11-10; O134's row carries them, with the ratios.*

The cold-pass wall-clock is a sequential loop of separate `curl` invocations
(one TCP connection per request) against this workstation, not the NAS; it is
a cold-generation figure — every request a cache miss, so each pays a resize —
not a warm-serving or network benchmark.

**The mutation sweep.**

```
scripts/mutants.sh --since main
```

23 mutants tested in 5 minutes: 13 caught, 4 missed, 6 unviable. The diff this
sweep covers is exactly `cover.rs` and `routes.rs` (`git diff main...HEAD
--stat -- '*.rs'`: those two files, 84 and 49 lines, plus their `tests.rs`
files, which cargo-mutants does not mutate). All 23 mutants come from those
two files; nothing in the diff went untested.

The 13 caught are the branch's functional core: `can_stream`,
`refuse_if_cannot_stream`, `tile_edge`, `get_thumb`, `cached_or_generated_thumb`
and `thumb_cache_path` each have a mutant a test catches — the sizing gate and
the fallback both have an assertion behind them, not just a line that runs.

**All 4 missed and all 6 unviable are the same ten lines**: the `const _: ()
= { ... }` block below `TILE_LONG_EDGES` that asserts, at compile time, that
`TILE_LONG_EDGES` and `COVER_LONG_EDGES` share no value (its own doc comment
says why: `get_thumb` tries the cover branch first, so an overlapping value
would take page 0 down the cover route instead of `tile_edge` and silently
break "a tile is always JPEG" for that one page). This is a compile-time
double loop, not runtime logic, and every mutant in it is a mutation of the
two loop guards or their increments:

```
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:86:13: replace < with ==   MISSED
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:86:13: replace < with >    MISSED
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:88:17: replace < with ==   MISSED
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:88:17: replace < with >    MISSED
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:86:13: replace < with <=   unviable
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:88:17: replace < with <=   unviable
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:95:15: replace += with -=  unviable
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:95:15: replace += with *=  unviable
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:97:11: replace += with *=  unviable
crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:97:11: replace += with -=  unviable
```

None of the 4 missed are in `docs/mutants-baseline.md` yet (the script:
"4 survivor(s) this run"). **They are equivalent mutants, not an untested
branch.** `==` and `>` both turn `while i < LEN` into a guard that is false
at `i = 0`, so the loop body — and every `assert!` inside it — never runs.
Since the real arrays already satisfy the invariant (the assertions never
fire in the unmutated code either), a build that skips them compiles
identically and every other test passes identically: nothing observable
distinguishes the mutant from the original, so no test — present or
plausible — could catch it without deliberately reintroducing an overlap and
checking that the *build* then fails, which is a compile-fail test this
project does not otherwise write.

**The 6 unviable are the same block's `<=` and its two increments failing to
build**, and reading one confirms why rather than assuming it: the `<=`
mutant at `cover.rs:86:13`, logged verbatim,

```
error[E0080]: index out of bounds: the length is 3 but the index is 3
  --> crates/taiyaku-serve/src/cover.rs:90:17
   |
90 |                 TILE_LONG_EDGES[i] != COVER_LONG_EDGES[j],
```

— `i <= TILE_LONG_EDGES.len()` lets `i` reach `3`, and `TILE_LONG_EDGES[3]` is
out of bounds for a 3-element array, so `const` evaluation panics and the
crate fails to compile. **The four increment mutants do not fail that way**,
and saying they did was wrong — compiled standalone to find out, since the
sweep reports only the verdict:

- `+=` → `-=` underflows rather than going negative, because these are
  `usize`: `error[E0080]: attempt to compute ⁠0_usize - 1_usize⁠, which would
  overflow`.
- `+=` → `*=` does not move the index at all — `j *= 1` is `j` — so the loop
  never ends: `error: constant evaluation is taking a long time`, under
  `#[deny(long_running_const_eval)]`.

Three different compiler errors, one per shape. **For this particular check
the compiler is the test**, and it rejected six of the ten mutations.

**What the six unviable results do and do not evidence.** They show the block
is genuinely const-evaluated — a block the compiler never ran could not fail
to build. They do **not** show the assertion inside it is the right one; an
unviable mutant is a mutant that never ran. That the guard fires on a real
overlap is a separate check, made the same way: the same block with an
overlapping value in both arrays gives `error[E0080]: evaluation panicked`.

**What this sweep cannot see.** `git diff main...HEAD --stat -- '*.ts'
'*.tsx'` shows **360 changed lines across ten files** — `tileSize.ts` (new),
`Filmstrip.tsx`, `ProposalRow.tsx`, `api.ts`, their tests, and
`styles/reader.css.test.ts` — the other half
of this branch's logic, entirely outside cargo-mutants' reach, which mutates
Rust only. Those files' own coverage is whatever `npx vitest` gives them; this
sweep says nothing about it either way.

### O134: the device pass — 2026-09-22

The reader on the user's own iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS Safari over the tailnet,
against **the production build** (`pnpm -C web run build`, served by
`vite preview` behind `tailscale serve`, which supplies the TLS iOS wants) and
a release `taiyaku serve` on the scratch copy of the NAS library
(`target/style-pass/lib/library.db`). Volume: `akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz`.

**What the phone asked for, read off the cache rather than a request log.** The
tile cache names every file for the long edge it holds
(`cover.rs`'s `thumb_keyed_path`: `{sha}-p{offset}-{edge}v{version}.jpg`), so
the sizes served are a directory listing. For this volume's member, during the
pass:

| written | tiles | long edge |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 02:16, the first burst | **26** | 320 px |
| 02:26, reading on | 14 | 320 px |

The 02:16 burst is the first chrome open rather than an inference from order: this member had no
320 px tile cached before this pass, so the first show is the first miss, and all 26 share one
minute's timestamp.

**Zero tiles at 160 px were written.** The one 160 px tile this member has is
dated 2026-09-09, from a session months before this branch. So the phone took
the 320 px rung and nothing else, which is what `requestedTileEdge(96, 3)`
answers: the strip's tile is 96 CSS px tall below the 900 px breakpoint, a 3×
screen wants 288 device pixels, and 320 is the first rung at or above it.

**26 on a first open is O140's own number.** That row measured a windowed rail
requesting 26 thumbnails on a first open against 101 unwindowed (its table,
"thumbnail requests on a first open | 101 | **26**"). The same 26 arriving here,
on real hardware rather than under emulation, matches that count exactly.

**It is not a check on the window itself.** The window is 33 tiles, fixed by
`tiles.ts`'s `windowMargin`; 26 is the smaller number that `loading="lazy"`
did not defer at that viewport, and the iPhone's Safari viewport is not the
390 CSS px O140 emulated. Two viewports agreeing on 26 is worth recording and
is not evidence about the window's size.

**What the user actually reported, which is not "sharp".** Asked whether the
strip looked sharp, they answered: *"by 'pretty sharp' it's hard to tell on a
phone because the thumbnails are so tiny. I can't really differentiate so I
would say they are sharp enough as is."*

Record that as it stands rather than rounding it up. **The improvement is real
and measured; it is not one the user could see.** Before this branch a 96 CSS
px tile on a 3× screen was given 160 px of image for the 288 device pixels it
draws into — 1.8× upscaled. It is now given 320, so nothing is upscaled. Both
states pass this reader's eye at this size.

**What that is evidence for, and what it is not.** It closes O134's own
question — the row asked whether the user minds the softness, they chose the
sharper tile on 2026-09-20, and the softness is gone by measurement. It does
**not** establish that a sharper strip tile is worth its price generally: the
cache cost this buys is 3.29× per edition at 320 px (measured above), paid for
a difference this device's own owner could not pick out. Any future proposal of
the same shape — a 480 px rung for a 3× desktop, or the same treatment
elsewhere — should be asked to show the difference is visible before it is
asked to show it is cheap.

### ⑤a: the device pass — 2026-09-23

The user's iPhone, iOS Safari over the tailnet, against the **production
build** — `npm run build`, then `vite preview` behind `tailscale serve`,
proxying `/api` to a `taiyaku serve` on a **copy** of the real library. The
original `library.db` was checksummed before and after and is unchanged. Two
questions, because two things on this branch are invisible to every other
check available here.

**Why neither could be settled on the development machine.** `base.css`'s
16 px floor lives inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`, and driven Chromium is
`pointer: fine` — the media query never engages, so a 390×844 browser pass
comes back clean whether the floor holds or not. `scripts/check-all.sh` does
not render at all. A real phone is the only instrument for this.

**1. ⑤a's own Critical, C2 — fixed.** The whole-branch review found
`.field input` at `0.8rem` beating that floor, because the floor is written
at `:where()` and so carries **zero** specificity while `.field input`
carries (0,1,1). That put all nine rule-form controls under 16 px, which is
what makes iOS Safari zoom the document on focus — the defect ④'s device
pass already recorded once, where signing in left the page zoomed and a
pinch was the only way back. **Tapping any field on the Rules screen no
longer zooms.** The fix is `var(--text-ui)` plus an equal-specificity
`(pointer: coarse)` companion at `max(16px, var(--text-ui))`, written after
the rule it corrects so it wins the tie.

**2. O151 — reproduced.** Building the gate for C2 surfaced the same defeat
one stylesheet over. `base.css`'s floor is scoped to `:where(.library,
.login)` and **the reader is neither**, so it never reached
`.reader-dialog-panel` — 14 px, handed to every control inside it by that
panel's own `font: inherit`, which is what `settingsFields.tsx` fills with
`type="number"` boxes for prefetch and motion. **Tapping one zooms the
document**, and it stays zoomed. Fixed on its own branch rather than here,
because the reader is not ⑤a's screen.

**And a third thing, which was on no checklist.** Typing the account name on
the login screen, the keyboard capitalised it: `local` became `Local`.
`user.name` is `TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` with no `COLLATE NOCASE`, so
`account::by_name`'s `WHERE name = ?1` compares under SQLite's BINARY
default — against this library, `local` returns 1 row and `Local` returns 0.
So **every iPhone was typing a name that could not match, on the one screen
there is no way past**, and nothing in the suite could see it because no
test types with a phone keyboard. `autocapitalize="none"` with `autocorrect`
and `spellcheck` off, on the login field and on the add-account field; fixed
on its own branch and re-verified on the device.

That third finding is the argument for running these on hardware rather than
under emulation. It was not what the pass was for, and it was the worst
thing the pass found.

### ⑤b: the device pass — 2026-09-24

The user's iPhone, iOS Safari over the tailnet, against the **production
build** — `npm run build`, then `vite preview` behind `tailscale serve`,
proxying `/api` to a `taiyaku serve` on a **copy** of the real library. The
original `library.db` was checksummed before and after: `d5ebc0c2…`,
unchanged. Five questions, and all five came back clean.

**1 and 2 — the 16 px floor, on the two screens ⑤b created controls for.**
Tapping *Edition key* and *Scan interval (seconds)* on Configuration → Roots,
and *Name*, *Password* and the *Role* select under "Add an account" on
Configuration → Users: **no zoom** in either place. This is the check nothing
on the development machine can perform. `base.css`'s floor lives inside
`@media (pointer: coarse)` and driven Chromium is `pointer: fine`, so the
media query never engages and a 390×844 browser pass comes back clean whether
the floor holds or not — which is exactly how ⑤a shipped C2 and how O151 hid
from a gate built to catch it. ⑤b put every one of these controls behind
`.field`, whose three coupled selector lists include the coarse companion;
this is the evidence that the companion is doing its job on real hardware
rather than only satisfying `base.css.test.ts`.

**3 — the whole-branch review's Critical, at a real 390 px.** After a real
scan on the phone, *"no scroll sideways — nothing exceeds the width of the
page"*. The defect was a rendered scan report putting 2 px of horizontal
scroll on the document: `.scan-report dl` was a descendant selector and so
also caught the nested `<dl>` of unreadable causes inside a `<dd>`, where
`minmax(16rem, 1fr)` gave it a hard 256 px floor — 344 px of content in a
309 px row. Fixed by scoping the grid to `.scan-report > section > dl`. The
fix had been measured only in desktop Chromium at a simulated 390 until now.

**4 — the zeros recede and nothing is hidden.** Confirmed on screen. The
report still draws all 47 facts; 38 read `0` or `no` on the scan measured
here, and they sit at `--muted` while the rest take `--text`. O90 closed by
making this report *name* what it skipped, and that is intact.

**5 — `--danger` is on the verb and not on Cancel.** Confirmed. The
distinction matters because the obvious rule, `button:first-of-type`, would
have painted Cancel: both removal blocks render their confirm button only
once the cost has loaded, so until then Cancel is the only button there.

Nothing else looked wrong to the user.


### ⑤c: the browser pass — 2026-09-25

The branch served by `vite` against a `taiyaku serve` on a **copy** of the real
library. The original `library.db` was checksummed before and after —
`d5ebc0c2378650356115a8cce637e50dc5b4ab7f7cc8f388553cadd575a59e67` — and is
unchanged. 68 captures in `target/style-pass-5c/pass/`: 36 whole screens, nine
rows at 390×844 and 1440×900 in Paper and in Ink, plus 32 crops.

**No sideways scroll anywhere.** `scrollWidth === clientWidth` on the document
*and* on `<main>`, all 36 combinations, with the inbox checked **expanded as
well as collapsed** — the expanded panel is the one carrying absolute paths.
Worth one line for anyone comparing against passes ①–④: headed Chrome's
scrollbar makes the 390 px layout viewport **375 px**, so these read 375/375
where the earlier passes read 390/390. Stricter, not weaker, but a different
number.

**The four places the token sweep moved pixels, all measured and all kept.**
The evidence panel's fact rows went from 0.8 px of vertical padding to 4 —
27 px rows, four a side, a 108 px list. The collapsed row's subject-to-`↳`
gap is exactly 4.00 px, up from 1.6. The state pills are exactly 34.0 px,
down from 37.2, with the three kind tabs on one line at both widths. Corners
are 2 px on cards, buttons and account cards, with pills and badges still
999 px.

**What it found, and it is on this branch's own screen.** In Ink the pressed
`Open` pill and the `strong` badge are the same object. Checked in the
stylesheet rather than off the pixels: the two rules carry the same three
declarations — `--accent` border, `--accent` fill, `--on-accent` text — in a
different order and in different files, each taking its 999 px corner from its
own base rule rather than from the rule that fills it. Not byte-identical, as
a first draft of this note said; identical in every way that reaches a
screen. A thing you
press and a thing you read, drawn alike. Both rules predate this branch;
what made it visible is this branch, because giving the filter row three
distinct treatments is what put a control and a verdict within a screenful
of each other. Drawn three ways and settled with the user: the verdict is
outlined now, `--accent` as text on the row's ground, which is 5.35:1 on
Paper and 6.13:1 on Ink. Filled stays the mark of pressable, and the weak
badge was outlined all along, so the two verdicts read as a pair.

**Two figures the PR body must not take from elsewhere.** `/config/backup`'s
rows measure **68 px at 390 px**; the 88 px recorded during Task 7 is the
*coarse-pointer* figure, and stating it as a width claim would be wrong. And
the reader's **Settings** panel is byte-identical in Paper and Ink by design —
`.reader` sets `color-scheme: dark` — so its four capture files are two
images, which is correct rather than a capture error. The **Account** panel's
four are four distinct images, and the difference is a clock: 428 and 412
pixels differ in one region, which cropped reads `last seen …22:27:13` against
`…22:26:11`. Same design, different minute. A claim that all eight were two
images would have been wrong, and only cropping the differing region showed
which.

**Two things confirmed rather than found.** The inbox's three filter controls
read as three different kinds of control at both widths in both themes; and
the Account panel is indistinguishable in weight from Settings opened beside
it (`pass/crops/panels-side-by-side-*.png`).

**Not attempted here, deliberately.** The 44 px touch floor: driven Chromium
is `pointer: fine`, so that media query never engages and a pass like this
one says nothing about it either way. Its figures were taken separately in a
Chromium context with `hasTouch` and `isMobile` set, which reports
`(pointer: coarse)` true and `(pointer: fine)` absent.

### ⑤c: the device pass — 2026-09-25

**Why a phone and not another Chromium run.** The browser pass above ends by
saying what it could not reach: driven Chromium is `pointer: fine`, so the
44 px floor §12.4a builds never engages and 68 captures say nothing about it
either way. A separate Chromium context with `hasTouch` and `isMobile` set
does report `(pointer: coarse)`, and that is what Task 7's figures were taken
in — but a synthesised coarse pointer is a media query answered, not a thumb
on glass.

**And the split is not the one that flatters the device pass.** Only two of
what follows strictly *required* a phone: the flash, which needs real network
latency, and the confirmation that iOS Safari declines to zoom. Every other
finding was available to the synthesised context and was not found there — the
pill skew was measured in Chromium and argued away, and the 54-versus-44 split
was under a measurement Task 7 took and read past. So the case for a device
pass here is not that it reaches what a driven browser cannot. It is that a
person looking at a screen asks questions no assertion was written to ask.

**The rig.** A production build behind `vite preview --port 4173`, with the
tailnet supplying the TLS iOS requires: `tailscale serve --set-path /` onto
the preview and `--set-path /api` onto a `taiyaku serve` on `:8497`, reachable
at `https://davey-endeavor.walrus-census.ts.net/` on the account `local`.
Against a copy of the real library, not the original — same
`d5ebc0c2…a59e67` checksum as the browser pass, verified unchanged after.

**One question withdrawn before it was sent.** The plan had the user open the
reader's Account *panel* on the phone and compare it with Settings. They
cannot: the panel is reached by pressing `A` through `keyPlan` and has no
pointer control at all. So §12.5's panel half is browser-tested only, and
that is a limit of this pass rather than a gap in the panel — worth writing
down because the obvious reading of "the account screen was device-tested" is
that both placements were, and only one was.

**1. The state pills were not optically centred.** *"the text inside the
pills isn't centered but otherwise the sizing is good"* — so the floor is
right and the ink inside it is not. Fixed in `bf5d6748`, 6 px of bottom
padding, scoped to the pills.

The methodology half is worth more than the fix. I measured the skew at +6 px
in Chromium, then talked myself out of it in the write-up — argued it was
"within 1 px by cap-to-baseline" and therefore not real. The user's own
screenshot settled it: "Accepted" 17.5 px above the ink and 11.9 below,
"Dismissed" 17.5 and 14.9, in a 44 px pill. That is +5.6 and +2.6, and the
first measurement was right. **The lesson is not "measure twice"** — I had
the right number and reasoned it away, which no amount of remeasuring
catches. A measurement that disagrees with a model of how type sits in a box
is evidence against the model.

One thing checked back in Chromium afterwards, because it would have changed
the fix: `line-height` is not the lever. 24 px to 16 px moved the ink zero pixels — the floor sets
the box height, so the line box has slack at either value.

**2. Every control in a user's card on `/config/users` greys when one
checkbox is toggled.** Filed as O159, not fixed: it is behaviour, which spec
§6 reserves. The user reported the scope as the whole screen — *"it's all the
checkboxes on that page"* — and that is right for the library it was seen in,
which holds **one** account. `saving` lives in `UserRow` and `Users.tsx`
renders one card per account, so with a second account only the touched card
greys. Worth the correction because the first draft of O159 wrote the
observation down as the mechanism.

The reason it is invisible on a desk is the reason it is visible on a phone:
`settled()` holds the lock until the list *reload* comes back, not until the
write answers, and over the tailnet that is long enough to watch. **And the
obvious fix is refused in writing already.** `settled`'s own doc comment
records why the lock covers the whole row — the grant checkbox sends a whole
list, so a second tick inside that window computes the new grants from the
pre-patch `user.roots` and silently revokes the first. The first draft of
O159 proposed scoping `saving` per control, which would have put that data
loss back on exactly the control the row is about. Three of that draft's
figures were also wrong; the commit message on `ac2add0f` has them.

**3. Three field defects, from one sentence.** *"it doesn't zoom but the text
looks a bit weird next to the input boxes. it overlaps also when you tap a box
and it gets highlighted."* Two separate facts:

- *It doesn't zoom* is ⑤a's 16 px floor confirmed on the device it was built
  for. That gate has only ever been checked by reading computed styles; this
  is the first time a real iOS Safari declined to zoom into a focused field.
- *Weird, and overlaps when highlighted* is three defects, fixed in
  `593eb94b`: a focus ring 4 px outside the border box against 2.4 px of
  label clearance on all five screens using the shared `.field` block; the
  same ring clipping the label *below* it on `/account`, where two fields
  stack with no gap; and a 44 px floor that was a floor on *content*, so
  every `<input>` rendered at 54 px beside a `<select>` at 44.

The third is the one a coarse-pointer Chromium context could have caught and
did not, because Task 7 measured `min-height` rather than rendered height.
The first two need a focus ring actually painted.

**4. The inbox as a whole.** *"proposals as a whole is alright"* — the
confirmation §12.3 was after: three filter controls that read as three kinds
of control, on the screen where they matter, at the width they matter on.

### ⑤c: the whole-branch review — 2026-09-25

**It had not run.** Ten task reviews, three claim-check rounds on the prose,
a browser pass and a device pass had all passed, and the gate this project
keeps for last was still outstanding when the PR went up. It found **two
Criticals**, and neither was reachable from a single task's diff.

**C1 — the Account panel's text boxes rendered at 14 px under a coarse
pointer, under O151's own floor.** `reader.css`'s floor was `(0,1,0)` and won
its tie by *sitting after* the `font: inherit` it corrects — the comment said
so in as many words. ⑤c then put the panel's controls on `.reader-field`,
whose own `font: inherit` is also `(0,1,0)` and sits about a hundred lines
*later*, so it took the tie back. Measured in Chromium at 390×844 with
`hasTouch`: the panel's three boxes computed **14 px** while every admin-screen
box in the same run computed 16. On `main` those inputs inherited the
document's 16, so the branch took them *below* a floor built on hardware two
PRs earlier.

The fix names `.reader-field` in the floor's prelude at `(0,2,0)`, so it wins
wherever either rule sits. **A floor that depends on being last is a floor the
next rule removes silently** — and the test that guarded it asserted the
source order, so it passed the whole time. That test now pins the specificity
instead, and its old name is in the diff as the record of what was being
guarded.

**C2 — the floor's gate could not see a selector narrowed by a prefix.** The
`inRule` helper anchored a selector to its `{`, which stops a suffix
(`button.nope`) and not a prefix: `.account-wide` still matched inside
`.config .account-wide`. The head comment claimed the class of defect was
closed and watched. Four narrowings passed that way, one of them the exact
defect the comment named. Both ends are anchored now, and three hand
mutations that previously passed were watched red against a control run
first: `.account-wide` → 3 failed, `.proposals .checks label` → 2, and
`.editor-actions .export` → 2, from a control of 31 passed.

**And the first attempt to watch those mutations was itself wrong**, which is
worth more than the fix. Two of three "survived" — until the diff showed the
mutation had landed on the *base* `.account-wide` rule at line 1793, because
the harness located the coarse block with an `indexOf` that found an earlier
one. `admin.css` has two `(pointer: coarse)` blocks and only the second is
the floor. Against the right block all three reddened. A survivor list read
before the mutation site is checked is fiction.

**I1 — two of the three underlined one-of-N rows took the 44 px floor.**
§12.8 excludes `.config-nav` on a measurement: 44 px puts the underline
12.5 px below the word and takes the strip from 29 to 49. `.proposal-tabs`
and `.preview-tabs` wear the same look and are `<button>`s, so the floor's
`button` prelude reached them where `.config-nav`'s `<a>`s escaped it.
Measured together at 390 coarse: 44/49 against 20/24. Settled with the user —
both are excluded now, so the same measurement governs all three, and they
join `.config-nav` in O157.

**I2 — the pill fix from the device pass was overcorrecting**, found
independently by the review and by the second claim check. It has its own
note below.

### ⑤c: the pill fix was measuring the wrong noun — 2026-09-25

The device pass's first finding was that the state pills' text was not
centred. The fix shipped as `padding-block: 0 6px` and was wrong, and the way
it was wrong is the one this project keeps writing down: **the measurement
was right and the noun was wrong.**

"Open" and "Accepted" carry a `p`. "Dismissed" does not. The recorded
before-figures — 17.5 px above the ink and 11.9 below on one pill, 17.5 and
14.9 on another — were read as two different skews. They are one skew and a
3 px descender. All three words share a single cap-top, which is what a
reader sees as the word's position.

Tuned against the ink bounding box of the two descender words, the correction
came out at 3 px when the real error was 1.5. Measured in Chromium at 390×844
with `hasTouch` against the built stylesheet, cap-top offset from the pill's
optical centre:

| `padding-block` | Open | Accepted | Dismissed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `4px 4px` (base) | +1.5 | +1.5 | +1.5 |
| `0 6px` (shipped) | −1.5 | −1.5 | −1.5 |
| `2.5px 5.5px` | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |

So the shipped rule turned a 1.5 px error into a 1.5 px error of the opposite
sign, and left "Dismissed" — the one word with nothing below the baseline —
sitting 15.0 above and 18.0 below. `2.5px 5.5px` keeps the total padding at
8 px, so only the content box's *position* moves, by the whole 1.5.

**Why the original after-measurement missed it**: it was taken on "Open" and
"Accepted", both descender words, and reported as bbox skew. Two measurements
of the same wrong quantity agree with each other.

### O149: the Provenance table at 390px

under the root" was selected on /config/rules and the Provenance tab opened.

**The first two could not draw a classic scrollbar.** They were launched
with Playwright's defaults, and Playwright 1.62.1 adds `--hide-scrollbars` to
every headless Chromium launch (`playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js`,
l.43070). For the desktop context that 0 is the flag's doing, as the third
context shows. The touch context was not run without the flag, so what its 0
owes to the flag and what to mobile emulation is not separated here. The
third was launched with `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--hide-scrollbars']` and
differs from the second in nothing else. It was measured at `90ea42fd`, whose
only change to the app is a comment. The second was taken twice, once beside
the first and again beside the third as a control, and gave the same figures
both times.

| | touch (`hasTouch`, `isMobile`), flag on | desktop, flag on | desktop, flag off |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches` | `true` | `false` | `false` |
| `table.provenance tbody tr` | 224 | 224 | 224 |
| `<th>` | file, series, volume, chapter | file, series, volume, chapter | file, series, volume, chapter |
| `table.provenance` width | 368 | 368 | 368 |
| its `.table-scroll`'s `clientWidth` | 358 | 358 | 343 |
| its `.table-scroll`'s `scrollWidth` | 368 | 368 | 368 |
| `innerWidth − clientWidth` (the scrollbar) | 0 | 0 | 15 |

`p.unset` read, in all three: "edition_key, kind, language and title are not
set for any of these 224 files."

The four fields empty in every row are gone from the table and named in one

**The design's figures, not this run's.** The admin follow-ups design

| "An administrator cannot take their own admin role away; …" | `li.user-row` | 12px | `rgb(107, 97, 81)` |

| "C4 §4: there is no self-service registration — …" | `form.add-user` | 12px | `rgb(107, 97, 81)` |

All three render alike. The design's §0 records the add-account one, before
the change, at 16px `rgb(35, 30, 23)`.

### O155: the inbox

`GET /api/library/proposals?state=open&min_score=0` answered 200 with 35
proposals, every one `open`: **18** at score 0, **13** at 1, **3** at 2 and
**1** at 3. Its `counts` were `attach-chapters` 1 and `edition-of` 34.

At /proposals, desktop context, 1440×900, counting `.proposal-list li` and
the `.score` chips by word:

| "Show weak proposals" | Rows | `strong` | `maybe` | `weak` | Tabs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unticked | 17 | 4 | 13 | 0 | All 17, Attach Chapters 1, Edition Of 16 |
| ticked | 35 | 4 | 13 | 18 | All 35, Attach Chapters 1, Edition Of 34 |

Each word is one score band: 4 `strong` is the 3 at score 2 and the 1 at
score 3, 13 `maybe` is score 1, and 18 `weak` is score 0. The default view
shows no row that says `weak`, and ticking the box adds exactly the 18 that
do.

### O159: the `can_download` checkbox's fill

Desktop context, 1440×900, /config/users, on `local`'s `can_download`
box: checked, drawn 13×13 at (269, 280.703), computed `accent-color`
`rgb(176, 54, 29)`. Each state was read from a 1×1 `page.screenshot` clip
at the box's centre, (275, 287), decoded with ImageMagick 7.1.2-31.

| State | Centre pixel |
|---|---|
| 1. as rendered | 249, 238, 236 |
| 2. `disabled = true` | 233, 232, 231 |
| 3. that, plus `input[type=checkbox]:disabled { accent-color: var(--accent); opacity: 1; filter: none; }` | 233, 232, 231 |
| 4. `disabled = false`, `aria-disabled="true"` | 249, 238, 236 |

**The centre pixel is on the tick, not the fill.** A 13×13 clip of the whole
box, taken with each reading, puts the centre on the tick's anti-aliased
edge, which is why it is near white. The fill beside it, at clip pixel
(2, 4), reads 176, 54, 29 in states 1 and 4, which is the accent exactly, and
206, 205, 203 in states 2 and 3. ImageMagick's `compare -metric AE` counts 0
differing pixels between the whole-box clips of 1 and 4, and 0 between 2
and 3.

So `disabled` changes the tick and the fill both, the three properties on
`:disabled` change no pixel of either, and `aria-disabled` without
`disabled` changes no pixel of the enabled box.

What this does not show: any browser but Chromium. O159 was reported from
an iPhone, and this does not measure its WebKit.

### O157: what the enable label costs in layout

/config/rules, the library's four rules, at `9c194cb0`, except the "before"
row of the desktop table, taken at `0e4ceb75` before `.rule-row .enable {
display: flex }` existed. Four contexts: desktop 1440×900, and touch 390×844
with `hasTouch` and `isMobile` (`(pointer: coarse)` matched `true` there and
`false` on desktop), each in a default launch, which adds
`--hide-scrollbars`, and again in one launched with `ignoreDefaultArgs:
['--hide-scrollbars']`. The two launches gave the same figure in every cell
below. In both, `innerWidth − clientWidth` was 0 at both sizes: this page
drew no scrollbar either way, so the flag decides nothing here.

"Without" is the same page with each `label.enable` replaced by its own
input by script (`label.replaceWith(input)`). That is `main`'s markup for
these rows: the label is the branch's only change to `RuleList`'s row, and
`.rule-row .enable` its only rules.

**Touch, 390×844.** The label is 44×44, computed `display: grid` (the
coarse rule's `inline-grid`, blockified as an item of the flex row), and
the box inside it 24×24 either way. `.rule-name`'s `line-height` is 24px.

| Rule | `.rule-name` height, with / without | `.select` width | Row height | Box's offset in its row (left, top) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| series from the first directory under the root | 48 / 48 | 184 / 197 | 85 / 85 | (42.5, 19) / (36, 12) |
| volume from the name, via taiyaku_read::volume_number | 96 / 72 | 184 / 197 | 133 / 109 | (42.5, 19) / (36, 12) |
| chapter from the name, via taiyaku_read::chapter_number | 96 / 72 | 184 / 197 | 133 / 109 | (42.5, 19) / (36, 12) |
| series from the filename where it repeats it | 48 / 48 | 184 / 197 | 85 / 85 | (42.5, 19) / (36, 12) |

The label takes 13px of width from every rule's name, and the two longer
names wrap one line more, 24px taller, which is the whole of their rows'
growth: `.mechanism` was 18px tall in every row, with and without. The box
is drawn at 24×24 either way, 6.5px further right and 7px lower.

**Desktop, 1440×900.** The same in all four rows:

| | Box's offset in its row (left, top), with the label | Without | The label |
|---|---|---|---|
| before, `0e4ceb75` | (36, 15) | (36, 12) | computed `display: block`, 20×24 |
| after, `9c194cb0` | (36, 12) | (36, 12) | computed `display: flex`, 20×19 |

Before, the label had no rule outside the coarse block and measured 20×24
around the 13×13 box, which sat 3px lower than without it. With
`display: flex` the box sits where it does with no label.
Nothing else in the row moved on desktop: `.select` was 202px wide, and the

### O157: the overlap check, as the design's §2.4 specifies

At `9c194cb0`, touch 390×844 (`hasTouch`, `isMobile`; `(pointer: coarse)`
`true` on all three screens), in a default launch and again with
`ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--hide-scrollbars']`. For every grown target on the
screen, from `.config-nav a`, `.preview-tabs > button`,
`.proposal-tabs > button` and `label.enable`: its 44px rectangle, centred on
the item's `getBoundingClientRect()` and `max(width, 44)` by
`max(height, 44)`. Each rectangle was tested for intersection, an overlap of
more than 0px on both axes, against the `getBoundingClientRect()` of every
visible control in the document: every `a`, `button`, `input`, `select`,
`textarea`, `label` and `summary` with a non-zero box and not
`visibility: hidden`, excluding the item itself, its descendants and its
ancestors. So a row's items were tested against one another, and controls
outside `main` were tested too. Every rectangle on a screen was read in one
pass, with no scroll between (`scrollY` 0).

The rectangle is the `::after`'s own size. For every tab item,
`getComputedStyle(item, '::after')` gave the width and height the rectangle
used: `44px` by `44px` for the items narrower than 44, and the item's own
width by `44px` for the rest. The enable label has no `::after`; its
rectangle is its own 44×44 box.

| Screen | Grown targets | Controls tested | Intersections |
|---|---|---|---|
| /config/rules | 4 `.config-nav a`, 4 `.preview-tabs > button`, 4 `label.enable` | 31 | 0 |
| /proposals | 3 `.proposal-tabs > button` | 45 | 0 |
| /config/users | 4 `.config-nav a` | 81, then 82 | 0 |

Both launches gave these figures, except that /config/users had one more
control in the second. Each sign-in adds a session to `local` and a Revoke
button with it: two consecutive sign-ins, checked for this, drew 39 and then
40 `revoke-session` buttons.

What this does not show: overlap between two grown rectangles. Each was
tested against other controls' drawn boxes, as §2.4 asks, not against their
grown ones.

## The accessibility audit (2026-09-26 and 2026-09-30)

The audit the accessibility pass's design puts first
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-accessibility-pass-design.md` §1). It
changes no code. Measured on branch `a11y-audit`, from `main` at `a173dd3c`.

**The rig.** A copy of the real library (`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db`)
at `target/a11y/lib/library.db`, with a second account, `reader`, added to it,
and `corpus/gotoubun-v01`'s sidecar copied with absolute member paths and
imported into the copy as a three-edition work. A release `taiyaku serve --db`
on the copy at `:8531`, a production build behind `vite preview` at `:4181`,
and `tailscale serve` sending `/` to the preview and `/api` to the server.
**With the sidecar passed on `serve`'s command line, library works did not
resolve**: `/api/works/<slug>` answered 404 for both library slugs tried until the sidecar was
imported and `serve` restarted on `--db` alone. The first run's
`reader-library` walks were taken in that state and are discarded; every
reader figure below is from the three-edition work. The
original's SHA-256 was `d5ebc0c2…a59e67` before the copy and after the phone
pass, and `find -newermt 2026-09-26T03:44:30-07:00` returned nothing under
`/home/davey/temp/manga-test` or `corpus/gotoubun-v01`.

### The desktop half, 2026-09-26

Playwright-driven Chromium 151.0.7922.34 (`HeadlessChrome/151.0.7922.34` in
the server's request log), signed in as

reader**: an ARIA snapshot per screen, and a walk of real `Tab` presses from

counts as drawn when its computed `outline` or `box-shadow` is not `none`.
The walk stopped when focus reached `BODY`, returned to its first stop, or
after 80 presses.

|---|---|---|---|
| load | no | no | `BODY` |
