## The reader's keyboard and screen-reader access (§3, 2026-09-30)

Measurements for the accessibility pass's §3
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-accessibility-pass-design.md`), on branch
`a11y-reader`.

**O166, reproduced before it was filed.** In the browser project (Chromium,
real key presses through `userEvent`), with Settings open by `s` and focus on
`layout`'s `mode` select: `s` closed Settings — `AssertionError: expected
false to be true // Object.is equality` — and `→` turned the page, writing
progress for slot 3 — `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at
all, but actually been called 1 times`. `isInteractiveTarget` answered
`false` for a `SELECT`, so `keyPlan` took both keys for the reader and
prevented their defaults.

**The ring, walked with real keys.** In the browser project (Chromium,
`userEvent.tab()`), from a reader loaded with focus put on its page area
(the test iframe needs focus before a real key reaches it), at 1440×900,
768×1024 and 390×844 alike, fourteen presses of `Tab` walked the same seven
stops twice:
Library, `single`, `two`, `scroll`, ⚙, the strip's one stop (`page 3`, the
stored position) and the page — the bars up at the first six and down at the
seventh. Seven presses of `Shift+Tab` walked them backwards at each size, the
strip first and the page last. With `preventDefault: false` put back on the
ring, the browser moved focus one stop further after the reader had: the
1440×900 walk began `single`, `scroll`, `page 3`, and then left the reader
for `<body>`. The page area's `tabIndex={-1}` is left out of
`isInteractivePress`; put back in, fifteen `App.test.tsx` cases that tap,
swipe or pan on the page area failed. One, "a tap on the right third
turns back and on the left third forward", read `AssertionError: expected
'50%' to be '33.33333333333333%' // Object.is equality`: the progress line
had not moved.

**Panels and focus.** `usePanelFocus` (`focus.ts`) closes O161's opening half
of the audit's table above. In jsdom, opened by its key with focus on the
page area, each of the five panels
that used to land focus on `BODY` now lands it on the panel itself: `s` on
Settings, `?` on "Keyboard help", `C` on "Credit pages in raw", `a` on "All
notes", `A` on Account. `Escape` — which the audit found left Settings and
Credits **open** — now closes every one of them (Task 2's arms), and focus
that used to land on `BODY` afterwards lands back on the page area. Settings
opened by ⚙ now hands focus back to ⚙ on Close, where the audit found it drop
to `BODY`; Settings and Account now carry `aria-modal="true"`. The note
editor still ends with focus in its textarea: `usePanelFocus` is called
before the editor's own focus effect in `NotePanel.tsx`, so it records what
held focus before the panel opened and puts focus on the panel, and the
editor's effect then moves it into the textarea. `Tab` inside an open panel
no longer shows the bars behind it (O161's first-`Tab` finding): it wraps
inside the panel instead, first to last and back. In the browser project,
with Settings open at 1440×900, 40 real `Tab` presses followed by 40 real
`Shift+Tab` presses — 80 in all — left the panel with nothing having escaped
it.

**On the real library, 2026-09-30.** Task 7's rig, following "The rig" above:
`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db` (sha256 `d5ebc0c2…a59e67`, matching
the audit's) copied to `target/a11y-reader/lib/library.db`, a throwaway
account (`a11y7`, role `user`) added to the copy only, a release
`taiyaku serve --db` on the copy at `127.0.0.1:8541`, and a production build
behind `vite preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4191`. Signed in as `a11y7`,
Playwright-driven Chromium at 1440×900, on `akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz`
(237 pages) — the volume O140 used.

**Seven `Tab`s from a fresh load** walked the ring of Task 4 exactly: Library,
`single`, `two`, `scroll`, ⚙, the strip's one stop (`page 1`, `aria-current`)
and the page area (`[data-reader-page]`) — the bars up (`[data-ring="bottom"]`
present) at the first six stops and down at the seventh.

**`akame-ga-kill----v01--2015--cbz` reads `rtl`** (`/api/works/…` says so), so
the physically-forward arrow for this volume is `←`, not `→`: pressed from a
bar stop or the page, `→` moved the readout backward one slot at a time,
clamped at slot 1, and `←` moved it forward — both through the same
`readerIntentRef` call a click on the hidden "Next page" button also makes, so
this is `stepFor` doing what spec §3.4 says it does, not a defect, and worth
recording only because it decided which key the next check pressed.
**Tab to the strip, then forty real `←` presses, one at a time**:
`document.activeElement` was the current tile every time (`aria-current`,
tag `BUTTON`), the rail was never blank (`button[data-group]` count 19 → 33
as the window grew, never 0) and the focused tile's
`getBoundingClientRect()` intersected the rail's on all forty, and the live
region, read after every press, advanced one page each time, `page 2, 1
percent` → `page 42, 18 percent`.

(sha256 `d5ebc0c2…a59e67`, no `-wal` or `-shm` beside it) copied to

at each width against each build: login, the nine library screens the audit
walked (series `/series/91`, search `?q=one`), and the reader on

**Each capture holds two trees, and they do not name things alike.**
Playwright's ARIA snapshot, which is what the audit recorded, and Chromium's
own accessibility tree, read over the DevTools protocol
(`Accessibility.getFullAXTree`). Row O165, as the audit filed it, says
"Chromium names the textarea …"; what it quoted was the first. Chromium's own tree applies the stylesheet's
`text-transform`: the roots screen's field labels, drawn as upper-case
micro-labels, are named in capitals there — "EDITION KEY", "DEFAULT KIND"
and "ADD A ROOT" among them — as are the users screen's ("NAME",
"PASSWORD" and "ROLE" among them) and the account screen's ("CURRENT",
"NEW"), where Playwright's snapshot gives them as written. On `main`
and on the branch alike, so older than this branch (O175).

What the two builds say, `main` then the branch:

- **Titles** (O173). `document.title` was "taiyaku reader" on all twelve
  captures at both widths. On the branch: "Sign in — taiyaku", "Library —
  taiyaku", "One Piece — taiyaku", "Search — taiyaku", "Proposals — taiyaku",
  "Rules — taiyaku", "Roots — taiyaku", "Users — taiyaku", "Backup —

  · raw — taiyaku", bars down and up.

  ("One Piece", "17 open"), and no `main` on login or in the reader. On the
  branch every capture has exactly one `h1` and one `main`: "taiyaku" on
  login (was a level-2 heading), "Library", "Search", "One Piece",
  "Proposals, 17 open", "Configuration" on each of the four configuration
  screens, "Account" (was level 2, its three sections level 3 and now
  level 2), and "Akame ga Kill! · Vol. 1 · raw" in the reader, with the bars

  then "Proposals, 17 open". At 390 neither build's tree holds the link — the
  drawer is closed.
- **Exclude globs** (O165), in Chromium's own tree: one name, "EXCLUDE GLOBS
  (ONE GITIGNORE PATTERN PER LINE) A trailing slash or bare name excludes the
  directory and everything under it; a '/**' suffix excludes only what's
  inside it.", and no description; then the name "EXCLUDE GLOBS (ONE GITIGNORE
  PATTERN PER LINE)" and that sentence as the description.
- **The permission boxes** (O154): on the users screen, no group round them;

  `tabpanel` named "Impact". The inbox gains `group` "State" and `group`
  "Kind", and the library `group` "Show". **The selected rule's mark is in

  button and not its `<li>`, in jsdom, and the selected row's computed

  Library link at 1440 and ☰ at 390, on all nine library screens; then

**Nothing else differs.** Every line the two builds' snapshots do not share,
indentation aside, is one of the above — but for the users and account
screens' session counts, user-agent lines and Revoke buttons, which are the
capture's own sign-ins.

**Measured in the browser project, on the way**:

- **A visually hidden span inside a name puts a space before itself.**
  `Proposals<span class="visually-hidden">, </span>17…` was named
  "Proposals , 17 open" by `toHaveAccessibleName`: the span is absolutely
  positioned, which makes it a block. So the link takes an `aria-label`. The
  inbox's `h1`, where the hidden words come first, is named "Proposals, 17
  open".
- **A promoted heading grows a step unless it is held**: with the pin removed,
  the sign-in heading and the account page's title each computed `32px`
  against the `24px` of an `h2` beside them.
- **`main` draws a ring when the skip link sends focus to it**, unless told
  not to: without `.library > main:focus`, its `outline-style` read `solid`
  after `Enter` on the link.
- **Without `position: fixed` the skip link is a cell of `.library`'s grid**
  at 1440: the sidebar column measured 224 px from the left edge instead of
  0, and the chip row broke onto three lines. The skip link's own cases did
  not see it; those two did. The skip link's cases now read the link's
  computed `position` themselves, and without the declaration both widths
  fail on `static`.
- **The chip row** keeps its four buttons on one line with the filters a
  column gap (24 px) apart, at 1440 and 390, on `main`'s markup and the
  branch's; without `gap: inherit` on the group the filters touch.

**What the whole-branch review found, and what was measured for each.**

- **A standing `tabIndex={-1}` on `main` takes every click's focus.** §4.6
  first gave `main` one so the skip link could focus it; the review
  reproduced, on a scratch page in Chromium, that a click on plain text
  inside a focusable `main` moves focus to `main`, so the next `Tab` starts
  from its top. `main` now takes the attribute only while it holds the skip
  link's focus. With the standing attribute put back, the browser case that
  clicks the series page's title fails with `main` as the active element;
  with the `blur` listener deleted, the skip cases fail on the attribute
  still being there.
- **The reader named no tab until its work had loaded.** It draws nothing
  before its load answers, so the tab kept the last screen's title. It says
  "taiyaku" now, from the first render: a case that reads the title before
  the load answers failed on `stale` without it.
- **The tabs' keys claimed modified arrows** — `Alt+←` is the browser's
  Back — and stepped from the selected tab rather than the focused one. A
  case pressing each of Alt, Ctrl and ⌘ with `→`, and one pressing `→` on a
  tab focused without being selected, each failed against the old handler.
- **The series screen had no `h1` until its series loaded**, and none on a
  series that is not one. It has a hidden "Series" in those states: with the
  heading withheld while loading, or for an id that is not a number, the case
  for that state fails on an empty list.

**Two things found that are older than this branch.** With the reader's
sidecar read made to fail, `App` rendered no markup at all — in the app
that is `Routes.tsx`'s black `.reader-route` with nothing on it — with the
tab reading "taiyaku" and one `console.error` (O176).
`Config.browser.test.tsx`'s "does not scroll sideways with a populated scan
report" failed run alone with `-t` — `expected 402 to be less than or equal
to 390` — once on `main` at `16504d61` and once on the branch, and passed on
the branch when its whole file ran. It is not simply a matter of order: the
same case failed inside a whole run on the reader branch on 2026-09-30 and
twice on this one — the second time inside `scripts/check-all.sh`, with that
same line, on a tree that differed from the one a green run had just passed
on by one sentence of `docs/status.md` (O177). **The cause is the fonts.**
With a probe added to the case and the case run alone, twice: when it
measured, `document.fonts.status` was `loading` with none of the faces
loaded and the document's `scrollWidth` was 402; after `await
document.fonts.ready` it was 390, and the case passed. **And the case cannot
see the defect it names.** The same probe with `.scan-report > section > dl`
put back to `.scan-report dl`: the nested `<dl>` computed one 256px column,
and the document and `main` still read 402 of 390 before the fonts and 390 of
390 after — as they do with the rule as it stands, where that `<dl>` has no
grid columns. The case now waits for `document.fonts.ready`, by the user's
decision of 2026-10-01; run alone it passed three times of three. The probe
was removed afterwards.

**Captured again after those fixes**, the branch at `a30bcdec`'s code, on the
same rig rebuilt: every title, `h1`, `main` count and first `Tab` stop the
same as the branch's first capture, and no line of either tree different but
the sessions'. So the figures above describe the code as it stands.

**No screen reader was run**, by the user's decision of 2026-10-01: the
evidence is Chromium's tree and the tests. So O164's VoiceOver reading —
*"proposals, visited, link"*, no count — is not known to have changed, and
nothing here says what VoiceOver or Orca does with a `tablist`, a named
group, a description or a skip link. For a tester who knows VoiceOver, with
O162's list: whether the Proposals link says its count; whether "Permissions"
and the three filter groups are spoken; whether Exclude globs' hint is read

/home/davey/temp/manga-test -newermt` the rig's start time printed nothing.

## O146 and O181 (2026-10-04)

**O146: the case, and what it was watched failing against.** Written in a
worktree of its own by a separate agent — a lane — and landed here by
cherry-pick as `1b300032`. The runs below were made again on that commit, and
a figure is that run's unless it is marked as the lane's.
`Filmstrip.browser.test.tsx` gains "a page turn after the reader has flicked
the rail", one case for each reading direction, at 1440×900 on the file's
120-tile fixture. Nothing is stubbed: the flick is a write to the rail's own
`scrollLeft`, the scroll event is the browser's, and the turn is a
`rerender` on the same instance.

Each row is a hand edit to `Filmstrip.tsx`, the two new cases run alone
against it, and the file put back:

| | the edit | left-to-right | right-to-left |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | none | passes | passes |
| M1 | the retry effect's body removed | fails: `scrollLeft` still 576, the tile's right edge at 6060 against the rail's 1440 | fails: still −576, the tile's left edge at −4620 against the rail's 0 |
| M2 | `recenter()` and then `pendingRecentre.current = false`, whatever it found | fails, the same two readings | fails, the same two readings |
| M3 | `if (recenter())` in place of `if (recenter() && !resetPending)` | passes | passes |
| control, after the last restore | none | passes | passes |

**Why M3 passes there** was checked rather than reasoned: two more edits
that change no behaviour and throw on one path each. One throws if the
centring effect's first attempt found a tile while a flick was pending, and
both cases pass against it. The other throws if that attempt found none, and
both cases fail with its message. So in these cases the first attempt finds
no tile, `recenter()` is false, and the condition is false with the guard or
without it.

**The lane's readings of the unmutated run**, not taken again here: after
the mount `scrollLeft` is 5759 (−5758 right-to-left); after the flick 576
(−576) with tiles 0 to 22 rendered and none current; after the turn 5866
(−5865) with tiles 45 to 77 rendered and tile 61's box from 669 to 770 in a
rail from 0 to 1440.

**O181: M3 passes everywhere.** With that edit applied, the whole `node`
and `jsdom` projects pass, 2,655 tests in 125 files, and the whole browser
project passes, 175 in 14. The lane also tried a flick of 800 px, which it
reports left the window at tiles 36 to 68 with tile 61 still inside it, so
that the first attempt does find a tile: with M3 applied the rail landed at
`scrollLeft` 5866 and the tile at 669 to 770, the unmutated figures. Those
are the lane's and were not run again. Why the guard changes nothing there
is not established.

**Counts**, each against `main`: `node` 1,428 and `jsdom` 1,227, unchanged;
browser 173 to 175, the two new cases.

## Deployable (2026-10-04)

Part B of `2026-10-04-day-to-day-deployment-design.md`. What was measured
while planning it, and what the plan changed because of it.

**A cold release build** of `taiyaku-cli` at `-j 4`, thin LTO and one codegen
unit, in a fresh target directory: 234 crates in 103 s on this workstation
(Ryzen 9 9950X3D), the planning session's reading, with no log kept. The NAS
is an i7-9700K, 8 cores; nothing was timed there. The image at `90e400d6` built
locally in 118 s, at 174,012,705 bytes (the first attempt failed: the wasm and
server stages raced on the shared cargo registry cache, and `sharing=locked` on both
registry cache mounts fixed it).

**The NAS's Docker** is 29.5.3 (API 1.54). The forge's runner automounts the
host socket into job containers and caps them at four CPUs, a cap that does
not reach a buildx `docker-container` builder.

**Nginx Proxy Manager**, read from the running container:
- `conf.d/include/proxy.conf` sets `Host $host`, `X-Forwarded-Scheme`,
  `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP`, and no
  `X-Forwarded-Host`.
- Every generated `location /` sets headers of its own, so a server-level
  `proxy_set_header` in the Advanced tab never reaches it.
- An Advanced config containing `location / {` replaces the generated one
  (`internal/nginx.js`, `advancedConfigHasDefaultLocation`).
- `assets.conf` caches by file extension in a public cache, ignoring
  `Cache-Control` and `Set-Cookie`.
- `block-exploits.conf` refuses any query parameter whose value starts with
  `/`.
- `nginx.conf` sets `proxy_read_timeout 90s`.
- The proxy listens on host ports 180 and 1443, which is why the Advanced
  block uses `$http_host`.

**The library share's permissions**: `/mnt/user/media 1/Manga` is
`root:root 755`; 73 of its 580 directories cannot be written by uid 99; all
67,925 files are world-readable. So a read-write mount alone lets the
container write neither `.taiyaku/` nor the watch probe's file at the root.

**Decided 2026-10-04**:
- The library's permissions stay as they are (`root:root 755`, 73 of 580
  directories unwritable by uid 99). The user loosens them only for as long as
  a write needs. A later part (spec Part E, "pending library writes") will
  queue the writes until an admin flushes them; with the decision on hand
  documents below, that means only ComicInfo write-backs.
- The hostname will be `taiyaku.daveynet.xyz`, proxied through Cloudflare
  (orange cloud) like the user's other sites. Cloudflare's edge reaches NPM
  directly, not through the Cloudflare tunnel, so taiyaku is public. This
  replaces the earlier plan of a name that resolves only inside the network.
- Client addresses behind Cloudflare, measured read-only on the NAS: NPM's
  global nginx config trusts private ranges and Cloudflare's published ranges
  (`set_real_ip_from`, via `conf.d/include/ip_ranges.conf`) but sets
  `real_ip_header X-Real-IP;`, a header Cloudflare does not send. taiyaku takes
  the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry (`crates/taiyaku-serve/src/auth.rs`,
  the `rsplit(',')` near line 152), which would be a Cloudflare edge address,
  so the login rate limiter would key every visitor together. The fix is
  `real_ip_header CF-Connecting-IP;` on its own line above the Advanced tab's
  `location /` block, at server level. Inside the location it loses to a
  client-supplied `X-Real-IP`, because nginx applies its real-IP module once per
  request, server level first, and NPM sets `real_ip_header X-Real-IP` at http
  level, which the server inherits. With the line at
  server level, NPM's `$remote_addr` becomes the client's address as Cloudflare
  reports it, for requests from Cloudflare's ranges.
- Cloudflare caching is not a risk for signed-in content: Cloudflare does not
  cache a response marked `private`, `no-store` or `no-cache`, and every guarded
  response carries one (`per_reader_by_default` in `routes.rs` adds
  `private, no-store` where none is set; pages and downloads send
  `private, no-cache`: `PAGE_CACHE_CONTROL`, and `download.rs`; and since
  the loading work's second PR a cover whose `?v=` names its bytes sends
  `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`: `COVER_CACHE_CONTROL`). Content-hashed
  `/assets/*` are cached at the edge, which is fine because they are
  immutable.
- The NAS trial happens after merge, on the image CI builds and pushes. No
  image is loaded onto the NAS by hand.
- Hand-written metadata documents may move into appdata (`/config`) instead of
  `<root>/.taiyaku/`, so a metadata edit would no longer need the library to be
  writable. Part E's plan settles the details.
- Because taiyaku is public, O57 (a burst of concurrent logins can allocate
  about 9.5 GiB of argon2 memory before the rate limiter bounds it) should be
  fixed soon after. O58 and O60 matter once other accounts exist.
- Appdata Backup keeps taiyaku on its stop list and excludes the cache
  directory.

**2026-10-05, the image job's first run on `main`** (the squash, `953b2486`):
193 s by the forge's tasks API, `run_started` 13:39:27 to 13:42:40. It pushed
`sha-953b248` and `latest`. The job's 60-minute timeout is to be re-sized at
the next CI change.

## Live works (Part A, 2026-10-04)

Part A of `2026-10-04-day-to-day-deployment-design.md`, which opened and
closed O183: the reader serves the library as it stands, not as it stood when
the server started.

**What changed.** Migration 14 adds a one-row table, `structure_version`, and
eighteen triggers: one after each insert, update and delete on `work`,
`edition`, `member`, `page_flag`, `alignment` and `run`, the six tables
`project::sidecar` reads, each adding one to the counter.
`taiyaku_library::structure::version` reads it. `taiyaku serve` with no paths
holds its works in a live registry (`registry::Works::library`) in place of a
`Vec<Work>` built once; `serve` handed sidecar paths holds a fixed one
(`Works::fixed`) that never reads the library again. A refresh reads the
counter and, when it differs from the value the registry last read at, reads
every `work` row again. A work it already holds keeps its `Work`, and its
document is replaced under that work's own write lock (`Work::reproject`), so
the notes lock and correction lock every request in flight holds stay the
ones it holds. A row whose `sidecar_path` changed becomes a new `Work`,
because `Work.path` is fixed for a `Work`'s life. A row that is gone is no
longer served. `ServeState::find` is the lookup for code on a runtime worker
(a hit is a read lock and an `Arc` clone; a miss in a live registry asks for a
refresh on the blocking pool and looks again), and `ServeState::find_blocking`
is the same for code already on the blocking pool. `serve` spawns a refresher
that asks every two seconds (`registry::REFRESH_EVERY`), so `/api/works` and
the OPDS feed, which never name a work, pick up a new one too. The scan
report's `note`, which said `/api/works` was a startup snapshot, is gone, with
the web's drawing of it.

**Why the counter is read before the works, never after.** A write that
commits while the works are being read leaves the counter ahead of the value
recorded as seen, so the next refresh reads again. Read afterwards, that write
would be recorded as seen without ever having been read.
`a_write_that_lands_while_a_refresh_reads_is_read_by_the_next_one` writes from
inside the first work's read, and failed with the read moved after the works.

**Why each work is read in its own `BEGIN DEFERRED` transaction.** One
transaction per work makes its document come from one committed state rather
than from both sides of a write that lands between two of `project::sidecar`'s
queries. Deferred, spelled out, because `Library::configure` sets every
connection's transactions to `IMMEDIATE`, which takes the write lock: a
refresh would wait out, and hold up, whichever writer was running.

**The race test** (`a_correction_racing_a_refresh_survives_it`). A thread holds
one work's write lock the way `patch_alignments` does and waits to be let go.
An unrelated write moves the counter, and a refresh starts on another thread
with a `project` that reports when it reads. The test waits 500 ms for that
report, lets the correction write its row and finish, and joins both. A
correct refresh takes the work's lock before reading it, so it reads after the
correction and serves it. A refresh that read first would swap a document
without the correction in once the lock came free. The 500 ms decides only how
long a correct refresh is given not to read early: the correct path passes
whatever the timing. With the read moved before the lock it failed: "the
refresh undid a correction that committed after it began: it read the work
before taking the work's lock".

**On a copy of the real library.** A release build of the branch as it stood
before its whole-branch fix round (`34af9649`, before the rebase onto Part B)
served a scratch copy of `library.db` in no-paths mode. `/api/works` listed
1896 works and the counter read 0. A separate `taiyaku library scan --add`
of a new three-directory root reported "3 added, 0 updated, 0 gone; derived
136 series, 1897 works, 1897 editions, 1897 members". The new work,
`drive-test---v01`, answered `200` in 0.013972 s on the first request for it.
Three seconds later `/api/works` listed 1897 and the counter read 18972. The
first request came right after the scan, so whether the refresher's tick or
the lookup's miss served it was not separated. The original `library.db`
hashed the same before and after, and the server's log had no "could not
refresh" line.

**The counter counts trigger firings, not scans.** That one scan moved it
from 0 to 18972. Every deriving scan moves it, because derive writes every
work it derives: its `UPDATE work
SET series_id = COALESCE(series_id_hand, ?1), volume = …` runs whether or not
anything changed. The server's scan always derives, and `library scan` does
unless given `--no-derive`, so every such scan moves the counter and the next
refresh reads every work.

**Two consequences, by reading the code.** A work whose rows will not project
keeps the document it had (or, if new, is not served), and is tried again only
when the counter next moves: the refresh that kept it recorded the counter as
seen. And a configured Stump source resolves only the works present at
startup: `serve` hands the resolution the registry's snapshot once, after the
bind, so a work a later scan adds is served from disk.

**Two fixes for what the rebase onto Part B found.** A refresh with something to say
printed it with `eprintln!`, which panics when nothing reads stderr. The
refresher's report of that panic panicked too, and the refresher ended for
the life of the process: the served works stopped picking up changes on their
own, and only a lookup miss still refreshed them. The notice and both panic lines now print with `writeln!`
and ignore the error. `serve_keeps_its_works_current_with_stderr_closed` runs
the binary over a live library, lets go of its stderr, makes a refresh
complain (one work's rows will not project) and then waits for a later change
to be listed; with all three lines back on `eprintln!` it failed, "the
refresher stopped once a complaint could not be written". It holds the
refresher's survival, not each line: with only the notice's line, or only the
refresher's own line, put back on `eprintln!` it passed, because the other of
the two alone keeps the refresher alive. And a library that stayed unopenable printed its
complaint every tick, because the message says how long opening waited
(`(waited 31µs for another process …)`) and the notice compared whole strings.
Complaints are now compared without that figure, and the line printed keeps
it. `a_failure_that_differs_only_in_how_long_it_waited_is_said_once` takes a
real failure's words (a file that is not a database, with its log moved aside)
and failed before the change: the second wait was said again.

**The mutation sweep** (`scripts/mutants.sh --since main`, after the two
fixes): 88 mutants in 9 minutes, 65 caught, 22 unviable, 1 missed, no
timeouts. The one missed, `Works::is_live -> true`, is equivalent: a fixed
registry asked to refresh answers `Unmoved` without reading. It failed nothing
in the three crates by hand, and `docs/mutants-baseline.md` records it.
Each of the 22 unviable is `Default::default()` against a type deriving no
`Default`, or a `JoinHandle` that cannot be built, and they leave twelve
functions with no viable mutant at all. Of those, `find`'s and `find_blocking`'s refresh on a miss were each taken out
by hand and failed a router test, and `read_one` on `IMMEDIATE` failed the
ordering test. `read_one` with no transaction at all failed nothing, so
`a_work_is_read_from_one_committed_state_of_the_library` was added: its
`project` reads the title, lets another connection retitle the work, then
projects it, and it fails without the transaction ("After" against
"Before"). Migration 14's SQL is a string literal, which cargo-mutants never
mutates, so its first task's three hand-applied trigger defects (a trigger
dropped, a trigger made to add nothing, and an extra trigger on `progress`)
are that file's only mutation evidence.

**Counts**, each against `main`: Rust 2257 to 2281; `node` 1,428, unchanged;
`jsdom` 1,238 to 1,237, the case that drew the scan report's `note` deleted;
browser 184, unchanged.

**Not measured**: the NAS; what a refresh costs while a long derive is
running, when each work it commits moves the counter and every tick reads
every work again; how long one refresh of the whole copy takes; and a library
larger than the 1,896-work copy.

## Libraries, F1 (2026-10-06)

Part F1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-libraries-design.md`: the store
keeps libraries, and nothing in the web app changes yet.

**What changed.** Migration 15 adds `library` (a name, unique), gives `root`,
`series` and `work` a `library_id`, rebuilds `work` so that `content_key` is
unique within a library rather than across the store, and replaces `user_root`
with `user_library`. Each existing root becomes a library of its own, taking
the root's id. A library's id is `AUTOINCREMENT`, so it is never given to a
later library. Triggers keep the shape: `root_gets_a_library` files a
root inserted without a library under one of its own, the two
`library_emptied_*` delete a library with its last root, and the two
`only_grant_refuses_*` refuse to delete or re-file the last root of a library
that is some account's only grant. Derivation groups by library, and its
series and work lookups are scoped to it. Proposals pair series of one
library only, and one whose two series are in different libraries is refused
at accept. A grant names a library and resolves to its folders. The CLI
gained `library libraries`, `scan --library` and `user
grant-library|revoke-library`; `scan --add` says which library the folder
went to and whether it made it, and `user list` shows each account's grants.
*(2026-11-03: the overlapping-libraries PR 1 has since made derivation and
proposals run across the whole store, and no proposal is refused for having
its two series in different libraries. See
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-overlapping-libraries-design.md`.)*

**Migration 15 files a work under its hub edition's library** because
`hand::path_for` addresses a work's document off the hub edition's root, so
the work stays with its document.

**`ON DELETE SET NULL`, not CASCADE, on `work` and `series`.** A library goes
only with its last root. Where the root is removed, `scan::apply_removal` has
already deleted every work that root alone accounted for; what still carries
the library has material elsewhere, and CASCADE would delete it uncounted.

**A row in no library is taken only by a library whose folders hold it.**
The plan had any library take one, the lowest id first. A review ran it: a
folder alone in its library was moved to another, a third library with a
lower id then scanned a folder holding the same title and volume, and the
moved folder's work went to the third library with its reading position.
Now a work in no library is taken by a library only where it has a member
under one of that library's roots, or no member under any root (an imported
one); a series likewise, by its works. The rule is written once, as
`libraries::own_or_adoptable_work` and `own_or_adoptable_series`, and
spliced into each statement by which a derive or a hand document finds a
work or a series for a library.

**Removing the last folder of a library that is an account's only grant is
refused**, naming the accounts. A library goes with its last folder and its
grants with it, and an account with no grant sees every library. The check
is `scan::removal_refusal`, asked by the removal and by its dry run, and the
route answers it 409. An administrator's grant counts: it does nothing while
the account administers, and its row is what a demotion restores.

**A library's name is looked up as given first, and stripped of spaces
second.** Migration 15's backfill keeps the spaces of two folders whose whole
paths differ only in surrounding spaces. With a stripped lookup alone, run
over such a backfill, the spaced library's own name answered the other one:
`scan --library` walked the other's folder and `grant-library` granted it
while printing the name typed.

**Two fixes from reading the branch whole.** The rule preview counted
series by title, which was right while one title was one series. A reviewer
ran it with `Alpha` in two libraries: it previewed four series where five
held works, and reported a rename into a title only the other library holds
as a merge. It counts series by row now. And a `taiyaku.json` import, which
looks its work up across the store, chose among several works of one content
without asking which already held the document. Run with the same bytes in
two libraries and the first library's folder since removed, the document's
next import moved it to the other library's work and left the first with
the reader's position and note. The work whose `sidecar_path` is the
document's path answers first now. A first import of a document beside one
library's copy can still land on another library's work of that content
(O194).

**On a copy of the real library** (`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db`,
copied to scratch; the release binary at `93bd9033`; `uptime` read between
3.8 and 5.3 across the timed runs):

- Before: schema 13, one root, 1896 works, 138 series.
- `library libraries` migrated the copy to 15 and listed it in 0.015 s:
  `Volumes: 1 folder(s), 1896 work(s)`. The dump of every work's id, slug,
  content key, title and series was byte-identical to before. 134 series were
  filed and 4, each holding no work, were in no library. The FTS
  integrity check, `foreign_key_check` and `integrity_check` were clean.
- A scratch folder holding `Akame ga KILL!/Akame ga KILL! - v01`, a title the
  copy already has, added with `scan --add … --library "Drive Other"`: 0.50 s,
  `derived 136 series, 1897 works`, one work in `Drive Other` and 1896 in
  `Volumes`, two series of that title, and the dump of `Volumes`' works still
  byte-identical, then and after eight more derives. That derive also filed
  one of the four series in no library under `Volumes`, the one a
  chapter-only directory there names; the other three stayed.
- `main` (`d1630cbb`), given the same folder on a second copy, answered
  `1896 works … 1 rekeyed, 1 merged`: it folded the scratch volume into
  `Volumes`' first work and changed that work's content key.
- A walk of the scratch folder and a derive of everything took 0.43 to
  0.62 s on the branch and 0.37 to 0.45 s on `main`, over five runs of each,
  interleaved.
- Served: the administrator was listed 1897 works by `/api/works` and by
  OPDS, and 2 roots; an account granted `Drive Other` alone, 1, 1 and 1, and
  a 404 for a work of `Volumes`. `DELETE /api/library/roots/2`, dry run and
  real, answered 409 with the refusal naming that account, and the works
  were still 1897.
- The original's digest was unchanged afterwards, and nothing under its
  folder was newer than the marker laid down when the copy was made.
- After `library.id` became `AUTOINCREMENT`, the migration was run again on a
  fresh copy with the same result: the dump byte-identical and the three
  integrity checks clean. A library made after another had been deleted took
  the next number, 3, and not the freed 2.

**What a folder moved between libraries does**, for F2's Move action (O192).
*(O192 has since closed: its row in `docs/status.md` says what Move does in each case.)*
Nothing in F1 moves one; each of these was run by a reviewer, by setting
`root.library_id` by hand and deriving:

- A folder alone in its library, moved into a library holding nothing at its
  works' addresses: the works keep their rows, slugs and positions and are
  filed under the new library (`derive::tests`'
  `a_folder_moved_out_of_a_library_it_was_alone_in_keeps_its_works` and
  `a_folder_moved_out_of_its_library_and_then_changed_keeps_its_work`).
- The same folder moved into a library that holds the same edition of a
  volume: the moved work stays in no library with its position, and both
  derives that were run reported `unfolded_works=1`.
- Moved into a library that holds the volume under another edition key: the
  moved work is folded into that one (`emptied_works=1`,
  `moved_positions=1`), its row and slug are deleted, and its series is left
  in no library.
- A folder moved out of a library that keeps another folder: its works are
  minted again under the new library and the old ones folded into them, so
  each has a new id and slug. With `keeps_documents` off, the new work had
  lost its hand title, hand volume and tag, and the series' alt title and
  external id stayed on the old series; with it on, they came back from the
  document.
- A work spanning the moved folder and one that stays is not folded: the old
  work keeps both editions and both positions, and the new library's work
  has no position.
- A work with members under two libraries' folders, in no library, goes to
  the library with the lower id whatever its hub.

One of these needs no move. Where migration 15 split a work across two
libraries, removing the folder that holds the old work's hub edition leaves
that work in no library with its positions and notes, an empty hub edition
and the other library's kept edition, and the derives run after it each
reported `unfolded_works=1`. Removing the other folder instead removes the split-off
work, counted, and leaves the old work an empty edition with its position and
note still on it.

**What migration 15 leaves in a store that held works across two roots, or
an accepted proposal**, each run by a reviewer; the one-edition case was run
in a store the branch made and split by hand. The real copy has one root and no accepted
proposal, so none of this.

- A work with an edition from each root: the old work keeps its id, slug,
  hand title, document, and the positions and notes on both editions. The
  other root's library gets a new work with a new slug, the derived title and
  no positions. A second and a third scan change no row.
- One edition gathered from both roots: the old work is rekeyed and keeps
  only its own root's pages. In the run it went from 5 pages to 2 with a
  position left at slot 4, and the other folder's pages became a new work
  with no position.
- A series that spanned the roots keeps its hand titles in the library where
  most of its works are. The other library's works move to a newly minted
  series of the scanned title, and where documents are kept each scan
  reports "1 document(s) disagree with the database".
- A proposal accepted before F1 leaves its subject series holding no work,
  so the migration leaves that series in no library. Un-accepting and
  accepting again is refused until a scan has filed it (O190).

**On SQLite 3.40.1**, which CI and the image link where this workstation has
3.53: the tests of the three crates that link SQLite (`taiyaku-library`,
`taiyaku-serve`, `taiyaku-cli`) were run inside `rust:1-bookworm` over an
export of the branch, and all passed but two, which trace with `strace`;
that container did not have it. Reviewers also ran migration 15 and its
triggers on 3.40.1 builds of their own.

**For F2 and F3**, from the whole-branch reviews. Unticking one folder of a
two-folder library on the Users screen does nothing (O193; *it has since
closed, with F2a: see its row*). The Roots
screen never shows the name of the library a folder it adds was given, and
draws the 409 refusal as the raw response. An unrestricted account's grid,
search, works list and OPDS feed show two series or two works of one name
with nothing to tell them apart.

**The mutation sweep** (`scripts/mutants.sh --since main`): 249 mutants in
20 minutes, 199 caught, 50 unviable, none missed, no timeouts. Each unviable
one replaces a function's whole body with a value that does not compile
there, which leaves some functions in the changed lines with no viable
mutant; `docs/mutants-baseline.md` names them. cargo-mutants never mutates a
string literal, and much of the branch's scoping is SQL inside one. What
those statements say was tested by the defects applied by hand in the
branch's tasks and reviews.

**Counts**, each against `main`: Rust 2281 to 2421. The web's are unchanged,
since no file under `web/` changed.

**Not measured**: the NAS; a library larger than the 1,896-work copy; how

since on the copy every work was filed; and `scan --library`
beside a folder of another library with `keeps_documents` on, where the

## Libraries, F2a (2026-10-06)

Part F2a of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-libraries-design.md`: the
Libraries screen, the folder browser and grants by library. Moving a folder
between libraries is F2b and is not here (O192). *(It has since been built; see
"Libraries, F2b".)*

**What changed.** The store makes a library with its folders in one
transaction (`scan::create_library`), adds a folder to a library by id,
renames a library, and removes one whole (`scan::remove_library`, with
`library_removal_cost` as its rehearsal). `account::Patch` takes `libraries`,
a list of library ids, where it took `roots`. The server gained
`/api/library/libraries` (list, create), `/api/library/libraries/{id}`
(rename, remove, and `?dry_run=true`), `…/{id}/folders` (add), `…/{id}/scan`
(start, status) and `/api/library/folders` (the folder browser), all
administrator-only; `POST /api/library/roots` is gone, and a users `PATCH`
that carries `roots` is refused with a sentence naming `libraries`. `taiyaku
serve` takes `--folders DIR`, repeatable, or `TAIYAKU_FOLDERS`; the image
sets the variable to `/media`. In the web app `/config/libraries` replaces
the Roots screen (`/config/roots` redirects to it) and the Users card grants
libraries: "Every library, including any added later", or "Only these" with a
tick per library.

**The plan's four corrections to the spec, as built.**

- `TAIYAKU_FOLDERS` is split on `:` only, since a folder's path can hold a
  comma or a space (the NAS share is `/mnt/user/media 1`). `--folders`
  replaces the variable when given.
- A library's removal is not the sum of its folders' own counts.
  `scan::DOOMED_WORKS` counts a work for a folder only when every member of
  it is under that folder, so a work with an edition in each of two folders
  is in neither folder's count. `remove_library` takes the folders one after
  another inside one transaction and sums as it goes, so such a work is
  counted when its last folder goes
  (`a_library_removal_counts_a_work_with_an_edition_per_folder_once`,
  `a_library_removal_counts_a_work_with_one_edition_in_both_folders_once`),
  and a removal that fails part-way removes nothing
  (`a_library_removal_that_fails_part_way_removes_nothing`).
- A library's scan reports per folder as a running flag, then every folder's
  report at once: the derive runs once, after the last walk, and each
  folder's report carries it. So each folder's registry entry is running
  until the whole scan ends.
- "No readable files yet" is drawn from a count the store keeps
  (`libraries::books`): the card says it when the library has no work and
  its scans recorded at least one EPUB or PDF entry.

**Removing a library that is an account's only grant is refused**, naming
the accounts, by `scan::library_removal_refusal`, asked before anything is
deleted by the removal and by its rehearsal; the route answers 409. It is
F1's rule for a library's last folder, asked of the library.

**The folder browser lists only beneath the configured folders, and says
nothing about anything else.** `folders_api`'s first version answered 403
for a path outside that exists and 400 for one that does not, and printed
the canonical path in the 403, so a request could learn what exists anywhere
and where a link points. It was rebuilt twice. As it stands: the path as
sent must begin, by whole components, with a configured folder; it is then
walked one name at a time from that folder, each name looked up without
following it; a link is followed one hop at a time and only where each hop
lands inside a configured folder; and anything else gets one refusal, built
from the path as sent, whether or not it exists. A broken or looping link
inside a configured folder is refused the same way, and so is a spelling
such as `/proc/self/root/<folder>`. The walk rests on the file system not
changing under it: with a second thread swapping a directory inside the
folder for a link out while `list` was called in a loop, some of its
answers were listings of the directory outside (O197).

**A library's scan checks its folders again before it walks.** The job is
reserved in the scan registry when the request arrives and may wait for the
job lock. Once it holds the lock it reads the library's folders again and
walks nothing if they are not the folders it reserved, and it writes a
report back only over its own reservation. The older per-folder scan job
does neither (O196).

**The two routes that take a folder's path refuse one that is empty or not
absolute**, before the store is asked. The store's own check, which the CLI
shares, resolves a relative path against the working directory, which is
right at a terminal and wrong in a server.

**On the Libraries screen a library and its folders hold each other's scans
and removals.** While a library is scanning, starting a scan, or known to be
scanning, while its removal dialog is open or its removal is out, or while
any of its folders is scanning or confirming a removal, every other Scan now
and Remove in that library is held. Folder settings, Rename and Add folder
are not held by a scan. A refused make, add or rename is drawn in the form
that was submitted, and a removal's re-derive report is kept at the top of
the screen, with focus moved to it, for a library's removal and for a
folder's.

**Departures from the plan made while building**, each after a review ran
the plan's version:

- `FolderPicker` holds one pick at a time, and the removal's report is drawn
  by the screen and not by the card that asked, which is gone by then (the
  plan's "Changed while building").
- The folder browser leaves out an entry whose name is not UTF-8, where the
  plan listed it lossily: such a path could not be entered or picked.
- The folder browser's refusal rule, above, where the plan's code compared
  the canonical path and answered by whether it resolved.
- A failed read of a directory answers an error where the plan's code
  returned the entries read so far.
- The make-a-library form draws its refusal inside the form, where the plan
  drew it between the list and the form.
- `sentenceOf` draws a short one-line plain-text body as the sentence (a
  reader's 403 is plain text); anything else keeps its path and status.

**The mutation sweep** (`scripts/mutants.sh --since main`) ran twice. At
`fb6b58e7`: 147 mutants, 117 caught, 27 unviable, 2 missed, 1 timeout. The
two missed were `libraries::rename`'s guard on the UNIQUE code and
`libraries_api::library_panicked`; the timeout was a test that called
`serve` in-process with no bound. At `71632679`, after a test for each: 149
mutants, 122 caught, 27 unviable, none missed, no timeout.

**On SQLite 3.40.1** (`rust:1-bookworm`, at `377cfcd5`; the Rust code is
unchanged since): `taiyaku-cli` 548 and 37 passed; `taiyaku-library` 981
passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored; `taiyaku-serve` 742 passed, 1 failed. The two
failures are the two that need `strace`, which the container lacks.

**On a copy of the real library** (`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db`,
copied to scratch; the release binary and the built web app at `904bec95`;
driven through the screen in a browser as an administrator, with a second
browser for a second account):

- `/config/libraries` listed the copy's one library, "Volumes", as "1896
  works in 1 folder", and `/config/roots` landed there.
- Browse… listed one folder at the top, the scratch share the server was
  started with, and Up from it led back to that list and nowhere else. A
  library made from two folders found that way read "0 works in 2 folders".
- Scan now on it took 1.006 s from the request to the first status read that
  found it done; the request log carries no duration for the scan itself.
  Both folder rows said "Scanning…" while it ran and each then showed a
  report, and the card read "1 work in 2 folders".
- With a third folder of twelve volumes added and scanned, the library read
  "13 works in 3 folders" and "Volumes" still "1896 works in 1 folder"; the
  store held 1896 and 13. The one volume both libraries hold is a work of
  each.
- While the library scanned, its Scan now and Remove library…, and each
  folder's Scan now and Remove…, were disabled, and Rename… and Browse…
  were not. A folder's Scan now pressed from a second tab was
  refused 409: "a scan of root 2 (…) is already running".
- A rename was taken. A rename to "Volumes" was refused under the name box:
  "a library is already called `Volumes`".
- An account set to "Only these" with that library ticked was shown 2 series
  and 13 volumes and none of the first library's 1896. Its last tick would
  not clear ("The last tick cannot be cleared here. Choose “Every library”
  to lift the limit."), and "Every library" left it no grant.
- With the library that account's only grant, Remove library… was refused
  409, naming the account. With a second grant the dialog read "Removing
  Drive Renamed removes its 3 folders, 13 works, 0 in-progress positions and
  0 notes."; the rehearsal took 0.47 s and the removal 0.90 s. Afterwards
  the card was gone, "Volumes" read "1896 works in 1 folder", the
  re-derive's report stood at the top of the screen and focus was on it.
- A library of one folder holding one PDF read "0 works in 1 folder" and "No
  readable files yet: its scans found 1 EPUB or PDF file, and reading those
  arrives with the books work. A rescan is all this library will need then."
- A folder removed from a two-folder library: "This removes 12 works, 0
  in-progress positions and 0 notes."; then the card read "1 work in 1
  folder" and the report named the folder's path. Its last folder removed:
  the card went, and the report named the library.
- A path typed by hand is not confined as the browser is: `/etc` was added
  as a folder, and its watch probe was refused by permissions. A relative
  path was refused: "a folder's path must be absolute, and `relative/dir` is
  not".
- At 390 wide a removal's report began 60 px down, below the 52 px bar.
- A refusal is drawn directly under the button pressed. Where that button
  sat at the foot of a 900 px window the sentence was below the fold, and
  the page did not move (O209).
- A reload in the middle of a scan showed the card scanning again, with the
  same buttons held.
- One ArrowUp on the "Only these" radio, reached by Tab alone, selected
  "Every library", and the account's grant was gone (O195).
- The request log held 613 lines: 13 answered 4xx, each caused on purpose or
  by signing in, and none 5xx.
- The original's digest was unchanged afterwards, and nothing under its
  folder was newer than the marker laid down when the copy was made.

**Counts**, each beside the figure `docs/status.md` gave on `main`: 2554 Rust
tests (2421); in `web/`, 1,461 in the `node` project (1,428), 1,411 in the
`jsdom` one (1,237) and 226 in the browser project (184).

**Not measured.** The NAS, and the image, which was not built. A directory
listing on a disk that is asleep (spec §13). A screen reader on the new
controls. Any browser but Chromium: iOS Safari resolving `env()` inside the
custom property the phone bar's height now comes from, and a browser without
scroll anchoring when a scan ends under a person who is typing. Two
connections racing: two creates with overlapping folders, a removal against
a scan that is walking, and a removal whose derive fails after its commit
(the routes then leave that library's registry entries in place). How long a
rehearsal holds its write lock on the real library.

The branch `f2a-followups` answers O195 to O209 on the rulings of 2026-10-07

The hand defects listed below are as each task's report gives them; no log of

migration and stayed at 15. The reading is in
`.superpowers/sdd/f2a-followups-evidence/migration16-store-copies.log`, which
is not committed.

## Libraries, F2b (2026-10-08)

The branch `folder-move` builds Move, the last part of F2: a folder's row on
Configuration → Libraries moves the folder to another library or to a new
one (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-libraries-f2b-move.md`). It closes
O192, and O208, whose duplicates it merges. This section records what was
decided, what was built and what was measured. The logs it cites are in
`.superpowers/sdd/folder-move-evidence/`, which is not committed.

**Decided by the user, 2026-10-07.** The plan's six spec corrections, as
written: a split drops, and counts, an alignment between two editions it
separates; a series the target holds no series of the title of, and every
work of which moves, moves whole, and otherwise the target gets a series of
that title; a third refusal, where the hub moves, other editions stay and the
target holds the volume; a rehearsal derives twice; a reader's place is also
checked by counting; a refusal lists its volumes beside its sentence. O208's
three duplicates merged here, the per-folder scan job included. Then, from
the reviews: the real move's answer is handed up to the screen as a
removal's is; a join that loses a row a person made refuses the move; a
work placed in a series by hand, where that series keeps works the move
leaves behind, refuses the move; the counts a move answers are the rows that
move; and a confirm the server refuses takes the rehearsal away with it, so
the person asks again. **Three rules were the controller's, not the
user's**: a move is refused where the derive before it, over the store as it
stands, would itself lose a row, with a sentence saying to scan first; where
a divided work would be folded away; and where the edition a split would
replace carries something a person put on it.

**What a move does** (`relocate::move_root`; `move_cost` is the same inside
a transaction it rolls back):

1. Refuses, before it files any work (`refused_before`), where the folder is
   its library's last and that library is an account's only grant
   (`scan::only_grant_holders`); where one edition has files under the
   folder and elsewhere; where the target holds a volume of the folder's
   under the same edition key; and where a work placed in a series by hand
   would move and leave other works of that series behind.
2. Derives once (`Documents::Skip`) and refuses where that derive reports a
   lost position, a dropped note, a discarded row or an alignment it could
   not carry.
3. Takes a census: the works wholly under the folder, the works divided by
   it, the rows that will move, and the store's positions, notes and
   ground-truth pages.
4. Files under the target each work whose hub edition is under the folder,
   unless the target holds a work of its content key or at its address, and
   each series every work of which moved, unless the target holds a series
   of its title.
5. Changes the folder's library. Migration 15's trigger removes the library
   it left where it was the last folder.
6. Derives (`Documents::Skip`).
7. Splits: each edition whose library this move changed is given, with what
   readers put on it, to the work the derive made for it on the other side
   (`fold::rehome_editions`, which moves the edition row itself and refuses
   seven cases before writing, among them an edition on the other side that
   carries anything a person made: a hand label, kind or language, a hand
   chapter number, a page flag or an edition credit).
8. Refuses the whole move, naming the works or volumes, where an edition had
   nowhere to go; where a divided work no longer stands where its hub went;
   where the derive in step 6 reports a loss that the one in step 2 did not;
   where a work newly could not be joined; where a work of the folder stands
   outside the target or in no library; or where the store holds fewer
   positions, notes or ground-truth pages than the census counted.
9. Commits, and derives again with documents reconciled.

**What the plan had not run, and what the store did.** `relocate`'s own
statements and `rehome_editions` inside a move are held by
`relocate/tests.rs`'s and `fold/tests.rs`'s cases, watched failing against
defects put back by hand (the tasks' reports and
`f2b-task-3-defects.log`, `f2b-task-3-fix1-defects.log`,
`f2b-task-3-sweep-defects.log`). A folder that keeps documents keeps its
works' documents where they were
(`a_move_with_documents_kept_leaves_the_works_document_where_it_was`), and
the pass after the commit writes back a document that had gone missing
(`a_move_writes_back_a_document_that_went_missing`). A work placed in a
series by hand is refused where its series keeps works behind, and moves
with the series where it does not. A work with no volume, of identical
bytes in both libraries under the same edition key, is refused
(`a_work_with_the_same_content_key_in_the_target_is_refused_and_not_a_store_fault`).
Identical bytes under different titles was not run.

**What the whole-branch reviews found.** Two Critical findings, both in the
shape migration 15 leaves when it splits a work across two libraries
(O191): moving the hub's folder into the library holding the other half
folded the work away, its id, slug and hand title with it, while answering
that it had split it; and a split replaced the other library's edition and
with it a hand label, kind, language and chapter number. Both moves are
refused now. A second pass found that a split also moved an edition the move
had not touched, and that page flags on the replaced edition were lost; both
are fixed. On the screen: a failed reload after a move left the moved folder
and an emptied library drawn with live buttons, the confirm's refusal slot
was never cleared, and two hand-ups (the rehearsal answered after the target
changed, the rehearsal's report handed up for the move's) were held by no
test.

**The drive** (`drive/readings.md`, at 7b31b366, then a second look at
3d60b92c). A copy of the real library's store, 1,896 works in one folder,
served with a scratch folder of two volumes repacked from one of its own:
`Enidewi - v01`, which the copy holds, and `Drive Test Comic - v01`, which it
does not. Made a library `Chapters` of the scratch folder, with edition key
`chapters`, and left a reading position on its `Enidewi` volume. Moved it into
the copy's library: the rehearsal said one work keeps its address and one

from the page beside a scan of the copy's library was refused, naming the
folder under scan.
A scan with
its derive takes about as long over that store, on `main` as on the branch
(O210, `o210-timings.log`); the move's own steps were not timed apart. Afterwards every work the copy held was the same row
(id, slug, content key, title, series), the only new rows being the two
scratch volumes', and the original store was untouched (`sha256sum -c` OK,

**The mutation sweep.** `scripts/mutants.sh --since main` at 958d680b: 225

**SQLite 3.40.1.** The three crates in `rust:1-bookworm` (`libsqlite3-0`
3.40.1-2+deb12u2) at 7b31b366: 2404 passed, and the two that fail there by

**Not measured.** The NAS. A library larger than the copy. A move of a

## O210: a derive's commits (2026-10-08)

**Where the twelve seconds went.** The store was a fresh copy of
`/home/davey/temp/manga-test/library.db`, itself a copy of the real library
(1,896 works), with a scratch
folder of one volume added as the library `Chapters`: 1,897 works. Over it,
`taiyaku library scan --root <the scratch folder>` with `main`'s release binary
at d0508b2a took 11.85, 11.83 and 11.75 s with the store on ext4, of which
1.4 s was CPU, and 0.46, 0.46 and 0.48 s with the same copy on tmpfs, where a
sync costs nothing (`runs-ext4-tmpfs-d0508b2a.log`). `strace -c` over one ext4
run counted 7,774 `fdatasync` calls taking 10.4 s, 1.34 ms each. A stack for
each (`strace -k`, resolved with `addr2line`) put 7,762 of them at four sites
in `derive::write_work`, each reached about once per work: the commit of
`import::scanned_in`'s transaction, `write_roots`, the `UPDATE work` and
`write_edition_metadata`, the last three each committed alone
(`fdatasync-chains-d0508b2a.txt`). `Library::configure` sets no `synchronous`
pragma, so SQLite's default, `FULL`, syncs every commit. Of the 0.46 s left
on tmpfs, 76% of the samples were in SQLite and 45% under
`sqlite3_prepare_v3` (`perf-tmpfs-d0508b2a.txt`).

**The fix.** `write_work` opens one `Nested` scope for the work and commits
it at the end; the import's own scope nests in it. A work rekeyed under
`Documents::Reconcile` commits twice, before its document is renamed and
after, so the rename follows a committed key — where the derive is not inside
a caller's transaction, as a rule save's is; there the first commit is a
`RELEASE`, as the import's was on `main`. Three ways were put to the
user — this one, `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL`, and one transaction for a
whole derive — and the user chose this one. Over the same store, alternating
with `main`'s binary: `main` 11.61, 11.59 and 11.69 s; the fix 3.69, 3.67 and
3.66 s. `fdatasync`: 7,774 calls and 10.8 s against 2,023 and 2.8 s. The two
stores left behind differ only in the scan's timestamps and the scratch
folder's mtime (`compare-o210-fix.log`). A move of the scratch folder into
the copy's library through `POST /api/library/roots/2/move`, by the server's
own figures: the rehearsal 1.35 s with `main` and 1.36 s with the fix; the
move 12.68 s with `main` and 4.97 s with the fix, both answering the same
counts (`move-o210-fix.log`). The fix's binary was built from the working tree
before two comments lost their figures; its code is the commit's.

**Tests.** Three, each run against the defect put back by hand and failing
(`mutations-o210-fix.log`). `a_derive_over_unchanged_files_commits_each_work_once`
counts the commits that write to the WAL, with `wal_hook`: on `main`'s code
it read 8 for the fixture's two works. Not SQLite's commit hook, which also
fires for a write statement that changed nothing, one that writes no frame
and costs no sync. `a_work_that_fails_part_way_leaves_none_of_its_rows_behind`
failed on `main`'s code with the member's root written back after the
refusal. `a_rekeyed_works_document_follows_only_a_committed_key` failed with
the rename moved inside the one scope: the document was not at the address
the rolled-back key gives.

**Isolation.** Nothing under `/home/davey/temp/manga-test` is newer than the
marker, `sha256sum -c` passes on its `library.db`, and the stat of
`library.db`, `-wal` and `-shm` is unchanged (`isolation.log`).

**Not measured.** The NAS. A scan that changes many works: every figure
above is a derive over unchanged files.

151.0.7922.34 launched through Playwright with `--hide-scrollbars` removed,

**The wheel.** On the build of `11a903a7`, with the pointer over the rail

**Tests, and what each was watched failing against.** The declarations are

these passing the two projects CI runs, caught only by the browser project:
the write assigned and not added, a wheel over a tile ignored, a listener
that fires once, and both rules moved inside a media block. Each now fails
a test in a project CI runs. One more is equivalent and is left:
`{ passive: false }` dropped, which is the default for a wheel listener on

**Not measured, and not claimed.**
- **Firefox.** `stripWheel` reads a line-mode wheel and a pixel-mode one as

  `WheelEvent.cpp`, which it had from a summary, Firefox hands a page which

- **A wheel under a hand.** Every reading used Playwright's wheel or a made

- **A device.** `scrollbar-width: none` also takes away the overlay bar that

- **The page behind the bar.** The spec's first reason for cancelling a

  review found a wheel over the rail leaving the page still with no listener

**What the ruling costs.** The bar's thumb was a mouse's fast way across a
long volume. A notch moves the strip 100 px, against a tile pitch of 117 px
at 900 px and wider and 74 px below. While correcting, the review measured

**Isolation.** The servers ran on copies of the database in the session's

### O60: a hidden work, driven

**The rig.** A scratch store built for the purpose: four real volumes
hardlinked into two folders, scanned as two libraries, `Shelf` (two volumes
of one series) and `Other` (two of another); an administrator, and an
account `reader` granted `Shelf` alone. A debug build of `main`'s code and
one of the branch at `7fdcc5b8`, each on its own fresh copy of that store.
The script, `o60-drive.py`, signs in as each account and sends eleven
requests to a work of `Other`, to a slug no work holds, and to a work of
`Shelf`: the six, and the writes with their own checks failing (an edition
the work lacks, a slot past the end, no `If-Match`, a stale one, a body that
is not notes). It compares the first two answers with each other, status
and body, the slug put aside.

| | hidden work against unknown slug | what the hidden work answered |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 10 of 11 differ | 204 to a position read and to a position write; `` `raw` has 219 slots `` to a slot past the end; 200 with the documents; 428, and 412 carrying the document's current `ETag`, to the notes and truth writes |
| the branch | 0 of 11 differ | `` 404 no work `…` `` to ten; 400 to the body that is not notes, as the unknown slug and the granted work also answer |

The one request that agreed on `main` is the body that does not parse, which
both answer before any work is looked up.

On `main` the position write on the hidden work reached the store: after the
run it held two positions for `reader`, one of them on a work that account
cannot open. On the branch it held one.

**An administrator's answers** to the same eleven on the same work are the
same on both builds: 204, 204, the two 404s that name the edition and the
slot count, 200, 428, 412, 400, 200, 428, 412.

**A narrowed grant.** `reader` writes a position on a work of `Shelf` and
reads it back. The grant is then moved to `Other` with
`taiyaku library user grant-library` and `revoke-library`, while the server
runs. On `main` the read still answers 200 with the position. On the branch
it answers `` 404 no work `…` ``, the store still holds the row, and with
`Shelf` granted again the read answers 200 with the same position.

**Tests.** They are in `routes/tests.rs`, each named in O60's row, with

than a write's own checks, or about the work the body names; a position on

**Isolation.** The four volumes in the scratch store are hardlinks, so a
