Each book's sentences split by `taiyaku_core::sentences` and paired by
`align_sentences` within each block link, 40% of the way through each
book, by eye:

| Pair | Sentences | Links one to one | What the sample showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harry Potter 1, en–ko | 7,424 / 9,273 | 67% | all five right |
| Botchan, ja–en (Mori) | 2,773 / 3,265 | 46% | right; one Japanese sentence left unpaired |
| Don Quixote, es–en (Grossman) | 10,785 / 13,234 | 73% | the first two right, the last three a sentence apart, where the two break paragraphs differently |
| Anna Karenina, en (Bartlett)–ru | 23,309 / 20,292 | 24% | wrong: the block links themselves are, the Bartlett file splitting its text unlike any other |

Sentence pairing refines a block link and cannot mend one: where the
blocks are mispaired, so are their sentences. The first request for a
book, which aligns both levels, took 0.3 s (Botchan) to 4.7 s (Don
Quixote) on the release build; a second is served from the cache.
In the browser, Harry Potter 1 in Korean, paged: a double tap on 「그건
햇빛 때문임이 분명했다.」 lit it and peeked "It must have been a trick of
the light."

Joining the next block links where a pairing ends lopsided, up to four,
the same samples again: Don Quixote's five all right (the first two of
five before), 74% one to one; Harry Potter 68% and Botchan 47%, their
samples right as before; the first request no slower.

**Why Anna Karenina pairs badly.** Bartlett's file is an Oxford "uncorrected
advance reading copy" converted from print: it separates paragraphs with
`<br/>` inside one `<p>`, so a run of dialogue reaches the reader as one
block (its longest is 14,485 characters, Schwartz's 6,662), and it is the
work's hub, the edition every other one is aligned to. `read_book` is right
to read a `<br/>` as a line break, which is what one is in verse and
addresses. The Russian file opens most chapters with Wikisource's list of
chapters ("Главы: I · II · …"), which the aligner leaves out as text the
English lacks.

Titled apart with a rule, Bartlett's copy kept its work, and Anna Karenina
became a new work of the Russian and Schwartz's, the Russian its hub: 88%
of its sentence links one to one (24% through Bartlett), the five sampled
all right. Doing it first showed both parts of the split finding the old
row by a member path and writing over it in turn; the probe now matches the
hub edition's paths alone. Deleting `raw` editions by hand had also left
nine works naming a hub they no longer held, read past by the derive (it
falls back to the first key) but wrong in the row: each was set to the key
the derive was already using.

*The probe has since been widened by the books PR's review: where no
group holds a path in a row's hub edition, a path in any of its editions
finds it, so long as every file of it the derive holds is one group's and
no other row has that group's document's key, so the translations left when a book's hub file goes keep its row
(`derive::held_work`). A rule titling part of a work apart still leaves
the row to the part holding the hub.*

## Books: interlinear, and what it shows of an alignment (2026-11-15)

Botchan, Japanese with Mori's English under it: 1,660 lines under 2,773
sentences. Read down the first chapter, the lines run one sentence late
from 「別段深い理由でもない。」 for a stretch ("O, you chicken-heart, ha,
ha!" under it, where it belongs under 「弱虫やーい。」). A peek showed one
pairing at a time; interlinear shows every one, and a pairing by length
alone is weakest between Japanese and English, whose characters carry very
different amounts. Labels: each edition of the grouped works was given its
language or its translator as its label, so the bar and a peek say
"Lattimore" or "Korean" rather than a key.

Reading aloud, driven in the test Chrome on Linux: it lists no voices at
all, and an utterance there ends in `synthesis-failed` within a second. The
reader now says so ("This device could not read ja aloud.") rather than
lighting nothing and staying silent. A reading actually spoken was not
heard on this machine; the voices it picks are each browser's own.

Three columns of the Aeneid (Fagles, Fitzgerald, Ruden): 10,033 rows. The
rows show how little of it pairs: Fitzgerald's line numbers are blocks of
their own ("310", "315"), each verse line another, against Fagles' stanzas,
and a run of Fitzgerald's lines sits beside a bibliography of Fagles'. That
is the verse and line-number work, not the columns.

## Books: verse line numbers, and editions of different grain (2026-11-15)

Before, the verse editions' printed numbers were text or blocks of their
own: 2,682 number-only blocks in Fitzgerald's Aeneid, 1,980 in Ruden's,
1,563 in Martin's Metamorphoses, and numbers opening lines in Fagles'
Odyssey (1,890), Lattimore's (2,445) and his Iliad (3,600). Read by shape
alone, a number opening a short paragraph also took "4 Privet Drive", the
Hogwarts list ("1 wand", "1 cauldron") and Botchan's "1919 A NOTE BY THE
TRANSLATOR"; required to agree with the next or last number by the lines
between, Harry Potter and Botchan keep every number, and the verse
editions number 1,570 to 3,133 lines each. Rutherford's Don Quixote numbers
184 paragraphs: its endnotes, one paragraph each and numbered in order,
which read as verse numbered every line would.

Line against line, translations pair well: Fagles–Lattimore Odyssey 81% of
links one block to one, Martin–Mandelbaum Metamorphoses 92%. Stanzas or
paragraphs against lines do not: Fagles' Aeneid (1,889 blocks, median 151
characters) against Fitzgerald's (14,289) and Ruden's (11,272), and
Fitzgerald's Iliad (2,726, median 237) against Lattimore's (17,625), 2-3%,
since a step joins at most four blocks a side. Joining the finer edition's
lines into runs that end where a sentence does (no more than twelve), where
it had over three times the other's blocks, raised the share of the hub
paired to 76-88%, but samples through the body were still a passage or a
book apart, the hubs' introductions, notes and glossaries pulling them off,
and no key covers these editions; so it was not kept. A key for a stretch
of the Aeneid is what deciding it needs.

## Books: dictionaries from Wiktionary (2026-11-15)

kaikki.org's extracts of English Wiktionary, imported with `taiyaku
dictionary import` on the release build: Japanese (370 MB of JSON lines)
to 143,973 entries and 950,609 forms, 68 MB, in 28 s; Russian (905 MB) to
62,535 entries and 1,996,913 forms, 168 MB, 39 s; Spanish (1.1 GB) to
124,487 entries and 2,391,083 forms, 132 MB, 26 s. No line was passed over.
Looked up through the server: hablaron to hablar, dijo to decir,
счастливые to счастливый, семьи to семья, сказал to сказать, 言った to
言う, and 親譲り, 無鉄砲 and 学校 as themselves; the first lookup in a
language took 0.9-1 s (the file opened cold), each after 1-4 ms. Korean had
no dictionary then: its particles join the word they follow, and a lookup
needed to take them off first, which the Korean dictionary's section below
records.

## O285 and O288: the cover-size slider and the Continue row (2026-11-15)

The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-cover-size-and-continue-row-design.md`
and the plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-15-cover-size-and-continue-row.md`.
The files named below are in `.superpowers/sdd/continue-row-evidence/`, and
the owner's rulings, indexed by date, in
`.superpowers/sdd/cover-size-evidence/rulings.md`; neither is committed.

**The owner's rounds.** The owner settled both items on prototypes served
from a scratch copy of the test library on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15, in
short rounds. The prototypes as they tried them are the four commits on
`continue-align` titled "Prototype as the owner tried it": the first holds
the Continue row's heading, covers and fade, and the three after it the
cover-size slider, the covers' layout, the line under the row and the View
menu's rows. The spec quotes each ruling where it settles an item: the
heading (item 1), the covers (2), the fade (3), the line (4), the slider's
scale, mark and reset (6 to 8, after a catch at the middle was tried at two
strengths and turned down), the exact layout (9) and the View menu (11,
12).

**Two rulings after the prototype**, both of 2026-11-15, are built here and
were not in it.

- **Covers fill the row on phones** (item 9). Below the shell's 900 px
  breakpoint the columns are `minmax(size, 1fr)` at the least gap, so the
  slider sets the least a cover may be and how many columns there are.
  *(`minmax(min(size, 100%), 1fr)` since O302: "O301 and O302", below.)*
  From 900 px up the covers stay exactly the size. `library.css` sets
  `--tile-fill: 1` in the same `@media (width < 900px)` block, so a script
  reads which layout is drawn rather than repeating the breakpoint.
- **The slider is a kind of setting** (item 13), not a control drawn by its
  key, so C1 §4 holds whole. A module declares it in `ReaderModule.sliders`,
  which maps a number preference's key to a `SliderScale`: `last`, the last
  position (the input steps by one); `valueAt` and `positionOf`, the value
  at a position and the position nearest a value; `unit`, written beside
  the name; and `spokenUnit`, read aloud in `aria-valuetext`. `fieldsOf`
  makes such a key a `'slider'` field carrying its scale and its default,
  for a number default and an own key of `sliders` only, and
  `FieldControl` draws it in the View panel and the reader's Settings
  alike. **A declared slider's default must be its middle position.** The
  mark under the track is drawn at the track's middle, the one place it
  sits under the thumb without knowing the thumb's width, which differs
  between browsers; so `sliderFaults` names a declared slider whose default
  is not a finite number at position `last / 2`, and `buildRegistry`
  throws on it at import.

**What the build found beyond the prototype.**

- **The comment guard was red** at the prototype: five comment blocks over
  its eight counted lines, one in `Library.tsx` (the Continue row's hook,
  since moved to `continueRow.ts`) and four in `library.css`
  (`T1-comments.log`). Each was cut by the task whose code it explains, and
  what was cut is below.
- **A zero-gap fallback.** The prototype's hook read the least gap as
  `px('--tile-gap') || 0`, so a gap it could not read counted the columns
  at no gap, more than the grid lays, and set the row to a spread gap the
  grid did not have. A token that is not a px length now removes both of
  the row's properties, and the row keeps the least gap through
  `library.css`'s `var(--continue-gap, var(--tile-gap))`.
- **The coarse mark.** Under a coarse pointer the range has a 44 px floor,
  and both engines centre the thumb in it, so the prototype's mark, hung
  from the bottom of that box, lay 14 px further below the drawn track
  than under a fine pointer in Chromium (`T2b-defect-d5-bottom-0.log`). The mark is now
  placed from the range's centre in the kind's own rule, so the reader's
  Settings panel has it too. Under a fine pointer it sits where the owner
  approved it in Firefox, and 2 px lower in Chromium, whose range box is
  shorter; the slider's row is 2 px taller in both (`T2b-report.md`).
- **The volume's panel was not laid again on a resize.** From 900 px up a
  tile is the cover size whatever the area's width, so a window or a
  sidebar change moves only the grid's width, and with it the laid gap and
  the tile's column; the observer on the tile alone never fired. It now
  watches the tile and its grid (`Series.tsx`), and the panel is laid
  again when the area's width changes and when the window crosses 900 px
  (`T5-report.md`).
- **Large covers were soft.** `Cover.tsx` offered the three cover sizes by
  screen density alone, sized for a cover drawn about 256 px tall; a
  240 px cover is 360 px tall, so the 1× pick was drawn about 1.4 times
  up. What changed is under "The O133 mechanism", below.
- **Firefox's label press.** In Firefox 153.0 a press on a View row's words
  that moved 3 or 4 px before its release reached the words as a click and
  did not toggle the box, where 0 to 2 px did; Chromium 151 toggled at
  every distance from 0 to 4 px (`T3-firefox-probe.log`,
  `T3-chromium-probe.log`). `ViewMenu.tsx`'s `sendRowClick`, on the panel,
  clicks the row's box itself and cancels the label's own activation, so
  Chromium, which still passes it on, does not toggle the box twice.
- **A ResizeObserver loop.** Setting the filled column inside the
  observer's callback changes the cards' width and so the list's height, a
  resize the observer cannot report in that frame, and Chromium fired a
  "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" error
  event on the crossing and on a resize below 900 px. The hook now stops
  watching the list when a measure changed what it set and watches it
  again on the next frame, whose first report carries the size then, as
  `MetadataEditor.tsx` does; a report that changes nothing keeps it
  watched, so there is no loop frame to frame (`T6-notes-for-docs.md`).
- **The first paint.** A first visit's answer reaches `Library` through
  `useSyncExternalStore`, a sync render, whose passive effects React runs
  before a mutation record is delivered, so a test of a first visit cannot
  tell a `useLayoutEffect` from a `useEffect`. The path where the layout
  effect matters is a return to `/` through the router, which commits in a
  transition; `Library.continue.browser.test.tsx` holds that one
  (`T6-notes-for-docs.md`).
- **Firefox's search box.** In Firefox the search box's line was 22 px
  where Chromium draws the 1.5 line at 21, so the box, and with it the page
  head, was 40 px tall against the 39 px the Continue heading's margin is
  built on (`--head-row`), and the Continue rule lay 1 px below the
  Libraries rule (`T11b-report.md`, row 4). A `line-height` of 21 px left
  the line at 22 px there (`review-probe-head.log`). `library.css` now
  sizes the box in the page head from the 1.5 line itself, which the same
  probe drew level in Firefox at a 16 px and a 20 px root. Chromium has no
  such floor, so its test forces the search box's line taller with a
  `<style>` and holds the head's height and the two rules.

**The decisions.**

- **The slider saves on each step of a drag**, not on its release. The
  shell holds one state and stores it on every change, so what is drawn is
  what is stored; a save on release would need a second, draft state for
  the drag, and would lose the drag if the panel closed on Escape or a
  press outside before the release. A `localStorage` write a step is small
  beside the render the drag already causes to make the covers follow
  (the plan, Task 2b).
- **The `@property` fallback is reachable only where the registration is
  missing.** `--tile-min` and `--tile-gap` are registered as lengths, which
  is what makes a computed value a px length rather than the `clamp()`
  text it was written as; a browser without `@property` (the build's
  targets include a Firefox without it, `vite.config.ts`'s `cssTarget`)
  hands the script the text, and the row keeps the least gap. In a browser
  that registers them nothing reaches that path, so its test deletes the
  `@property` rule for the case and puts it back after ("falls back to the
  least gap when the gap is not a px length").
- **A phone's `sizes` is a bound.** Below 900 px a cover is its filled
  column, a width `sizes` cannot write, so `coverSizes` names a width the
  column never reaches: a column is always narrower than two covers and a
  gap, or a second cover would fit, and the least gap is at most 1rem, so
  `2 × size + 32` px never asks for less than the cover needs up to a
  32 px root. It may ask one image step more than a filled cover needs:
  worked out from the selection rule and not driven, two 171 px columns at
  390 px and 144 px, at 1×, ask for 320 px and get the 512 px image where
  the 256 would do (`T9-notes-for-docs.md`).
- **A cover-size change keeps the Continue row's place.** The hook
  measures in the commit that sets the new size, and that read lays the
  row with the new size and the old gap. Left to itself, a row scrolled to
  its end was clamped by a step down: at 1280 px with 20 cards at the end
  at 131 px, one step to 130 px left it 22 px short of its new end
  (`T7-probe2.log`). A step up let the row grow under a `scrollLeft` that
  held, most where the grid loses a column: a drag right from the end left
  it 377 and then 949 px short, in both engines (`T11b-report.md`, rows 61
  and 62). Each mark now records the row's place: whether it is at its
  end, and the card at its start edge as steps of the cards' pitch. A run
  for a new size puts the row back after its measure, at its new end, or
  with that card at the start edge and its offset scaled to the new
  pitch, as far as the row reaches: a row too short at the new size to
  bring the card to its start edge stops at its end. The place is the last mark's, since by that run
  the row may have been clamped. It is kept until the row is scrolled or its cards
  move: Chromium reads a set `scrollLeft` back in whole px
  (`wave-scrollprobe.log`), so a place worked out again at each step of a
  drag would drift, and a row that fits at some size on the way keeps the
  place a drag back returns to. `Library.continue.browser.test.tsx` holds
  both places across changes that move the grid's columns, and the end
  through a size at which every card fits (`wave-report.md`). A window
  resize does not put the row back, a kept place can outlive a change in
  the number of cards, and two parts of the place have no test; O301 has
  them (`wave-rereview.md`). *O301 has since closed all three: "O301 and
  O302", below.*

**The O133 mechanism.** O133 (closed 2026-09-19) offered a cover's three
long edges, 256, 512 and 768 px, as density descriptors, `1x`, `2x` and
`3x`, so the browser picked by screen density alone. `library.ts`'s
`coverSources` now describes the same three addresses by their width in a
cover's 2:3 box (`171w`, `341w`, `512w`), and `Cover.tsx` sets `sizes` from
`coverSizes`, so the browser picks by the drawn width, or on a phone a
bound on it, and the density together. The server is unchanged: the same three edges
(`cover.rs`'s `COVER_LONG_EDGES`) and the same `?w=`. From 900 px up a
144 px cover gets O133's pick at 1×, 2× and 3×, and at 1× a 240 px cover at
1280 px gets the 512 px image; at 390 px and 1× a 240 px cover, one column
drawn 358 px wide, gets the 768, where `sizes` of the size alone gets the
512 (`Cover.browser.test.tsx`; `T9-report.md`, its watched defects).
Chromium takes the smallest image wide enough for the drawn width at the
screen's density (`T9-notes-for-docs.md`), so from 900 px up a cover wider
than about 170 px gets the next size up at 1× and 2× (the 171w image runs
out there at 1×, and the 341w at 2×), and at 3× one under about 114 px gets
the 512 (341w over 3), where O133 gave every cover the 768; worked out from the three
widths and that rule, not driven (`T10-fix1-derive.log`).
`library.css` and `coverSizes` both write the breakpoint and the gap's
1rem cap, since `sizes` cannot read a stylesheet; `library.css.test.ts`'s
"library.css and coverSizes agree" ties them.

- **Not fixed: a 3× screen enlarges a wide cover.** 768 px is the server's
  largest cover, 512 px wide at 2:3, so on a 3× screen a cover drawn wider
  than about 170 CSS px has fewer image pixels than device pixels. O133's
  `768 3x` gave such a screen the same image, so this is no regression;
  the slider allows larger covers. A larger cover size on the server would
  fix it.
- **Not decided: `sizes="auto, …"`.** It would let Chromium pick a lazy
  cover's image from its laid-out width, ending the phone's one-step
  over-ask there, while an engine without `auto` skips that entry and
  keeps the bound. Not built; it needs a ruling.

**Accepted and not fixed.**

- **The row's own scrollbar fades with it.** Where a browser draws the
  Continue row's scrollbar, it is drawn by the list the fade's mask is on,
  so it fades at its ends with the row (the spec's "Left to the builder").

**A question for the owner at the PR, since ruled.** Below 900 px
the columns were `minmax(var(--tile-min), 1fr)`, so where the list is
narrower than one cover it overflowed sideways. The home grid's list is the
window less 32 px of padding (358 px at 390, `T4-notes-for-docs.md`), so
that is 240 px covers in a window under about 272 px, or a browser zoomed
in until it is that narrow in CSS pixels; at WCAG's 320 CSS px reflow width
a 240 px cover fits. The owner approved
`minmax(min(var(--tile-min), 100%), 1fr)`, at the cost of the slider no
longer setting the least a cover may be where the list is narrower than
one, and it shipped as O302 ("O301 and O302", below).

**A fact about the test browser.** In the browser project's launch that
hides scrollbars, a series page's list is narrower than the home grid's at
the same window width, 993 px against 1008 at 1280 (`T4-notes-for-docs.md`):
the gutter that `scrollbar-gutter: stable` keeps on a series page (O283) is
kept even where a scrollbar takes no width. A series page can therefore lay
a column fewer than the home grid at the same size and width, and a figure
for a series page is worked out from its own list.

**What the comments no longer say.** Five blocks were cut to the guard's
cap; the reasons they gave that are held nowhere else:

- **The least gap's curve.** 0.6rem at the slider's least size, rising
  linearly to 1rem at the default, and 1rem above; the comment says only
  that the gap narrows under the default, and why, and the clamp states
  the values.
- **Why a script lays the Continue row.** From 900 px up the grid's spare
  room is spread into its gaps by `justify-content: space-between`, and a
  row that overflows has no spare room to spread, so CSS alone cannot give
  it the grid's gap. Below 900 px the row could lay the grid's
  `minmax(…, 1fr)` tracks, but once its cards overflow, `1fr` tracks shrink
  to their least width (the prototype's first round), so the hook sets the
  filled column as a fixed track. It reads `--tile-min` and `--tile-gap`,
  not the list's own track and gap, which it sets itself, and its
  `ResizeObserver` is also what lays the row for the other layout, since
  the list's width always changes where the sidebar's column comes and
  goes.
- **The fade's lengths.** Clear for 12 px at the edge, half see-through at
  50 px and solid at 80 px, the owner's after "a soft fade" and "a bit more
  obvious"; `library.css` names them `--fade-clear`, `--fade-half` and
  `--fade`.
- **The heading's alignment.** Each hairline is centred on its heading's
  line box, and under a coarse pointer the Libraries heading is as tall as
  its 44 px link. The Libraries hairline lies under the wordmark's
  `--space-4` margin, the wordmark, the sidebar's `--space-4` padding and
  half its heading; the Continue hairline under `main`'s 1rem padding, the
  page's heading row (`--head-row`) and half its own heading. The margin is
  the first sum less the second.
- **The hook's properties.** `--continue-gap` is the exact layout's spread
  gap and `--continue-col` the fill layout's column, chosen by
  `--tile-fill`, and the `data-more-*` marks it sets are what the fade
  reads.

**The drive.** A release build of the branch, over a copy of the test
library's database, was driven with Playwright's real mouse and keyboard
in Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Firefox 153.0, both headless, at 1280, 1024,
899 and 390 px wide and at sizes 96, 144 and 240, and driven again after
the last review's fixes for what those fixes changed (`T11b-report.md`
and its round 2). The Continue cards sat over the grid's columns at its
covers' width at every width and size, and kept the grid's pitch past the
row's edge. The list's inline style held `--continue-gap` from 900 px up
and `--continue-col` below, also across a live 1280 → 899 → 1280 resize,
and a series page's open panel stayed two tiles and the laid gap wide
through the same resize. From 900 px up the covers were exactly the
slider's size; below it they filled the row at the least gap, two 171 px
columns at 390 px and 144, as `main` draws them, and one 358 px cover at
240. The fade showed on each side the row can still scroll to, at its
start, middle and end, and not at all when two entries fit. A press on a
faded cover opened it, and a focused card was never faded. The line under
the row was 1 px in `--line`, 16 px under the cards and 16 px over the
chips, with a classic scrollbar's 15 px between the cards and the line
where one is drawn. There was no line with the strip off, on search
results, or for an account with nothing in progress. After the search
box's change the Continue rule was drawn on the same pixel row as the
Libraries rule in both browsers, and in Firefox 157.0 too, at a 16 px and
a 20 px root; under a coarse pointer, driven in Chromium before that
change, it was level too. The slider stepped 1 px below 144 and 2 px
above, a double-click on the thumb or the track saved 144, a drag moved
the covers and saved on each step, and a stored `compact` and
`comfortable` came in as 104 and 144. During a drag a row scrolled to its
end stayed at its end, and a row scrolled partway kept the same card at
its start edge with the offset into it scaled, also where the grid's
column count changed, at 1280, 899 and 390 px; where the row became too
short to hold that card it stopped at its end. A row that came to fit and
then overflowed again went back where it had been. The View panel
selected no words, and its checkbox row toggled exactly once from a press
at either end and from a press on its words, still or moved 1 to 4 px, in
Firefox as well, leaving the focus on the checkbox with no ring drawn.
Not driven: iOS Safari, a desktop browser with the system's own fonts,
the Paper and Ink themes, the library page in a dark theme, and a window
resize with the row scrolled (O301). The reader's Settings panel draws no
slider, since no reader module declares one.

## O301 and O302: the Continue row across a resize, and covers that never spill (2026-11-16)

The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-15-continue-row-resize-design.md`
and the plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-15-continue-row-resize.md`.
The task reports named below are in
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-15-continue-row-resize/`, which is not committed.
The owner agreed to take O301 and the question "O285 and O288" left open
in one PR, approved the rule that became O302, and approved the design.

**One put-back for a size change and a resize.** `useContinueRow`'s
`restore` is the one step that puts the row back where a kept place
stood: at its end, or the card at its start edge `first` steps along at
the pitch the row is laid at now, which scales the offset into that card.
The cover-size path and the `ResizeObserver` callback, `resized`, both
call it. `resized` puts back the place the last mark kept, not one read
from the row, since by then the new width has laid the row with the old
gap or column, which may have clamped it; and a place worked out again
from `scrollLeft` at each report would drift over a drag's steps, since
it reads back rounded or clamped.

For the same reason `mark` keeps the place while the list stands at a
width the row is not yet laid for. A window drag can bring a new width
each frame. The scroll a put-back queues is marked in the next frame,
before the observer reports that frame's width, and the mark's read lays
the row at the new width with the old gap or column. Where that clamped
the row, a place near its end read as its end, and the row then stayed at
its end as the list narrowed again: 187 px and 196 px off the card in the
two drags the tests below make. `measure` records the list's width it
lays the row for, and `mark` keeps the place while the list's width
differs; the observer lays the row and puts the place back in the same
frame. Where there is no `ResizeObserver`, nothing lays the row again, so
`mark` reads the row at any width.

The place records how many cards there are, because a card more or fewer
moves no pitch, and moves `scrollLeft` only where it clamps a row near its
end, so `mark` keeps it only while that count holds. It records the row's
travel too, so a size change in the same commit as a change in the count
puts the row back from the place as last seen (`seenAt`), not from one a
put-back carried forward.

**O302's rule.** `library.css`'s `@media (width < 900px)` rule for
`.grid, .volumes` lays `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(var(--tile-min),
100%), 1fr))`. Where the list is narrower than one cover the one column
takes the list's width; anywhere wider, `min()` gives the slider's size and
nothing changes. With one column `filledColumn` already gave each
Continue card the list's width, so the grid now agrees with the row there.
`coverSizes` is unchanged.

**The tests, and the defect each was watched failing against.** Each
defect was applied to the code by hand, the test was run red, and the
code was restored. The O302 tests were watched at the head of the task
that wrote them (`task-2-report.md`). Every O301 test was watched again,
against each defect named for it below, on the final code after the
whole-branch review's fix wave (`fix-wave-report.md`; the first runs are
in `task-1-report.md`). The browser tests are in the browser project,
which CI does not run and the local gate does.

- `Library.continue.browser.test.tsx`:
  - "keeps %s across window resizes, a phone turning and back, also across
    900 px", for its end and for the card at its start edge: 12 cards at
    144 px from a 390 px window to 844, 1280, 899 and 390, the grid's
    columns moving at each. Red with no put-back in `resized`, and the
    start-edge case also with the place worked out again from `scrollLeft`
    at each report.
  - "does not creep over a window drag", twenty widths from 390 to 844
    px, a new one each frame: red with no put-back, and with the place
    worked out again at each step, which crept. Its drag sets the test
    frame's width from the page around it, in a task between two frames,
    and the test checks that each frame drew the next width.
    `page.viewport` waits for a frame of its own before it answers, so it
    cannot pace a width a frame.
  - "keeps a card near the row’s end at its start edge over a window drag
    out past the row’s reach and back", the tenth of 12 cards, 390 to 844
    px and back, and "… across 900 px", the eighth, 1000 to 800 px, each
    a new width a frame: red with `mark` reading at a width the row is not
    yet laid for (off by 187 px and 196 px), with no put-back, and with
    the place worked out again at each report.
  - "keeps its end through a window at which every card fits", 7 cards
    that overflow at 1280 px and fit at 1400: red with no put-back, and
    with the place worked out again at each report.
  - "lays its cards over the grid’s columns and as wide as its tiles at
    %i px, %i px covers, %i cards" gained a 260 px window at 240 px covers
    and 3 cards: red with O302's rule taken back, the cards the list's
    width and the grid's tiles 240 px.
- `coverLayout.browser.test.tsx`'s "never lays a cover wider than the list
  on %s, at a 260 px window and 240 px covers", on the home grid and a
  series page: one column, no overflow, and each tile and cover the list's
  width. Red with O302's rule taken back.
- `continueRow.hook.test.tsx`, in jsdom, with the cards' pitch and the
  row's widths set by the test:
  - "keeps the card at its start edge across a resize, the same fraction
    past its edge", "keeps its end across a resize" and "keeps a resize’s
    place through a cover-size change after it": red with no put-back in
    `resized`, and the first and third also with the offset into the start
    card left unscaled.
  - "scales the offset into the start card to the new pitch on a size
    change": red with the offset left unscaled. It passed on `main`.
  - "never counts a row that fits as at its end": red with `seenAt`'s
    `travel > 1` removed. It passed on `main`.
  - "keeps a place scrolled to between two resizes": red with a put-back
    that swallows the user's next scroll, at the place before the scroll,
    and with the width the row was laid for kept from the first measure,
    which leaves a scroll at a later width unmarked.
  - "keeps the place through a scroll marked at a width the row is not
    yet laid for": red with `mark` reading at any width, at the row's end
    instead of the card. "marks a scroll at a new width where no
    ResizeObserver lays the row again": red with `mark` keeping the place
    at a new width also where no observer exists, at the place before the
    scroll.
  - "drops a kept place when the number of cards changes, before a size
    change (O301’s sequence)": red with the count ignored everywhere.
    "…, before a resize": red with no count in `mark`'s check. "… in the
    same commit as the size": red with the size path putting the kept
    place back whatever the count, and with `atEnd` taken from the kept
    place.
  - "keeps %s as last seen through a size change in the same commit as a
    change in the number of cards", both cases, and "keeps its end as last
    seen where a resize clamped the row to it, …": red with the size path
    keeping no place when the count changed; the last also with `atEnd`
    taken from the kept place.

**Not driven.** The plan drives no release build: the resize follows the
rule of the size change the owner already tried (the spec, "Decided").

## The first scan: the walk on NFS, the guard, and Cancel (2026-11-16)

**The walk, over NFS.** `crates/taiyaku-read/examples/walk.rs`, a release
build, lists every fourth series of the share's `Manga/Volumes` and
resolves each file, `sniff` and then `member_pages` for one that sniffs as
a zip, opening each file read-only and running no server. It ran
over this machine's NFS mount of the share (nfs4,
`/mnt/daveynet/nfs/media 1`), so these are NFS figures: the seek a page
cost belongs to that substrate, and the deployment's own figure comes from
the owner's redo of the import. Each run's lines, with the load average
read at its start and its end:

Before, at 09ca3ca3, reading each page's local header (series offset 0):

```

files=605 archives=604 pages=119524 list_secs=0.22 resolve_secs=2703.15 per_archive_ms mean=4475.33 p50=4257.55 p90=7061.30 max=19482.09
loadavg at end: 28.87 26.78 24.51 21/5233 1302216, 2026-11-15T21:39:34-08:00
```

After, at 0de28945, reading the central directory through one 64 KiB
buffer, first over series the bench had not read (offset 1):

```
files=568 archives=563 pages=121067 list_secs=2.69 resolve_secs=94.48 per_archive_ms mean=167.08 p50=139.77 p90=325.48 max=1031.18
loadavg at end: 45.05 54.41 44.61 42/5122 1852407, 2026-11-15T21:58:32-08:00
```

and then over the "before" run's series (offset 0), which may have been in

```
files=605 archives=604 pages=119524 list_secs=4.86 resolve_secs=100.27 per_archive_ms mean=165.92 p50=132.44 p90=333.30 max=1045.46
loadavg at end: 51.83 55.52 46.17 42/5565 1921760, 2026-11-15T22:00:18-08:00
```

The runs are not like for like: the before run's one-minute load average
read 39.75 and 28.87, the after runs' between 45.05 and 55.68, and the series the
bench had not read came out about the same as those it had. The fix round
after 0de28945 (205f90c2), which leaves out the entries `by_index` refuses,
adds checks on the central directory already read and no read, and the
figures were not taken again for it.

**The guard.** Listing from the central directory lists an entry whose
local header is damaged, where reading each local header dropped it, so it
could move later pages' indices. Before the walk changed, `walk guard`
opened every zip archive in the manga-test copy of `Volumes` (since
trimmed) and
counted the pages the old listing dropped for that reason:

```
files=1918 archives=1915 pages=380772 dropped_by_local_header=0 lists_differ_otherwise=0 unopened=0
```

None, so no page index moves in that library and there was nothing for the
owner to decide.

**Reads per listing.** `listing_an_archive_reads_no_more_for_four_hundred_pages_than_for_four`
runs again as a child under `strace` and counts the reads on each
archive's own path, for a `.cbz` of 4 pages and one of 400. As first
written, the child listed each archive alone (`member_pages`). Before the
change:

```
reads: 16 for 4 pages, 1204 for 400 pages
```

and after it, and after its fix round:

```
reads: 5 for 4 pages, 5 for 400 pages
```

The final review had the child sniff each archive first, as a scan's walk
does (`sniff`, then `member_pages`), so that `zip_flavour`'s buffer is
counted too. Sniffing and listing:

```
reads: 10 for 4 pages, 10 for 400 pages
```

and with `zip_flavour` reading unbuffered (`ZipArchive::new(file)`), the
test failing:

```
reads: 17 for 4 pages, 809 for 400 pages
```

(`.superpowers/sdd/first-scan-evidence/FW-rust-read-green.log` and
`FW-rust-read-mutant.log`, not committed.)

**Cancel, driven.** A debug build served a scratch copy of six series of
the manga-test library, its CPU held down by a cgroup quota so that each
step stayed on screen long enough to press Cancel in. An administrator
drove it in one browser context, and an account granted only that library
read it in another.

- **In Reading files**, on a first scan the scheduler started and again on
  one Scan library started: the job stopped after the file it was on, and
  the walk did not commit. The library page read "Cancelling…" where a
  feed poll fell before the job stopped, then "Paused until Scan is
  pressed, since …", and its button read Scan library again. The
  directory's Last scan read Never, the tab that pressed Cancel showed the
  report "Cancelled while reading files", and the directory's status word
  was `cancelled`. The reader's view, not reloaded, read "Not read yet".
  The scheduler passed the directory over at every tick after that.
- **In Hashing**, on a first scan the scheduler started and on one Scan
  library started, after the walk had committed: "Cancelling…" in the
  library's line and the directory's while the job finished its file, then
  the same paused line, Never, and the report "Cancelled while hashing". The
  reader's view went from Scanning, over the step's word alone, to "Not
  read yet", never to "Nothing here".
- **Across a restart**, stopped and started again by its PID, the server
  started no scan, and the library page still read the paused line with
  the same time.
- **Scan library** then hashed only what the cancelled job had not hashed,
  wrote the works, and the library page and the reader's view read again
  without a reload: the paused line went, Last scan showed the new scan's
  time, and the reader's view listed the series.

## Edition matching by content: PR 1's measurement (2026-11-16)

The spec is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-15-edition-matching-by-content-design.md`
and the plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-16-content-matching-measurement.md`.
PR 1 aligns pairs of the test library's members with the solver `align`
uses, scores each pair, and sets a bar for each class of pair so that no
wrong pair clears it. The harness is `taiyaku-cli`'s
`#[cfg(test)]` module `match_experiment`.

### Pre-registered before any page was fingerprinted

This subsection was committed before this measurement fingerprinted any
member of the library, and nothing in it changes once the runs begin.
Earlier experiments aligned some of these editions
(`docs/notes.md:2758-2764`), and the design's §3 drew on their results.
The proof of order at the end of this subsection covers this
measurement's fingerprint cache only. The subsection serves three
sentences of the spec, quoted verbatim:

- "The bar is set so that no wrong pair in the measurement clears it."
- "If PR 1 finds no bar that keeps every wrong chapter pair out, chapter
  matches start as suggestions only, and volume matches go automatic
  alone."
- "If PR 1 measures a first pass over the NAS library at more than a
  day, this comes back to the owner before PR 2 is planned."

**The truth.** The manifest is
`crates/taiyaku-cli/src/match_experiment/manifest.json` as committed at
`d641f069`. It lists 1,905 members of the test library: 1,415 dev and
490 held-out. It holds no adjudications. It stays as committed there,
except for the adjudications the owner's rounds add to the same file. A
member is one entry of a measured directory: an archive, or a directory
of images or of archives. Its kind and numbers come from its name and
its directory's row in `manifest.rs`'s `TABLE`. Its series and split
come from the row. A pair's label comes from its two members' fields
(`label`).

| Kind | Dev | Held-out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `volume` | 551 | 112 |
| `pack` (a volume range, `v01-03`) | 36 | 4 |
| `omnibus` | 28 | 0 |
| `chapter` | 781 | 356 |
| `chapter-pack` | 0 | 1 |
| `issue` | 0 | 14 |
| `collected` | 0 | 3 |
| `extra` (One Piece's Cover Stories) | 19 | 0 |

**The split is by series.** The held-out series are `go-toubun`,
`bocchi*`, `zelda-tp`, `bisque*` and `invincible`, and every other series
is dev. A pair is held-out when either member is, so a dev pair is one
whose two members are both dev.

**Where a chapter's place comes from.** 1,040 members carry a `truth`,
which says how a chapter's place or a collected edition's issues were
set:

- 514 chapters by their name, which gives the volume (`v16 c152`);
- 523 chapters by a printed contents page: 352 inside a volume
  (`in_volume`) and 171 after the last held volume (`after_volume`);
- 3 collected editions by their indicia, which list their issues.

The other 100 chapters have neither `in_volume` nor `after_volume`, and
are `Unlabelled` against every volume and pack of their series.

**The printed truth, confirmed by the owner.** Contents pages and indicia
were transcribed from page images of 67 volumes. The owner confirmed
every transcribed range on the rendered sheet on 2026-11-16, with no
corrections. The owner also approved three readings:

- An unnumbered "Final Chapter" printed after Ch.N counts as N+1, so
  Go-Toubun v14 ends at 122 and Dungeon Meshi v14 at 97.
- Dungeon Meshi v05 keeps its contents page's number for its first
  chapter, 29, over the 26 its title page prints.
- One-Punch Man's fan chapter N is print Punch N+7. Three titles match:
  fan c150 is print 157, c157 is 164 and c162 is 169. Its fan chapters
  are labelled through this reading. They are reported as their own
  sub-class, because the web and print pages may be redrawn.

**Rulings on chapter truth.**

- **After the last held volume.** Call a series' last held volume vM. A
  whole-numbered chapter past the last chapter vM prints is in no held
  volume. It gets `after_volume` M. Against any volume or pack of its
  series it is `ChapterNotIn`. None of these series holds a volume or
  pack numbered past vM. `explicit_pairs` pairs the chapter with vM in
  every edition and with every pack holding M (its rule 5).
- **Fractional and zero chapters** never get `in_volume` or
  `after_volume`, since an extra may be printed as a volume's bonus or
  nowhere. Dungeon Meshi c097.5 is v14's printed bonus. Its first page
  is headed "Monster Tidbits 14" and carries the page number 180. v14's
  contents page lists "Miscellaneous Monster Tales -14-" at page 180.
- **No contents page, no label.** Kobayashi's EN v16 and Bocchi's v06
  and v07 have no contents page in their first 12 pages. Bocchi v07's
  last 14 pages hold none either. So these three volumes place no
  chapter. Bocchi's c82 to c87 carry no volume in their names either,
  and stay unlabelled.
- **Invincible.** The indicia give v01 issues #1–4, v02 #5–8 and v03
  #9–12. Issues #0 and #13 are in none of them.

**The explicit pairs.** `explicit_pairs` names 12,062 pairs before any
page is read, each unordered pair once. The lookup's leaders add more
(below). By label and split:

| Label | Dev | Held-out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SameVolume`, in two directories | 182 | 103 |
| `SameVolume`, copies in one directory | 18 | 0 |
| `Neighbour` | 344 | 191 |
| `InPack` | 428 | 18 |
| `NotInPack` | 147 | 10 |
| `ChapterIn` | 2,626 | 787 |
| `ChapterNotIn` | 2,360 | 1,481 |
| `InCollected` | 0 | 12 |
| `NotInCollected` | 0 | 30 |
| `OtherSeries`, one franchise | 49 | 9 |
| `OtherSeries`, two franchises | 855 | 181 |
| `CoverStories` | 2,109 | 0 |
| `Omnibus` | 122 | 0 |
| total | 9,240 | 2,822 |

No explicit pair is `SameSeriesOther`, `PackOverlap` or `Unlabelled`.

**Orientation and slots.**

- A is the side with fewer slots. On a tie it is the lexically smaller
  path (`oriented`). So a pair scores the same whichever member names it
  first.
- Each member is fingerprinted on its own, as `align` reads an edition
  (`cached_edition`). Spreads are split against the member's own pages.
  Pages read right-to-left, except comics, which read left-to-right.
- A member that is a directory of archives (Raw/Zelda's `v03-05` and
  others) is fingerprinted as its archives joined end to end, in natural
  name order.

**Features and scores.** For each pair, `features` reports the solver's
verdict, the separation and margin, the average run length, the paired
slots over |A|, and long_paired, the slots in paired runs of at least 4.
Two scores are computed from them:

- **V = long_paired / max(|A|, |B|)**, which is low unless long runs
  cover most of both sides.
- **C = (long_paired / |A|) × (long_paired / span_B)**, where span_B is
  the stretch of B from the first long run's start to the last one's
  end. It is the chapter-in-volume test, defined in advance: A's long
  runs must land in one stretch of B about A's own length.
- With no long run, both are 0.

**The rules.** Each rule judges one class of pairs on one score
(`class`). A pair outside a rule's lists is outside the rule.

- **The volume rule, on V.** Positives are `SameVolume` pairs: two
  members of one series with the same volume number or range. They may
  be two editions, a colour or fan variant, or copies. Negatives are
  every other labelled pair except `Omnibus` and `PackOverlap`. So
  `ChapterIn`, `InPack` and `InCollected` pairs are volume-rule
  negatives.
- **The chapter rule, on C**, only where A is a chapter or an issue of
  at least 8 slots. Positives are `ChapterIn` and `InCollected`.
  Negatives are `ChapterNotIn`, `NotInCollected`, `OtherSeries` and
  `CoverStories`. A chapter under 8 slots is never automatic, because a
  short side always aligns (`docs/notes.md:1904-1916`).
- **The pack rule, on C**, only where A is a volume and B a pack.
  Positives are `InPack`. Negatives are `NotInPack` and `OtherSeries`, a
  volume against another series' pack. The rule reads B's kind as well
  as A's, since an `OtherSeries` label alone does not say B is a pack.
- **Omnibus editions** are reported only, and their names decide (the
  spec's ruling 5). The check is that `is_omnibus_name` marks every
  omnibus member and no other.
- **`Omnibus`, `PackOverlap` and `Unlabelled` pairs are neither
  positive nor negative under any rule.** Two packs of one series whose
  ranges overlap but differ are `PackOverlap`. Disjoint packs of one
  series stay `SameSeriesOther`, a volume-rule negative. Packs with the
  same range are `SameVolume`.
- **Why `InPack` is a negative and `PackOverlap` is not.** A volume
  inside a pack scores V of at most |A| / |B|, about 1 / (the volumes in
  the pack). The smallest packs hold 2 volumes. There are 9 of them: 8
  dev, and Zelda's `v06-07` held out. So `InPack` pairs can lift the
  volume bar to about 0.65 at most, which keeps the bar conservative.
  Two packs whose ranges overlap approach V = 1 as the overlap grows.
  As negatives they would leave the volume rule unable to pass, on a
  relation the names already separate. And the product never puts two
  packs of different ranges to the volume rule, because it cuts packs at
  the seams (the design's §4, "Range packs").
- **Chapter against chapter.** `label` makes every pair of one series'
  chapters, and every pair of one series' issues, `ChapterNotIn`,
  whatever their numbers. No series holds two chapter or issue files
  with one number. Such pairs come only from the lookup's leaders. They
  are chapter-rule negatives when A has at least 8 slots. They are
  volume-rule negatives too. Two different chapters are a wrong pair
  even when they share credit pages.

**The bar.** A rule's bar is its highest dev negative plus **0.15**.

- A rule passes only if it passes on both splits.
- It passes on dev if it has at least one dev negative and its bar is
  at most 1.0. A rule with no dev negative claims no bar ("no
  negatives, no bar claimed"). No evidence of safety is not a pass.
- The bars are committed in
  `crates/taiyaku-cli/src/match_experiment/bars.json` before any
  held-out pair is scored.
- It passes on held-out if no held-out negative scores at or above its
  frozen bar, and at least one held-out negative is in its class. A
  rule with no held-out negative is "untested on held-out", which is
  not a pass either.
- A rule that passes while no positive on either split is at or above
  its bar is reported as "passes, matches nothing automatically". It
  makes no match automatic.
- The share of positives at or above the bar is reported per rule and
  per sub-class: raw against EN, colour, fan and copy pairs for volumes,
  each series for chapters, and packs.

**The comics.** Every comics member is held out. The manga chapter rule
is the chapter rule over pairs whose A is a chapter. Every issue is
held out, so on dev the manga chapter rule is the whole chapter rule.
Its held-out verdict covers the held-out pairs whose A is a chapter.
The comics sub-class is every pair whose A, the oriented short side, is
an issue, under any label. It holds an issue against a collected
edition, against another issue, and against another series. It is
judged under the frozen chapter bar, on C. The comics fail when any
chapter-rule negative in the sub-class scores at or above that bar.
The comics positives clearing the bar are reported beside the verdict.
Issues go automatic only if the manga chapter rule passes and the
comics pass. A failed manga chapter rule leaves no trusted frozen bar
for the comics.

**Unlabelled pairs and possible mislabels.**

- An unlabelled pair is put to a rule only if it passes that rule's
  gates, the kind and slot gates `class` applies to a labelled pair.
  The volume rule has no gate, and scores V. The chapter rule needs A
  to be a chapter or an issue of at least 8 slots, and scores C. The
  pack rule needs A to be a volume and B a pack, and scores C.
- On dev, an unlabelled pair is shown to the owner when its score under
  a rule it passes is at or above that rule's highest labelled dev
  negative. The rounds repeat while that line moves.
- On held-out, it is shown when that score is at or above the rule's
  frozen bar.
- The owner's verdict turns the pair into a label through the
  adjudication mapping (`adjudicated`). For a chapter pack such as
  Zelda's `ch01-15` against a volume, either verdict gives `ChapterIn`
  or `ChapterNotIn`. Both are volume-rule negatives.
- On held-out, a "different" or "can't tell" verdict on a shown
  unlabelled pair is a held-out failure of that rule. It never changes
  a bar.
- Labelled negatives scoring at least 0.5 are shown too, on both
  splits. Each is scored by the rule under which it is a negative: V
  for the volume rule, C for the chapter and pack rules.
- The owner may relabel a labelled negative only on "same drawings".
  Every relabel is counted and reported per split. On held-out, a pass
  that depends on a relabel is reported as "passes after N relabels",
  never as a plain pass. Such a pass carries a pass's consequences, and
  its N is reported with it.
- A round holds at most 40 pairs. The controller may only split a
  longer list into further rounds of at most 40. The score, the gap, the
  classes, the gates and the label function never change.
- "Can't tell" counts as different. If the owner stops before every
  shown pair has a verdict, each pair still without one counts as
  different too.

**What a failure means.**

- If the manga chapter rule fails, chapter matches are suggestions
  only, and volume matches go automatic alone. Issues are then
  suggestions only too.
- If the volume rule fails, nothing is automatic, and the result goes
  back to the owner before PR 2.
- If the pack rule fails, PR 4 cuts packs by their names, and content
  only suggests.
- If the comics fail, issues are suggestions only. A comics failure
  demotes issues alone. It does not fail the manga chapter rule.

**Instrument controls**, on the first dev `SameVolume` pair in the
scored list's order. That list sorts pairs by member index, which is
manifest order.

- A member of it against itself gives V ≥ 0.99 and C ≥ 0.99. `score_dev`
  asserts it.
- The pair with its B shuffled gives V ≤ 0.10. `score_dev` asserts it.
- Its paired slots, runs and verdict equal `taiyaku align --stats` on
  the same two members. This is compared by hand, and the comparison is
  recorded.
- A failed control stops judgement. No rule is judged until the
  instrument is fixed and the run is repeated, and the notes say so.

**The lookup.**

- Each informative slot of a member, one with 8 to 248 of its 256 bits
  set, votes for the member holding its nearest informative slot among
  all other members. A tie, in distance or in votes, goes to the member
  listed first in the manifest.
- Leaders rank by votes. The top 3 of every member are scored with the
  explicit pairs, each unordered pair once.
- A query's positives and negatives come from the label, for every kind
  of query, not from a rule's class. Positive: `SameVolume`, `InPack`,
  `ChapterIn`, `InCollected`. Negative: `Neighbour`, `SameSeriesOther`,
  `NotInPack`, `ChapterNotIn`, `NotInCollected`, `OtherSeries`,
  `CoverStories`. Neither: `Omnibus`, `PackOverlap`, `Unlabelled`. The
  lookup finds candidates to align, and a pack holding a volume is a
  candidate, not a wrong pair.
- Reported: the share of queries whose best positive leads, the depth
  needed to reach it, the margins, and the time. A query's margin is the
  votes for its best positive less those for its best negative, over its
  informative slots.
- **P1:** every labelled query's best positive is in its top 3. A query
  with no labelled positive ("no positive") is left out of P1, and so is
  one whose positives all failed to print ("positive unprinted"), whose
  count is reported.
- **P2:** of the chapter queries that have a `ChapterIn` positive, at
  least 90% are led by a volume or pack holding the chapter, in any
  edition. The subset with 8 or more slots is reported beside it,
  without a prediction of its own.
- P1 and P2 are judged and reported for dev and for held-out
  separately. Each split's P1 and P2 are judged on the manifest as it
  stands after that split's last adjudication round. The figures from
  before any round are reported beside them.

**The cost on the NAS.**

- `nas_timing` runs on the NAS over
  `crates/taiyaku-cli/src/match_experiment/nas_sample.txt` twice: on
  all cores, then with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`. A Hamming kernel is
  benchmarked at both.
- The sample is 26 members, each with its class: six EN volumes
  (`volume`: Kaguya v01 and v02, One Piece v105 and v106, Monster - The
  Perfect Edition v01 and Bocchi v01), five raw members (`raw`:
  `Oshinoko v01`, `Kaguya-sama_Zunousen_v02`, `Monster v01`,
  `DLRAW.TO_Kobayashi-san Maid Drago v02` and the pack
  `Oshinoko v01-03`), twelve chapters (`chapter`: Kaguya v16 c152 to
  c161, One Piece c1134 and c1135), two issues (`issue`: Invincible #1
  and #2) and one collected edition (`collected`: Invincible v01).
- Each path is relative to the NAS's `media 1` share, and each is in the
  test library at the same place, with `Manga/` read as the library's
  root and `Comics/` as its `Comics/`.
- A class stands for one NAS directory: `volume` for `Manga/Volumes`,
  `raw` for `Manga/Raw`, `chapter` for `Manga/Chapters`, `issue` for
  `Comics/Issues` and `collected` for `Comics/Collected`.
- A sample entry's class is its top directory, not its kind. That is
  why the Perfect Edition, an omnibus, counts as `volume`.
- A directory with no measured class takes one, and the result flags
  it. `Ecchi` and `Extras` take `volume`. `Graphic Novels` and
  `Webcomics` take `collected`. Any other such directory takes the
  nearest measured class.
- The first pass's hours are the sum, over the NAS's `Manga/*` and
  `Comics/*` directories, of bytes ÷ the cold read rate + bytes × the
  fingerprint seconds per byte of the directory's class, plus the
  lookup, slots² ÷ the kernel's comparison rate.
- The lookup's slots² squares the NAS's total slots, searched as one
  index. It is not a sum of each library's slots².
- A directory's slots are its bytes × its class's slots per byte,
  measured on the test library's fingerprint run, leaving out members
  that could not be read (such a member has 0 bytes and a non-zero
  time).
- The cold read rate is the median of the all-cores run's read rates,
  leaving out its first member, which carries any disk spin-up. The
  4-thread hours take the 4-thread run's fingerprint and kernel rates,
  and the all-cores hours the all-cores run's.
- **If the 4-thread first pass exceeds 24 h, the result says so and the
  owner is asked before PR 2.** The all-cores figure is reported beside
  it.

**Fixed from this commit:** the features, the run length 4
(`LONG_RUN`), the gap 0.15 (`GAP`), the 8-slot minimum
(`MIN_CHAPTER_SLOTS`), the classes (`class`), the label function
(`label`), the split and the sample. Anything else in the results is
descriptive and does not replace V or C in this PR.

**The proof of order.** The fingerprint run's log opens with the run's
stamp, written before any member is read. Its members line reports
`cache hits: h`. The proof that this measurement fingerprinted no page
before this commit is a stamp later than this commit together with
`cache hits: 0`. If h is above 0, the proof falls back to the
modification time of the oldest entry in the run's fingerprint cache.
That cache is keyed by content and written only on a miss.

### On the NAS

`nas_timing` ran on the NAS in a container of the deployed taiyaku
image, with the library share mounted read-only and the test at
`nice 19`. Each run timed the registered sample twice: on all 8 cores,
then with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`. The sample is 26 members and 2.85 GB,
and every run found and fingerprinted all 26.

**The quiet run is the result.** It ran on 2026-11-16 from 15:16:58 to
15:19:15 UTC. No Forgejo Actions job was running when it began, and
both qBittorrent containers were paused for the run, as the owner
approved. Before the run, the sample's own pages were advised out of
the page cache with `dd iflag=nocache count=0`, and no other cache was
touched. `fincore` then showed 0.00% of the sample cached, both through
shfs and on the disks behind it. The 1-minute load was 2.51 when the
all-cores pass began and 4.00 when the 4-thread pass began, and no
member finished with it above 4.00. The first member read at
106.71 MB/s, so no disk spin-up shows in it.

**The busy run** ran earlier the same day, from 13:39 to 13:48 UTC.
`fincore` showed 0.0% of the sample cached before it. It ran beside
both qBittorrents, and when it ended a `rustc` build was running too.
Its 1-minute load was 12.62 when the
all-cores pass began and 32.32 when the 4-thread pass began, and it
peaked at 34.15. The contention shows in its figures. `Oshinoko v01-03`
took 133.3 s to digest and 115.2 s to re-read, against 9.6 s and 0.6 s
in the quiet run. Its 8-thread kernel (17.1 s) was slower than its
4-thread one (12.6 s), with the test's `nice 19` threads competing with
that load for the 8 cores.

The extrapolation follows "The cost on the NAS." above:

| | Quiet | Busy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold read rate (median, first member left out) | 85.01 MB/s | 15.48 MB/s |
| Kernel, all cores (comparisons/s) | 1,868,848,727 | 584,595,585 |
| Kernel, 4 threads (comparisons/s) | 1,147,822,786 | 793,234,094 |
| Read | 6.73 h | 36.98 h |
| Fingerprint, 4 threads | 14.66 h | 18.42 h |
| Fingerprint, all cores | 10.27 h | 17.04 h |
| Lookup, 4 threads | 0.78 h | 1.13 h |
| Lookup, all cores | 0.48 h | 1.53 h |
| **First pass, 4 threads** | **22.18 h** | **56.53 h** |
| First pass, all cores | 17.48 h | 55.55 h |

These are the quiet run's rates per class. Slots per MB come from the
test library's fingerprint run, and the lookup squares the NAS's
1,795,463 slots:

| volume | 9.21 | 15.78 | 0.7181 |
| raw | 6.71 | 11.93 | 2.2718 |
| chapter | 14.60 | 17.22 | 1.9788 |
| issue | 34.98 | 43.64 | 0.9594 |
| collected | 13.59 | 21.74 | 0.8340 |

| Library | Directory | GB | Class | Read h | Fingerprint h, 4 threads | Fingerprint h, all cores |

Each library's read and fingerprint hours come to:

The lookup over both libraries adds 0.78 h at 4 threads and 0.48 h on

**One day.** Measured quietly, the first pass takes 22.18 h at
4 threads, under 24 h, so the pre-registered condition for asking the
owner before PR 2 is not met. On all 8 cores it takes 17.48 h. The busy
run puts the same pass at 56.53 h at 4 threads. The quiet figure is the

**Beside the method, descriptive only.** Neither figure in this
paragraph replaces those above. The quiet run's size-weighted read rate
is all bytes over all digest time, the first member included. It is
97.85 MB/s, which would make the read 5.85 h rather than 6.73 h. The
method also leaves out the re-read, when `read_edition` unpacks the

### What it decides

**Nothing goes automatic.** The volume rule fails on held-out, and the
pre-registration says what follows: "If the volume rule fails, nothing
is automatic, and the result goes back to the owner before PR 2."

- **The scores** are V and C as pre-registered, unchanged since.
- **The volume rule, on V,** froze its bar at 0.9147 on dev and fails
  on held-out ("Held out" above). Both failures pair two Bisque Doll fan
  extras, `c023.5` with `c055.5` and `c063.5` with `c071.5`, each at
  V 1.0000, and the owner judged both different ("Held out" above).
- **Chapters cannot go automatic.** The chapter rule has no bar: its
  highest dev negative, C 0.8667, leaves no room below 1.0 for the 0.15
  gap ("Dev" above). Chapter matches start as suggestions only, and
  issues with them.
- **The pack rule, on C,** froze its bar at 0.4957 and passes on
  held-out at that bar with no relabel, all 18 of its positives clearing
  it ("Held out" above). Under the volume rule's failure it makes
  nothing automatic. Whether pack cuts go automatic on that bar once a
  volume rule passes is the owner's to decide (O340).
- **The comics** have no frozen chapter bar to be judged by, so they are
  reported only, and issues are suggestions only ("Held out" above).
- **The exploratory chapter-in-volume line** passes on held-out after 2
  relabels ("Held out" above). It is exploratory, not pre-registered,
  and informs PR 5's design only.

**The owner's ruling (2026-11-17).** PR 2, fingerprints in the server,
goes next, and makes no match. Before PR 3, a short new measurement
tests a volume rule limited to volume-against-volume pairs, which is all
PR 3 compares. Its bar is frozen on the series already scored, and it
is tested on series never scored. Until a rule passes, every content
match is a suggestion. Both held-out failures pair two chapters, and
such a rule leaves them out. O340 holds the measurement.

**How many candidates PR 3 should align.** P1 fails on both splits, and
P2 holds:

- The top 3 hold the best positive for 867 of 908 dev queries and 436
  of 440 held-out ones ("Dev" and "Held out" above), so 3 candidates per
  member miss some.
- Before any round, 23 dev best positives got no vote at all (the
  fingerprint run's dev `lookup.txt`, over every vote). On held-out, 1
  best positive is not among the 10 leaders kept for its member (the
  held-out run's `lookup.txt`). That member, Zelda's raw pack
  `v06-07`, voted for only 4 members, so its best positive got no vote
  either (the fingerprint run's `leaders.json`). No depth reaches those,
  so the lookup alone cannot supply every candidate.
- A member holding the chapter leads 97.7% of dev chapter queries and
  98.4% of held-out ones ("Dev" and "Held out" above): for a chapter,
  the first candidate is nearly always a volume or pack holding it.

**Names in PR 3 (the owner, 2026-11-16).** PR 3 examines names as a
penalty across series, or to rank candidates, and never as a boost
within one series, because a same-series pair sets the volume bar.
Kaguya's fan extras `v20 c201.5` and `v22 c221.5`, two chapters of one
series, are dev's highest volume-rule negative at V 0.7647, which sets
the volume bar, and its highest chapter-rule negative at C 0.8667 ("Dev"
above).

**The verdict, a lead for PR 3.** Every dev volume-rule negative
pairing two different series at V 0.5 or more, 54 of them, has the
verdict Fragmented, which V ignores (the dev run's `scores.tsv`). A gate
on Fragmented would not do: 33 of the 201 dev volume positives are
Fragmented too, as are 39 of the 103 held-out ones, and both held-out
failures are Sound (the dev and held-out runs' `scores.tsv`). It would
drop true positives and would not have caught the failures.

**The cost on the NAS.** Measured quietly, a first pass takes 22.18 h
at 4 threads and 17.48 h on all 8 cores, and the busy run puts it at
56.53 h at 4 threads ("On the NAS" above). The quiet figure is under a
day, so the cost alone would not send the result back to the owner
before PR 2. The volume rule's failure did, and the owner has ruled.

**The proof of order**, the test the pre-registration's "The proof of
order" sets. The fingerprint run's log opens at 2026-11-16
12:20:06 UTC, after the pre-registration's last commit, at 12:10:45 UTC
(committed on the branch before its squash merge), and its members line
reads `cache hits: 0`. `bars.json` was committed at 14:21:08 UTC, before
the first held-out score at 15:23:17 UTC ("Held out" above). Nothing in
the test library changed after the comics were copied in, and its
`library.db` is unchanged.

## Edition matching by content: the volume-against-volume test (2026-11-18)

The design is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-content-matching-volume-test-design.md`
and the plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-18-content-matching-volume-test.md`. The
harness is `taiyaku-cli`'s `#[cfg(test)]` module
`match_experiment::volume_test`, and O340 holds the measurement.

### Pre-registered before this measurement fingerprinted any page of the test series

This subsection was committed with the frozen bar, before this
measurement fingerprinted any page of a test series. Its wording was
corrected in docs-only commits before the run read any test page, and
nothing in it changes once the run begins. The run's fingerprint cache
did not exist when the bar was frozen.

**What is measured, and why.** The owner wants raw and fan editions to
join their English volumes by page content, with confident matches
applied automatically. PR 1's volume rule failed on held-out on two
pairs of Bisque Doll fan extras the owner judged different. The owner
ruled on 2026-11-17 that a short new measurement comes before PR 3: a
rule limited to volume-against-volume pairs, which is all PR 3 compares,
its bar frozen on the series already scored and tested on series never
scored by this measurement. The score is V as PR 1 defined it, long-run
pages over the longer side's pages. The test scores all 12,246 pairs of
157 volumes. The run also reports how many true pairs clear the bar, by
kind of edition.

**The RuriDragon repack, disclosed.** Before the design was written,
RuriDragon's four raw archives were unpacked and repacked as zip,
because they are RAR5 and taiyaku refuses RAR5. Each page file's bytes
were hashed to prove the repack identical (`ruri-1-sha256.txt` to
`ruri-4-sha256.txt` in
`.superpowers/sdd/content-matching-o340-evidence/`). No page was
decoded, fingerprinted or scored. The result states this too.

**A related book PR 1 did score.**
`Hunter × Hunter - Kurapika's Memories`, a separate one-volume book PR 1
scored, is not one of the test series.

**The earlier Tongari work, disclosed.** Tongari stays in the test with
its earlier work disclosed (owner's ruling, 2026-11-18). Its raw and
English v01 and v09 went through the aligner in early project work
("Tongari confirms the pattern on a fifth series", "A letterbox has to
come off both sides equally", and the rows `tongari-v01` and
`tongari-v09-letterbox`, all in this file), and the rule that trims page
borders was designed on v09. An early survey also measured volume 13 for
gatefolds ("No gatefolds exist in anything measured", in this file). V
was never computed on these volumes, and the bar comes only from PR 1's
scores. The result states this too, and the report shows Tongari's true
pairs on their own line.

**The members.** `volume_test/members.json` lists the 157 volumes,
drafted from directory names without opening an archive.

| Series | Editions | Same volume in two editions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tongari Boushi no Atelier | raw 14, English 14 | v01 to v13 |
| RuriDragon | raw 4, English 3 | v01 to v03 |
| Hunter × Hunter | black and white 36, colour 37 | v01 to v36 |
| Parasyte | black and white 8, Full Color Collection 8, Colored Council 10 | black and white against the Collection, v01 to v08 |
| Yu Yu Hakusho | black and white 19, Colored Council 4 | none |

**How a pair is classed.** `pair_class` writes out the owner's rulings,
and the frozen bar holds a digest of every pair's class.

- **True: 59 pairs count.** Sixty pairs are the same volume in the
  editions the table names, and one of them is damaged, which leaves
  Tongari 13, RuriDragon 3, Hunter × Hunter 35 and Parasyte 8. Tongari
  raw v09 against English v09 is a true pair (owner's ruling,
  2026-11-18): a complete volume of joined two-page spreads.
- **Damaged: one pair.** Hunter × Hunter colour v35 against black and
  white v35 is outside pass and fail and is reported separately. The
  damaged volume's pairs with every other volume stay ordinary wrong
  pairs.
- **Different split: 236 pairs (owner's ruling, 2026-11-18).** Every
  Parasyte Colored Council volume against either 8-volume Parasyte
  edition (160 pairs) and every Yu Yu Hakusho Colored Council volume
  against the black and white edition (76 pairs). These are wrong pairs
  even where the volume numbers agree.
- **Wrong: the other 11,950 pairs.** Tongari raw v16, Tongari English
  v14, RuriDragon raw v05 and Hunter × Hunter colour v37 have no
  partner, so every pair of theirs is here.

**The bar.** The bar is the highest V of any volume-rule negative among
pairs whose two members are both `Kind::Volume` in PR 1's dev and
held-out scores, plus `rule.rs`'s `GAP`. The harness computes it, and no
code or test holds its value. `freeze_volume_bar` writes it to
`crates/taiyaku-cli/src/match_experiment/volume_test/bar.json` with the
pair that set it, the integers behind that pair's V, and SHA-256 digests
of PR 1's two score tables, the members and the pairs' classes. It
refuses to write over a bar already there. One commit freezes the file,
and no later commit touches it.

**The control.** Before the first test page is read, the run
fingerprints the ten pairs of `volume_test/control_pairs.json` again
from nothing, in a new cache, and compares each with its row in PR 1's
scores: V, both slot counts, paired pages, long-paired pages, runs and
the solver's verdict. The ten include the pair that set the bar. An
answer from a cache, or any difference, stops the run.

**Pass or fail.** The rule passes if no wrong pair, different-split
pairs included, scores at or above the frozen bar, and at least one
wrong pair exists. A wrong pair exactly at the bar fails. Any wrong pair
at or above the bar goes to the owner one pair at a time, with its pages
beside it on a sheet from `volume_test_sheets`. Each ruling is committed
to `volume_test/verdicts.json` and the saved scores are judged again,
while `report-first.txt` keeps what the run said before anyone ruled. A
pair the owner calls the same volume is relabelled, counted and
reported. A different-split pair cannot be relabelled, because the owner
has already ruled on it. "Can't tell" and an unanswered pair stay wrong.
The bar never moves.

**What each result decides for PR 3.** In the design's words: "If the
rule passes, PR 3 may apply volume matches at or above the bar
automatically. If it fails, every PR 3 match is a suggestion." O340
stays open either way, because the owner has still to rule on pack cuts.

**What will not be adjusted once the run begins.** The bar, the gap, the
score, the members, the pairs' classes and the code. A low score is
reported, never adjusted, and that includes a true pair below the bar.
No name or solver verdict rescues a pair. PR 1's `bars.json` and
`manifest.json` do not change. The run scores once: it refuses an
uncommitted change, a commit since the freeze that touches `crates/`,
`Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, a `bar.json` PR 1's scores do not derive,
a used fingerprint cache, and a scoring already saved. A member that
cannot be read whole stops the run with no report. After the first
scoring, the owner's verdicts are the only commit the harness accepts
under `crates/`.

### The result

**The rule passes.** No wrong pair scored at or above the frozen bar of
0.87: 0 of 12,186, the 236 different-split pairs among them. The
report's last line reads `verdict: passes`. No wrong pair reached the
bar, so the owner had none to rule on: the report counts 0 verdicts and
0 relabels, and `report-first.txt` is byte for byte `report.txt`.

**The control.** Before any test page was read, the run fingerprinted
the ten control pairs again in a new cache and compared each with its
row in PR 1's scores. Its log reads `control: 10 of 10 pairs reproduced`.

**The proof of order.** `bar.json` was committed at 2026-11-19 01:16:25
UTC, and no other commit touches it. Only documents changed between that
commit and the one the run used. The run's log opens at 01:45:55 UTC.
The scoring's stamp, taken after the control and before the first test
page is fingerprinted, reads 01:46:15 UTC. The log's members line reads
`members: 157, fingerprinted: 157, unreadable: 0, cache hits: 0`.
These times are recorded in the evidence directory,
`.superpowers/sdd/content-matching-o340-evidence/`, which git ignores:
the commit's time in `report.txt`'s `bar.json: committed` line, the
log's opening in the stamp on the first line of `logs/volume-test.log`,
and the scoring's stamp on the first line of `report.txt`.
`logs/freeze-commit.txt`, written at the freeze, holds the commit's time
as a Unix time. Rebasing the branch onto main rewrote its committer
times, so the freeze commit's committer time in the branch's history is
the rebase's, not the freeze's.

The pre-registration says its wording was corrected in docs-only
commits before the run read any test page. Two commits after the freeze
made those changes, and they did more than correct wording: they added
that the run also reports how many true pairs clear the bar by kind of
edition, and that an early survey measured Tongari's volume 13 for
gatefolds. Neither addition touches the bar, the members, the pairs'
classes or the code.

The first launch of the run, about a minute earlier, used a mistyped
test filter that matched no test, so it read nothing and scored nothing,
and the run was launched again with the exact name. Its log was
overwritten.

Two pieces of earlier work are disclosed, as the pre-registration sets
out. RuriDragon's four raw archives were unpacked and repacked as zip
before the design was written, and each page file's bytes were hashed to
prove the repack identical, with no page decoded, fingerprinted or
scored. Tongari's raw and English v01 and v09 went through the aligner
in early project work, the rule that trims page borders was designed on
v09, and an early survey measured volume 13 for gatefolds. V was never
computed on these volumes before this run, and the bar comes only from
PR 1's scores.

**The library was not written to.** `library.db`'s SHA-256 was the value
the plan gives, before the run and after it. `find -newer` and
`find -cnewer` against a stamp file touched at the launch list no path
(`isolation-newer.txt`, `isolation-cnewer.txt`). That stamp is the second
launch's, so a further `find -newermt` with a cut-off earlier than the
first launch was run too, and it lists no path either
(`isolation-since-first-launch.txt`). All three are in
`.superpowers/sdd/content-matching-o340-evidence/logs/`.

**Against the bar.** The bar is the 0.72 of `[Oshi no Ko]` fan v10
against v12, the highest volume-rule negative among the pairs of two
volumes in PR 1's dev and held-out scores, plus the gap of 0.15. The run scored 59 true pairs, 1 damaged pair, 236
different-split pairs and 11,950 other wrong pairs. The highest wrong
pair is a different-split pair, Parasyte Colored Council v10 against
Full Color Collection v08, at V 0.810909 (223 long-paired pages, slots
229 and 275, verdict Sound).

**True pairs clearing the bar: 52 of 59.**

| Editions | At or above the bar | True pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tongari raw against English | 11 | 13 |
| RuriDragon raw against English | 3 | 3 |
| Hunter × Hunter black and white against colour | 31 | 35 |

**The damaged pair, outside pass and fail.** Hunter × Hunter colour v35

**What the result decides for PR 3.** The rule passed, so PR 3 may apply
